details.body: To BAA , v. n. u (c. 1. avate, otuM), mezavat or uraBravat SabdaM kf.
Babble, v. i. jalp 1 P, pralap 1 P. 2 rahasyaBedaM kf 8 U. [Babbl]ing, s. jalpaH, pralapitaM. [Babbl]er, s. jalpakaH, vAcAwaH, vAcAlaH, pralApin m., vAvadUkaH.
BABBLE (v. i.): (1) jalpati (jalp, c. 1.);(2) pra-lapati (lap, c. 1.);(3) vAvadye, vAvadmi, or vAvadImi (freq. of vad);(4) vAvacye, vAvacmi (freq. of vac).
BABBLE, BABBLING (subs.): (1) jalpaH;(2) jalpanam;(3) jalpitam;(4) pralapitam.

To BABBLE , v. n. (To prattle like a child) bAlavat jalp (c. 1. jalpati, jalpituM). — (To talk idly) jalp. — (To tell secrets) rahasyaM prakAS in caus. (-kASayati -yituM) or viKyA, in caus. (-KyApayati -yituM), rahasyaBedaM kf.
BABBLE or BABBLING, s. jalpaH, jalpanaM, vAvadUkatA, bAlavacanaM, AKyAyikA.
BABBLER: (1) (jalpakaH (kA, kaM);(2) jalpAkaH (kI, kaM);(3) vAcAwaH (wA, waM);(4) vAvadUkaH (kA, kaM); (5) pralApin (f. nI).
BABBLER , s. vAcAlaH, jalpakaH, upajalpI m. (n), vAcAwaH, jalpAkaH, vAvadUkaH.
Babe, Baby, s. SiSuH, SAvakaH, dArakaH (rikA f.), stanaMDayaH. [Baby]hood, s. bAlyaM, SESavaM, bAlaBAvaH. [Baby]ish, a. bAliSa, bAleya.
BABE , BABY, s. bAlaH -lA, bAlakaH, SiSuH m., SAvakaH. — (At the breast) stananDayaH, stanapAH m. (pA), kzIrapaH.
Babel, s. saMkaraH, kolAhalaH, saMkIrRanAdaH.
BABEL , s. (Confusion) saNkaraH, sANkaryyaM, tumulaM, kolAhalaH, kAlakIlaH.
Baboon, s. vAnaraH, kapiH, markawaH.
BABOON: hanumat (m.) (?); vAnaraviSezaH.
BABOON , s. vAnaraH, kapiH, markawaH, plavaNgaH, plavagaH, SAKAmfgaH, balImuKaH.
BABY, BABE: dArakaH, m. (dArikA, f.): v. Infant, suckling, child.
BABYHOOD: SESavam (childhood: q. v.).
BABYHOOD , s. bAlyaM, bAlakatvaM, bAlaBAvaH, SESavaM.
BABYISH: bAliSaH (SA, SaM): v. Childish.
BABYISH , a. bAlakIyaH -yA -yaM, bAliSaH -SA -SaM, bAleyaH -yI -yaM.
Bacchanal, Bacchanalian, s. madyapAnAsaktaH, madyapriyaH, pAnarataH.
BACCHANAL, BACCHANALIAN: tAntrikaH (kI, kaM) (?).
BACCHANALIAN , s. pAnarataH, pAnaprasaktaH, madyapItaH, madyapriyaH, sampItirataH.
Bachelor, s. akftadAraparigrahaH, akftodvAhaH avivAhitaH.
BACHELOR: (1) akftadAraH or akftodvAhaH: v. Un- -married;(2) vaRwaH or vaRWaH (very rare). Ph.: a b. of arts *‘vi e’ upADiDArin (f. RI).
BACHELOR , s. (A man unmarried) avivAhitaH, akftadAraH, akfta- dArasaNgrahaH, akftavivAhaH. — (One who takes his first degree) vidyAlaye pUrvvapadaprAptaH.
Bacilli, s. (Pl.) rogajaMtavaH.

Back, s. pfzWaM, pfzWadeSaH; ‘lying on the b(ack)’ uttAnaSayaH; ‘behind oneʼs b(ack)’ parokze-kzaM. adv. prati, apA, ni, parA, with verbs; punarnivft 1 A ‘come b(ack)’, ‘give b(ack)’ pratidA 3 U. prep. See Before. v. t. anumud 1 A, samarT 10, rakz 1 P. 2 (horse), A-aDi-ruh 1 P. 3 parARud 6 P; See Drive. [Back]bite, v. t. parokze aDikzip 6 P, parivad 1 U, asUyati (D.) with dat.; pfzWamAMsaM ad 2 P or KAd 1 P (with gen.). [Back]biter, s. piSunaH, pfzWamAMsAdaH, parivAdarataH. [Back]biting, s. pESunyaM, pari(rI)vAdaH [Back]bone, s. pfzWavaMSaH, kaSerukA. [Back]door, s. pakzadvAraM, pakzakaM. [Back]gammon, s. carmapawwikAkrIqA. [Back]ground, s. paScAdBUmi f.; ‘throw into the b(ackground)’ (lit.) dfzwipaTAnnivAr 10, niBfte sTA c. (sTApayati); (fig.) ‘Urvaśī throws Lakshmī into the b(ackground)’ urvaSI pratyAdeSaH SriyaH (V. 1); raterapi hrIpadamAdaDAti (K. iii. 57). [Back]room, s. aMtargfhaM, aMtaH-upa-SAlA. [Back]side, s. pfzWa-BAgaH-deSaH. [Back]slide, v. t. svaDarmAt BraMS 1 A, 4 P or cyu 1 A. [Back]stairs, s. upa-pracCannaM-sopAnaM; ‘b(ackstairs) influence’ pracCanna-sAmarTyaM-guRaH. [Back]ward, a. parANmuKa (KI f.), atItakAla. 2 maMdaDI- mati, maMda, (of a boy). 3 anicCu, pratIpa. [Back]wards, adv. parA, prati, with verbs; pfzWataH, pfzWaBAge-deSe. 2 paScAt, pratIpaM; gatAgataM; ‘move b(ackwards) and forward’ gatAgataM-gamanAgamanaM kf 8 U.

BACK (subs.): I Of an animal: pfzWam, whose b. s the enemy has seen dfzwapfzWAnarAtinA, Ki. xv. 19.: Ph. behind one's b.:(1) pfzWataH;(2) parokze (in one's absence).II As opposed to front:(1) pfzWam, on the b. of a writing leKasya pfzWe, Y.;(2) pfzWadeSaH.
BACK (adv.): v. Backwards. It is generally expr. by the prefix prati: to come back pratyA- gacCati; to give back prati-dadAti etc.
BACK (v. i.): pratyA-vartate (vft, c. 1.): v. To go back.
BACK (v. t.): I To mount: q. v.II To support, second: q. v.III To drive back- -ward: pratIpaM nudati (nud, c. 6.) or cAlayati (c. of cal).

BACK , s. pfzWaM, vigrahAvaraM; ‘to turn the back, avert the face,’ parANmuKaH -KI -KaM or parAcInaH -nA -naM BU; ‘to turn back, away from,’ apavft (c. 1. -varttate -varttituM), vinivft, apAvft, nivft; ‘turned back,’ viparivarttitaH -tA -taM; ‘at one's back, behind the back,’ pfzWatas; ‘behind one's back, in one's absence,’ parokze. — (The hinder part) pfzWadeSaH, paScAddeSaH, paScAdBAgaH, pfzWaM, nitambaH; ‘the back of the hand,’ karapfzWaM.

BACK , adv. (To the place whence one came) commonly ex- pressed by prati prefixed; as, ‘to go back,’ pratigam; ‘come back,’ pratyAvfttaH -ttA -ttaM, punarAgataH -tA -taM; ‘brought back,’ pratyAnItaH -tA -taM. — (Backward from the present station) expressed by parA, prati, or paScAt prefixed; as, ‘to beat back,’ parAhan, pratyAhan. — (Again) expressed by punar, prati, or anu prefixed; as, ‘to give back,’ pratidA. — (Kept back) nigfhItaH -tA -taM, nivAritaH -tA -taM; ‘in the back-ground,’ dUrasTaH -sTA -sTaM, niBfte.

To BACK , v. a. (To mount a horse) Aruh (c. 1. -rohati -roQuM), aDiruh, samAruh. — (To support, justify) rakz (c. 1. rakzati, rakzituM), aBirakz, saMrakz; pakzapAtaM kf, upakf, anugrah (c. 9. -gfhlAti -grahItuM). — (To impel backwards) parARud (c. 6. -Rudati -RottuM), viparItaM praRud.
To BACK , v. n. (To go backwards) apakram (c. 1. -krAmati, c. 4. -krAmyati, -kramituM), vyapakram, parAvft (c. 1. -varttate -varttituM).
BACK , s. pfzWaBAgaH. — (Of the hand) avahastaH.
BACK-GAMMON: krIqAviSezaH. b.-board: (1) azwA- padam (?);(2) carmapawwikA (?).
BACK-SIDE: (1) pfzWaBAgaH;(2) pfzWadeSaH v. Also buttocks.
BACK-SLIDE: svaDarmAd BraSyati (BraMS, c. 4.), cyavate (cyu, c. 1.): v. To go astray.
BACK-SLIDER: (1) GarmaBrazwaH (zwA, zwaM);(2) GarmacyutaH (tA, taM): v. Apostate
BACK-STAIRS: (1) *pakzasopAnam;(2) *antaHsopAnam.
BACKBITE: (1) parokze pari-vadati (vad, c. 1.), asUyati (nomi.), etc. v. To slander;(2) pfzWamAMsam atti (ad, c. 2.) KAdati (KAd, c. 1.) (with gen) (not very common).
To BACKBITE , v. a. pfzWamAMsaM KAd (c. 1. KAdati, KAdituM). — (To slan- der) parivad (c. 1. -vadati -te -vadituM), apavad.
BACKBITER: (1) pfzWamAMsAdaH;(2) yaH parokze parivadati etc.;(3) piSunaH (?).
BACKBITER , s. pfzWamAMsAdaH, parokze apavAdakaH, parivAdakaH, piSunaH.
BACKBITER , s. parokzapiSunaH, parokzanindakaH, parokzApavAdakaH.
BACKBITING: (1) pfzWamAMsAdanam;(2) piSunavAkyam: v. Slander.
BACKBITING , s. parivAdaH, apavAdaH, piSunavAkyaM.
BACKBITING , s. parokzapESunyaM, parokzanindA, parokzApavAdaH.
BACKBONE: (1) pfzWavaMSaH;(2) kaSeruH;(3) kaSerukA; (4) rIwakaH (rare).
BACKBONE , s. kaSerukA, pfzWavaMSaH, pfzWAsTi n., rIQakaH.
BACKDOOR: (1) pakzadvAram;(2) pakzakaH.
BACKDOOR , s. pakzadvAraM, antardvAraM, upadvAraM, pracCannaM, pakzakaH, KaqakkikA.
BACKGAMMON , s. carmmapawwikAkrIqA. — (Backgammon-board) carmma- pawwikA, azwApadaM, baDnaH.
BACKGROUND: *paScAdBUmiH (in ana. with agra- BUmiH) or expr. by circumlo.
BACKROOM , s. antargfhaM, antaHSAlA, uparoDakaM, upaSAlA.
BACKSIDE , s. (The hinder part of any thing) pfzWadeSaH, paScAddeSaH, paScAdBAgaH, aDodeSaH. — (The hinder part of any animal) ni- tambaH, pfzWaM.
To BACKSLIDE , v. n. svaDarmmAt pariBraMS (c. 4. -BraSyati -BraMSituM) or cyu (c. 1. cyavate, cyotuM), sTaDarmmaM tyaj (c. 1. tyajati, tyaktuM).
BACKSLIDER , s. DarmmacyutaH, DarmmaBrazwaH, svaDarmmatyAgI m. (n), unmArgagAmI m. (n), anyaSAKakaH.
BACKSTAIRS , s. upasopAnaM, antaHsopAnaM, pakzasopAnaM, pracCannasopAnaM.
BACKWARD (adj.): I Reluctant, averse: q. v. parANmu KaH (KI, KaM).II Slow, dull: q. v. kuRWitaH (tA, taM).III Late: q. v.IV Reversed: q. v.: pratIpaH (pA, paM).

BACKWARD or BACKWARDS, adv. Expressed by parA or prati pre- fixed; paScAt, pratIpaM, viparItaM, avakawaM; ‘to walk backwards and forwards,’ gatAgatAni or pratigatAgataM or gamanAgamane or yAtAyAtaM kf.

BACKWARD , a. (Unwilling) pratIpaH -pA -paM, anicCaH -cCA -cCaM, asa- mmataH -tA -taM, anicCakaH -kA -kaM. — (Sluggish) mandaH -ndA -ndaM, alasaH -sA -saM, vilambI -mbinI -mbi (n). — (Dull of apprehension) manda- matiH -tiH -ti. — (Late, after its time) atItakAlaH -lA -laM, ati- krAntakAlaH -lA -laM, dIrGakAlInaH -nA -naM, dIrGapakvaH -kvA -kvaM, dIrGapakva- SIlaH -lA -laM.
BACKWARDNESS: parANmU KatA: v. Reluctance, aversion.

BACKWARDNESS , s. (Unwillingness) anicCA, asvIkAraH, asammatiH f. — (Sluggishness) AlasyaM, mAndyaM, vilambatvaM. — (Dulness) mandama- titA. — (Lateness) dIrGakAlInatA, atItakAlatvaM, dIrGatA, dIrGapakvatA.
BACKWARDS: I Towards the back: pfzWaBAge or pfzWadeSe.II On the back: to fall b. avamUrDa- pAtaM patati.III In a reversed direction: pratIpam. Ph. to go b. (fig.) kramaSo'vanatiM gacCati.
Bacon, s. SUkaramAMsaM.
BACON: *lAvaRaSuzkaSUkaramAMsam; Perh. valluram.
BACON , s. vallUraM, SUkarasya SuzkamAMsaM,
Bacteria, s. (Pl.) rogajaMtavaH.

Bad, a. niMdita, garhya. 2 aSuBa, aBadra. 3 asAra nirguRa, ahita. 4 sadoza, aSudDa; gen. ex. by duH, vi, ku, kiM, kat, apa, prefixed; ‘a b(ad) man’ durjanaH; durdEvaM &c.; kupaTaH ‘a b(ad) way’; kumatiH; kiMsaKA ‘a b(ad) friend’; ‘b(ad) coin’, kUwanARakaM; ‘b(ad) debts’, apratilaByaM fRaM, apayaSaH ‘b(ad) fame’, infamy; kadaSvaH ‘a b(ad) horse’. [Bad]ly, adv. Gen. Ex. by dur; ku; ‘b(adly) prepared’ kunirmita; ‘smells b(adly)’ durgaMDaH asya; ‘b(adly) bitten’ tIvraM-balavat-asuKaM-dazwa; ‘b(adly) off’ duHsTita, kazwApanna, durgata. [Bad]ness, s. Ex. by (a.); ‘b(adness) of result’ kupariRAmaH; durAcAraH. 2 durjanatA, duzwatA. 3 niHsAratA, nirguRatA, aBadratA. 4 aSudDatA, sadozatA.

BAD: Gen. expr. by the prefixes dur, ku, apa etc. and sometimes by the affix ka: a b. man durjanaH; b. weather durdinam; b. luck durdEvam; not a b. speaker akadvadaH; a b. road kadaDvan (m.); b. food kadannam; b. design kumatiH; b. policy apanayaH; b. reputation apayaSaH; a b. horse aSvakaH: v. Wicked, injurious, unfavourable.

BAD , a. (Vicious, corrupt) pApaH -pA -paM, duzwaH -zwA -zwaM, aDamaH -mA -maM, nIcaH -cA -caM, KalaH -lA -laM, kutsitaH -tA -taM, kadaryyaH -ryyA -ryyaM. — (Not good) aBadraH -drA -draM, asADuH -DuH -Du, aDArmmikaH -kI -kaM, asAraH -rA -raM, asan -satI -sat (t). — (Worthless) nirguRaH -RA -RaM. — (Hurtful, unwholesome) hiMsraH -srA -sraM, ahitaH -tA -taM, apaTyaH -TyA -TyaM, rujAkaraH -rA -raM. — (Sick) rogI -giRI -gi (n), vyADitaH -tA -taM. — (Sick of) AturaH -rA -raM, ArttaH -rttA -rttaM in comp. — (Un- fortunate) vipannaH -nnA -nnaM, durgataH -tA -taM. ‘Bad,’ as a general word, is often expressed by dur, ku, kat, or sometimes by vi or apa prefixed; as, ‘a bad road,’ duraDvaH, kupaTaM, kadaDvA m. (n), vimArgaH; ‘a bad man,’ durjjanaH, durAcAraH; ‘bad wea- ther,’ durddinaM; ‘bad food,’ kadannaM; ‘bad thing,’ apadravyaM; ‘bad conduct,’ durRayaH, kukarmma n. (n), apakarmma n. (n); ‘bad policy,’ anItiH f.
Badge, s. cihnaM, lakzaRaM.
BADGE (subs.): (1) cihnam;(2) lakzaRam;(3) liNgam.
BADGE , s. cihnaM, liNgaM, vyaYjanaM, lakzaRaM. — (Badge of rank) padacihnaM, padasUcakaM cihnaM.
BADGER (subs.): BallUkajAtIyajantuviSezaH.
BADGER , s. garttavAsI jantuviSezaH.
Badinage, s. upahAsaH, laGUkti f., wawwarI, narman n.
BADINAGE (subs.) narmaBAzitam: v. Joke, raillery.
BADINAGE , s. laGuvAkyaM, laGUktiH f., hAsyavAkyaM, narmma n. (n), wawwarI.

BADLY: Ph. I am b. off for servants BftyABAvAt kliSyAmi; you have behaved b. towards her tasyAM tvayAnAryamAcaritam; he is b. bitten by the dog sa kukku reRa tIvraM or balavat dazwaH, b. governed kuSAsitaH (tA, taM): b. formed kadAkAraH (rA, raM); smell- ing b. durganDaH (nDA, nDaM): v. Wrongly, wickedly, unfortunately.

BADLY , adv. duzWu, duzwaM, aBadraM. Often expressed by dur, ku, apa prefixed; as, ‘badly managed,’ durRItaH -tA -taM; ‘badly shaped,’ kurUpaH -pI -paM; ‘badly-behaved,’ duHSIlaH, kuSIlaH; ‘badly done,’ duzkftaH -tA -taM, apakftaH -tA -taM.
BADNESS: (1) by the adj.: b. of character durAcAraH; the b. of this soil is proverbial *asya pradeSasya kumfttikA prasidDA;(2) duzwawA (=wicked- -ness);(3) nirguRatA (=worthlessness).
BADNESS , s. duzwatA, dOzWavaM, nirguRatvaM, nIcatA, aBadratA, kadaryyatvaM. — (Of character) durAtmatA, durAcAratvaM.
BAEATHING-TIME: Ph. give me b. SvasitumavakASa dehi: v. Pause, respite.

Baffle, v. t. vyarTI-moGI-kf 8 U, KaMq 10, BaMj 7 P, prati-vi-han 2 P. 2 parABU 1 U, parAji 1 A; ‘b(affl)ed in efforts’ BagnodyamaH; ‘the scene b(affle)s description’ varRanavizayAtikrAMtaM tatsTAnaM. [Baffl]ed, a. KaMqita, BagnASa, moGASa; parAjita.
BAFFLE (v. t.): (1) vyarTIkaroti;(2) moGIkaroti: v. Frustrate, elude.

To BAFFLE , v. a. (To make ineffectual) moDIkf, nizPal (nom. nizPalayati -yituM), KaRq (c. 10. KaRqayati -yituM), vyarTIkf, pratihan (c. 2. -hanti -hantuM), muDA kf, vfTA kf. — (To defeat) parABU (c. 1. -Bavati -BavituM), parAji (c. 1. -jayati -te -jetuM).

BAFFLED , p. p. pratihataH -tA -taM, moGaSaH -SA -SaM, manohataH -tA -taM, prati- [Page036-a+ 51] badDaH -dDA -dDaM, BagnodyamaH -mA -maM, KaRqitaH -tA -taM, KaRqitASaMsaH -sA -saM, parAjitaH -tA -taM.
Bag, s. puwaH-waM, prasevaH, syUtaH, kozaH; ‘leather b(ag)’ carmaBastrikA. v. t. syUte niDA 3 U; ‘to let the cat out of the b(ag)’, guhyaM sPuw c., guhyasPowaM kf 8 U.
BAG (subs.): (1) Perh. puwam; canvas b. *SARa- puwam;(2) BastrA; leather b. carmamastrikA D. ii.; (3) goRI (=sack. q. v.).
BAG , s. SARapuwaH -waM, syUtaH, syotaH, kozaH, ADAraH.
To BAG , v. a. (To put into a bag) SARapuwe or syUte or koze niDA (c. 3. -daDAti -DAtuM) or niviS in caus. (-veSayati -yituM). — (To make tumid) Svi in caus. (SvAyayati -yituM).
To BAG , v. n. (To swell out like a bag) syUtavat lamb (c. 1. lambate, lambituM), pralamb, or pF in pass. (pUryyate), or Svi (c. 1. Svayati, SvayituM).
BAG , s. puwaH -waM -wI, puwakaM; ‘leather bag,’ dftiH f.
BAG-PIPE: suziravAdyaviSezaH.
Bagatelle, s. kzudravizayaH, agurvarTaH.
BAGATELLE: I a trifle: q. v.II A game: kandukakrIqAviSezaH.
BAGATELLE , s. svalpavizayaH, alpamUlpadravyaM, kzudradravyaM, kzudravizrayaH.
Baggage, s. sAmagrI, upakaraRaM, sADanaM; ‘bag and b(aggage)’ sarvamapi gfhItvA, kimapi nAvaSezya.
BAGGAGE: I Of an army:(1) sADanam; the bugle sounding and the b. being ready AhatAyAM prayARaBeryAM sajjIkriyamARe sADane, K.;(2) vIvaDaH (provisions), Si. ii. 64.II A strumpet: q. v. banDakI.
BAGGAGE , s. (The furniture of an army) sAmagrI -gryaM, BAraH, upa- karaRaM, paricCadaH. — (A worthless woman) puMScalI f., veSyA, banDakI.
Bagnio, s. snAnAgAraM. 2 veSavAsaH, veSyAlayaH.
BAGNIO: I A bath: q. v. snAnAgAram;II A brothel: q. v. veSyAlayaH.
BAGNIO , s. (A house for bathing) snAnAgAraM, gAtramArjjanaSAlA. — (A brothel) veSyAlayaH.
Bah, interj. ahaha, Dik.
Bail, s. pratiBUH, lagnakaH, prAtiBAvyaM; ‘admited to b(ail)’ pratiBUdAnena muktaH. v. t. lagnakaM dA 3 U, dattvA muc c. 2 potaM nirjalI kf 8 U.

BAIL (subs.): I The person who gives b.:(1) pratiBUH, he who stands a b. to produce a man yo yasya pratiBUstizWeddarSanAyeha mAnavaH, M. viii. 158; (2) lagnakaH.II Security: prAtiBAvyam, on b. prAtiBAvyana. D. vi.

BAIL (v. t.): I As applied to securities: Ph. I will b. you tavAhaM pratiBUrmavAmi (BU, c. 1.) or tizWAmi (sTA, c. 1.)II as applied to magis- -trates: pratiBAvyena muYcati (muYc, c. 6.) or mocayati (muc c. 10.).

BAIL , s. (Security for one's appearance) darSanapratiBUH m., darSanaprAti- BAvyaM, pratiniDiH m., pratiBUH m., prAtiBAvyaM, pAriBAvyaM, lagnakaH, nyAsaH, anvADiH m., banDakaH, tfRamatkuRaH. — (The person who gives the security) pratiniDiH m., pratiBUH m., lagnakadAyI m. (n).
To BAIL , v. a. (To give bail for another) pratiniDiH or pratiBUH BU, lagnakaM dA (c. 3. dadAti, dAtuM).
BAIL-BOND: *prAtiBAvyapatram.
BAILABLE: Ph. this offence is b. *grAhyalagnako'parAGaH or asminnaparAGe pratiBUrgfhyate.
BAILABLE , a. yo lagnakaM dattvA moktuM Sakyate or SakyaH.
Bailiff, s. AseDdfAsedDf m., grAhakaH.
BAILIFF: *AseDAdikarmaRi niyuktaH SeriPasya pratiniDiH; *yazwiDaraH.
BAILIFF , s. (An officer who arrests) AsedDA m. (dDf), AseDakarttA m. (rttf), grAhakaH, yazwiDaraH, daRqanAyakaH. — (A steward) kAryyADISaH.
BAILMENT , s. AkzepaH.
BAIRN , s. bAlaH, bAlakaH, SiSuH m.

Bait, s. AmizaM; ‘b(ait) fixed to a fish-hook’ baqiSayutaM piSitaM. 2 pra-vi-loBanaM. 3 pravAsopahAraH. v. t. pra-viluB c. 2 AmizaM dA 3 U (with dat.); AmizaM baqiSe niDA 3 U or yu 2 P or niviS c.; ‘this is surely a b(ait) to catch me’ mAM vaSIkartuM nUnamidamAmizaM prakalpitaM. 3 (horses) viSram c.; Buj c. 4 See ‘Harass’. 5 (pravAse) mArge upahAraM kf 8 U. v. i. BojanArTaM viSram 4 P.
BAIT (subs.): Amizam (Lit. and Fig.), Ka. i. 44.

BAIT (v. t.): I To apply a bait:(1) sAmizaM karoti (?);(2) AmizaM vaqiSe nidaDAti (DA, c. 3.) II To furnish animals with food on a journey: yavasAdinA Bojayati (c. of Buj) (?): Ph. b. ing his horse enaM tAvadAgfhItakatipayadUrvA- prabAlakavalaM kftvA, K.III. To attack an animal with dogs: Ph. to b. a bear BallUkabADanAya kukku rAn praRudati (nud, c. 6.).

To BAIT , v. a. (To put meat on a hook to tempt animals) matsyAdigrahaRArTaM vaqiSe AmizAdi niDA (c. 3. -daDAti -DAtuM), or ni- viS in caus. (-veSayati -yituM). — (To give food to horses on the road) maDyayAne yavAdinA vAhanAni Buj in caus. (Bojayati yituM), yAnaSrAntAni vAhanAni viSram in caus. (-SrAmayati -yituM). — (To incite dogs to attack a bull) vfzaBam AkramituM kukkurAn pracud in caus. (-codayati -yituM).
To BAIT , v. n. (To stop on the road for refreshment) maDyayAne BojanArTaM viSram (c. 4. -SrAmyati -SramituM).
BAIT , s. matsyagrahaRArTaM yad AmizaM vaqiSe niveSyate. — (Temptation) praloBanaM.
BAIZE , s. SARaM, kambalaH, UrRAmayo vastraviSezaH.
Bake, v. t. (kadO) pac 1 P, tap c., Brasj 5 P. [Bak]ed, a. pakva; ‘b(acked) brick’ pakvezwakA; kaMdupakva. [Bak]er, s. kAMdavikaH; ApUpikaH. [Bake]house, s. ApAkaH; kaMdu m. f.

BAKE (v. t.): (1) pacati (pac, c. 1.) (prop. to cook: q. v.), b. d brick pakvezwakA, Mr.;(2) Bfjjati, te (Brasj, c. 6.) (=to fry, q. v.), the [Page054] word lāja (also) means b. d grain lAjaM BfzwaGAnye Ph. b. d in an iron pan or oven (as bread, cakes etc.) kAndavaH (vI, vaM).
To BAKE , v. a. ApAke or kandO or cullO pac (c. 1. pacati, paktuM) or tap (c. 1. tapati, taptuM, c. 10. tApayati -yituM) or Brajj (c. 6. Bfjjati, BrazwuM), kAndavIkf.
To BAKE , v. n. (To be heated) taz in pass. (tazyate), pac in pass. (pacyate).
BAKE-HOUSE, BAKERY: (1) pUpaSAlA (?);(2) pAkaSAlA (?).
BAKE-MEATS , s. kAndavaM, kAndavAnnaM, uKyaM, pakvAnnaM, ApUpikaM, SAzkulikaM.
BAKED , p. p. kAndavaH -vA -vaM, uKyaH -KyA -KyaM, kandupakvaH -kvA -kvaM.
BAKEHOUSE , s. ApAkaH, kanduH m. f., pUpAgAraM, pUpaSAlA.
BAKER: (1) ApUpikaH;(2) kAndavikaH;(3) pizwaka- pAcakaH.
BAKER , s. ApUpikaH, kAndavikaH, modakakft, BakzyakAraH.
BAKING , s. kandupacanaM, cullipacanaM, pacanaM, tapanaM, tApanaM.

Balance, s. tulA, mApanaH; ‘beam of a b(alance)’ tulAdaMqaH-yazwi f. 2 SezaM, avaSezaH ‘what is the b(alance) against me’ mayA deyaH (dravya-)SezaH kiyAnvartate. 3 vivecanaM; vigaRanaM, samatolanaM. 4 tulyatA, samAnaBAratA. v. t. tul 10 (tulayati); ‘b(alance) accounts’ samI kf 8 U, SuD c. 2 (In thought) vivic 7 P; vikxp c. v. i. dolAyate (D.). [Balanc]ed, a. tulita. 2 tulyaBAra; samIkfta; ‘b(alanced) sheet’, s. saMkziptagaRanAleKaH, deyAdeyaSezadarSakaM gaRanApatrakaM.

BALANCE (subs.): I A pair of scales:(1) tulA;(2) mApanaH (?). The beam of a b. tulAdaRqaH; the string by which it is suspended pragrahaH or pragrAhaH; the cup of a b. GawaH; assay b. nArAcI. II Of an account:(1) SezaH (=remainder: q. v.), he asked for the b. of money gfhItaSezaM dAtuM sa DanaM prArTayatATa taM, Raj.;(2) antaram (differ- -ence: q. v.), gives the whole b. dIyatAM sakalAntaram, Raj.III Counterpoise: q. v.IV Com- -parison, estimate: q. v. tulanA.

BALANCE (v. t.): I To bring to an equipoise; tulayati (tul, c. 10) (Lit. and Fig.): Ph. their equipment is not b. d na tulADftastAvadanayoH parikaraH, Vi. vi.II To counterpoise: q. v.III Of accounts:(1) samIkaroti (kf, c. 8.);(2) ekIka- roti (?), b. ing the account gaRanAmekIkftya, Raj.
BALANCE (v. i.): I To be in equipoise: samIBavati (BU, c. 1.) (?).II To fluctuate, hesitate: q. v.: dolAyate (nomi.).

BALANCE , s. (Scales) tulA, mApanaH, mApanadaRqaM, tOlaM, tOladaRqaM. — (The act of comparing two things in the mind) vivecanaM, vikalpanaM, vigaRanaM, upamAnaM. — (That which is wanting to make two parts of an account even) avaSezaH, SezaM, SezaBAgaH, aDikAMSaH, nyUnAMSaH. — (Equipoise) tulyatA, BAratulyatA.

To BALANCE , v. a. (To weigh in a balance) tul (nom. tulayati yituM), tUl (c. 10. tUlayati). — (In the mind) vikxp in caus. (-kalpayati -yituM), vigaR (c. 10. -gaRayati -yituM). — (To equipoise) samIkf, tulyaBAraM -rAM -raM kf. — (To regulate an account) SuG in caus. (SoDayati -yituM), samIkf, apanayanaM kf, vigaRanaM kf.
To BALANCE , v. n. (To hesitate, fluctuate) dola (nom. dolAyate yituM), vikxp (c. 1. -kalpate -kalpituM). — (To be equipollent) samIBU, tulyIBU.
BALANCED , p. p. tulitaH -tA -taM, samIkftaH -tA -taM, tulyaBAraH -rA -raM. — (As an account) SoDitaH -tA -taM, apanItaH -tA -taM, vigaRitaH -tA -taM.

BALARĀMA , s. (A celebrated demigod, half-brother to Kṛṣṇa, and the third of the Rāmas; and considered to be the eighth avatār of Viṣṇu) balarAmaH, baladevaH, rAmaH. — As elder brother of Kṛṣṇa) acyutAgrajaH. — (As armed with a plough-share) halAyuDaH, halaBft m., halI m. (n), sIrapARiH, saNkarzaRaH. — (As carrying a pestle-like club) musalI m. (n). — (As having the palm for a banner) tAlaDvajaH, tAlANkaH. — (As diverting the stream of the Yamunā) kAlindIBedanaH. — (As dressed in blue) nIlAmbaraH. — (As husband of Revatī) revatI- ramaRaH. — (As killer of a certain demon) pralambaGnaH. — (As guar- dian of Kāma) kAmapAlaH.

BALARĀMA . This god is not often regarded as an avatār of Viṣṇu, but rather as an incarnation of the great ser- pent Ananta; hence he is sometimes called SezaH or anantaH. He was the son of Vasudeva by Devakī, but was trans- ferred from the latter to the womb of Rohiṇī, the other wife of Vasudeva, and hence his name, saNkarzaRaH. Other [Page853-a+ 51] names for him are — (Fond of wine) priyamaDuH m. — (Killer of the boxer Muṣṭika) muzwikAntakaH. — (Secret in motion) guptacaraH. — (Strong and good) balaBadraH.
Balcony, s. varaMqaH, pragrIvaH, vitardi-rdI f.
BALCONY: (1) pragrIvaH (?);(2) vitardDiH (?); (3) indrakozaH (?).
BALCONY , s. varaRqaH, indrakozaH, pragrIvaH -vaM, nizkASaH, vitardDiH f. or -rdDI.
Bald, a. vi-a-keSa (SI f.), muMqa, Kalati. 2 anAvfta, nagna, asaMskfta. 3 asaBya, aSizwa, alaMkArahIna.
BALD (adj.): I Hairless: q. v.:(1) akeSaH (SA, SaM);(2) Kalati (mfn.) (by disease).II Without natural covering: anAvftaH (tA, taM). III Unadorned, inelegant: q. v.: asaMskftaH (tA, taM).

BALD , a. (Without hair) muRqaH -RqA -RqaM, muRqitaH -tA -taM, akeSaH -SA -SaM, vikeSaH -SI -SaM, keSahInaH -nA -naM. — (Without natural co- vering) anAvftaH -tA -taM, vivftaH -tA -taM, nagnaH -gnA -gnaM. — (Un- adorned, inelegant) asaMskftaH -tA -taM, aparizkftaH -tA -taM, asaByaH -ByA -ByaM. — (As style) alaNkArahInaH -nA -naM, avyaYjanaH -nA -naM.
BALD-PATED , a. muRqitaSirAH -rAH -raH (s), muRqamastakaH -kA -kaM, nagna- mastakaH -kA -kaM.
BALDERDASH , s. (Any thing jumbled together) prakIrRakaM. — (Non- sense) anarTakavAkyaM, AlasyavacanaM, vfTAkaTA.
BALDNESS: I Want of hair: akeSatA and sim. comp. morbid b.:(1) indraluptam;(2) KAlityaM Bha.II Of style: v. Inelegance.
BALDNESS , s. mORqyaM, muRqatA, akeSatvaM. — (Inelegance) asaByatA.
BALDRIC: prAlambam (?): v. Belt, girdle.
Baldrick, s. meKalA, kAMcI, rasa(Sa)nA. 2 rASimaMqalaM, jyotiScakraM.
BALDRICK , s. (A girdle) meKalA, kAYcI. — (The zodiac) rASicakraM, rASimaRqalaM, lagnamaRqalaM, jyotiScakraM.
Bale, s. BAMqaM, BAraH; dravyapowalikA. 2 kleSaH, vinASaH. v. t. jalaM utkzip 6 P. [Bale]ful, a. saSoka, kleSArta, duHKita. 2 prARahara (rI f.), vinASin; See Deadly.
BALE (subs.): powwalI: v. Bundle.
BALE (v.): To b. out the bilge-water (nAvaH) jalaM siYcati (sic, c. 6.).
BALE , s. BARqakaM, BARqaM, dravyakUrccaM, powalikA, dravyapowwalI, BAraH.
To BALE , v. a. (To make up into a bale) BARqaM kf, dravyARi kUrccIkf. (To bale out water) abBriRA or droRyA jalam utkzip (c. 6. -kzipati -kzeptuM) or uttul (c. 10. -tolayati -yituM).

BALEFUL , a. (Full of misery) kleSI -SinI -Si (n), duHKI -KinI -Ki (n), saSokaH -kA -kaM, SokAnvitaH -tA -taM. — (Destructive) nASI -SinI -Si (n), AtpayikaH -kI -kaM, prARaharaH -rA -raM, kleSakaH -kI -kaM, hiMsraH -srA -sraM.
BALEFULLY , adv. saSokaM, sakleSaM, duHKena, yaTA hiMsA jAyate taTA.
BALING-VESSEL , s. sekapAtraM, secanaM, sektraM, abBri n., aBriH f., ambusecanI, droRiH f., -RI, avagAdaH, kAzWakuddAlaH, kAzWAmbuvAhinI f.
Balk, v. t. See Baffle. s. setuH, setubaMDaH.
BALK (subs.): I Of a field:(1) AliH;(2) AlI (f.).II A beam, rafter: q. v.III Disappointment: q. v.: ASABaNgaH.
BALK (v. t.): KaRqayati (KaRq, c. 10.): v. To frustrate, disappoint.
BALK , s. (A ridge of land left unploughed) setuH m.

To BALK v. a. (To frustrate, disappoint) KaRq (c. 10. KaRqayati -yituM), pratihan (c. 2. -hanti -hantuM), vfTA kf, muDA kf, BagnASaM -SAM -SaM kf, moGASaM -SAM -SaM kf, vyarTIkf, moGIkf, vaYc in caus. (vaYcayati -yituM).
BALKED , p. p. pratihataH -tA -taM, BagnodyamaH -mA -maM, KaRqitaH -tA -taM, vaYcitaH -tA -taM, parivaYcitaH -tA -taM, vipralabDaH -bDA -bDaM.
BALKH , s. (The country) vAhlIkaH.
Ball, s. kaMdukaH (for playing); golaH-la, vartula, maMqalaM; ‘eye b(all)’ tArA. 2 nftyakrIqA; ‘b(all) room’ nftyasTAnaM.

BALL (subs.): I A playing-ball: alternately striking with her left and right hands, sent (th b.) up vAmadakziRAByAM karAyAM paryAyeRABiGnatyudasTApayat D. vi.II A round mass:(1) gola (mn.) (2) vartulaH. a small b. gulikA; the eye b. tArA a b. of thread sUtrakozam (?)III A meeting for dancing:(1) nftyam;(2) nartanam (=dancing).

BALL , s. (Any thing round) golaH -laM, maRqalaM, parimaRqalaM, golakaH, varttulaH, niGaH, piRqaM. — (The ball of the earth) BUgolaH, BUmaRqalaM. — (For playing) kandukaH, guqaH, geRquH m., geRqukaH, giriH m. — (A dancing party) sahanarttanaM, nftyakrIqA. — (A ball of thread) sUtrakozaM. — (Ball of the eye) akzigolaH. — (Ball-room) nftyasTAnaM, raNgaSAlA, vAsakarRI f.
To BALL , v. a. (To make into a ball) varttulIkf, golIkf.
BALL-ROOM (subs.): *nftyaSAlA; nartanakozWaH.
Ballad, s. gItaM, gIti f., gAnaM; ‘b(allad) singer’ gAyakaH.
BALLAD: gATA. b. singer; (1) gATikaH;(2) gATAkAraH.
BALLAD , s. (A song) gItaM, gAnaM, gItiH f., saNgItaM.
BALLAD-SINGER , s. gAyakaH, gATAkAraH, gATakaH, gAtA m. (tf).
Ballast, s. potasTEryadravyaM.
BALLAST *nilamaH; potasTEryArTaM tadaGomAganivizwaM prastara- -lohAdidravyam.
BALLAST , s. nAva aDoBAge sTApito BAraH, potasTirIkaraRAya tadaDoBAge yat prastarabAlukAdi dravyaM niveSyate, sTEryyadravyaM.
To BALLAST , v. a. nOkAyAH sTirIkaraRAya tadaDoBAge BAraM sTA in caus. (sTApayati -yituM), sTirIkf.
BALLET: no equiv.: yAtrA would do. b. girl: ( I) nartakI;(2) nawI.
BALLET , s. hallIzaM -zakaM. BALUSTRADE, s. pragrIvaH.
Balloon, s. vimAnaM, AkASa-vyoma-yAnaM.
BALLOON: (1) vimAnam;(2) vyomayAnam.
BALLOON , s. AkASayAnaM, vyomayAnaM, AkASavartmanA gamanArTaM vimAnaM.
Ballot, s. guwi(li)kA.
BALLOT (subs.): I A ball or ticket used in voting: *guwikA.II Voting. by b.: *guwikA; niBftaguwikApAtena matAmataprakASanam.
BALLOT (v. i.): guwikApAtena matAmataM prakASayati (c. of. kAS).

BALLOT , s. (A ball or ticket used in voting) guwikA, gulikA, kAkinI f., kaparddakaH, svIkftAsvIkftacihnaM. — (The act of voting by ballot) guwikAM niBftaM pAtayitvA svIkftAsvIkftajYApanaM or matAmatasUcanaM.
To BALLOT , v. n. svIkftAsvIkftajYApanAya guwikAM niBftaM pat in caus. (pAtayati -yituM).
Balm, s. guggulaH, vfkzaniryAsaH. 2 praSamaH, SAMtiH f. [Balm]y, a. suraBi. 2 tApahara (rI f.), SAMtida, upaSamaka.
BALM: I The sap of a shrub: niryAsaviSezaH. II Solace, comfort: q. v. suGAlepaH (?).
BALM , s. (The juice of a shrub) gugguluH m. — (That which al- leviates) praSamanaM, SAntiH f., upaSAntiH f., vedanASAntiH f.
BALMY: I Odoriferous, aromatic: q. v. suganDi (mfn.).II Assuaging, soothing(1) tApaharaH (rI, raM);(2) SAntidaH (dA, daM). Ph. the b. tree *vAmavfkzaH.
BALMY , a. (Having the qualities of balm) pUrvvoktavfkzarasopetaH -tA -taM. — (Soothing) upaSamakaH -kA -kaM, upaSAyI -yinI -yi (n). — (Fra- grant) sOganDikaH -kI -kaM, suraBiH -BiH -Bi.
Balsam, s. vilepanaM, aByaMjanaM. [Balsam]ic, a. snigDa, cikkaRa.
BALSAM , s. (Ointment, unguent) vilepaH, vilepanaM, upadehaH, aByaYjanaM.
BALSAMIC , a. (Unctuous) snigDaH -gDA -gDaM, meduraH -rA -raM, prameditaH -tA -taM, cikkaRaH -RA -RaM, snehI -hinI -hi (n), mfduH -dvI -du.
Baluster, s. laGustaMBaH.
Balustrade, s. laGustaMBapaMkti f.
BALUSTRADE: pragrIvaH (m. n.) (?); vfttiviSezaH.
BALUSTRADE , s. paNktikrameRa racitaH kzudrastamBasamUhaH, kzudrastamBaSreRI.
Bamboo, m. veRuH, vaMSaH, kIcakaH (‘sounding b(amboo)’).
BAMBOO: (1) veRuH;(2) vaMSaH;(3) kIcakaH (when rattling).
BAMBOO , s. veRuH, vaMSaH, vetasaH, tvaksAraH, SataparvvA m. (n), maskaraH, tfRaDvajaH, yavaPalaH, tejanaH, karmmAraH. — (When rattling) kIcakaH.
BAMBOOZLE: (v. t.): vaYcayate (vaYc, c. 10.): v. Fool, to make a; to deceive.
To BAMBOOZLE , v. a. (To cheat) vaYc in caus. (vaYcayate -yituM), parivaYc, pralaB (c. 1. -laBate -labDuM), vipralaB, Cal (c. 10. Calayati -yituM).
BAMBOOZLED , p. p. vaYcitaH -tA -taM, pralabDaH -bDA -bDaM, vipralabDaH -bDA -bDaM.
BAMBOOZLER , s. vaYcakaH, CalI m. (n), DUrttaH, kUwakaH, kitavaH, pratArakaH.
Ban, s. GozaRaM. 2 aBiSApaH, AkroSaH. 3 ni-prati-zeDaH. v. t. aBiSap 1 U, pratiziD 1 P.

BAN: I A proclamation: q. v.II Of marriage: Ph. have you published the b. s of marriage *api vivAhaGozaRA prakASitA.III Inter- -diction, proscription: q. v.: Ph. under b. to touch nizidDasparSaH (rSA, rSaM).IV Curse: SApaH.

BAN , s. (Public notice of any thing) GozaRaM -RA, GozaRApatraM, utkIrttanaM, samAcAraH. — (A curse) SApaH, aBiSApaH, AkroSaH; ‘under a ban,’ SApagrastaH -stA -staM. — (Interdiction) nizeDaH, pratizeDaH, vAraRaM, viroDaH.
To BAN , v. a. (To curse) Sap (c. 1. Sapati -te, c. 4. Sapyati, SaptaM), aBiSap, pariSap.
Banal, a. kzudra, laGu, tucCa.
Banana, s. kadalI, tfRasArA, gucCaPalA.
BANANA: I The tree:(1) kadalI;(2) ramBA. II The fruit:(1) kadalIPalam;(2) campakam (a species of it).
BANANA , s. kadalI, tfRasArA, gucCaPalA, vAraRavuzA, ramBA, mocA, kAzWIlA.
Band, s. baMDaH, pASaH, baMDanaM. 2 samUhaH, SreRI. 3 dalaM, gulmaH-lmaM (of troops). 4 tUryasamUhaH, vAditragaRaH. v. samil 6 P, saMyuj 10; See Assemble.

BAND (subs.): I That which binds:(1) banGaH: b. of hope ASAbanGaH, Me. i. 10;(2) banGanam;(3) banGanI.II A company of persons:(1) dalam;(2) gulmaH (b. of troops). III Musical instruments:(1) vAdyaBARqam. (?);(2) tUryEGaH (?).

BAND , s. (That which binds) banDanaM or -nI or -naH. — (Bond) pASaH, SfNKalaM. — (Union or connection) sambanDaH, saMyogaH. — (A company of persons) paNktiH f., samUhaH, SreRI, samAgamaH. — (Of musical instruments) vAdyaBARqaM, vAditragaRaH, tUyyOGaH. — (A com- pany of soldiers) gulmaH, sEnikaH.
To BAND , v.a. saMyuj (c. 10. -yojayati -yituM), ekatra kf.
To BAND , v. n. ekatra mil (c. 6. milati, melituM), sammil.
BAND TOGETHER (v.): saMhataH (tA, taM) (Bavati) (BU, c. 1.) v. To combine.
BAND-BOX: pewikA.
Bandage, s. baMDaH, baMDanaM, pawwaH, AvezwanaM.
BANDAGE (subs.): (1) banDaH, Śr.;(2) pawwaH (cloth) (only when the sense is clear).
BANDAGE (v. t.): baDnAti (banD, c. 9.), b. with a soft cloth mfdupawwaM niveSya baDnIyAt, Śr. Ph. things used in b. ing sores vraRabanGanadravyARi, Śr.
BANDAGE , s. pawwaH, banDanaM, pawwakaH, AvezwanaM, kavalikA. — (Securing with bandages in surgery) anuvellitaM.

details.body: BANDBOX , s. yat kiYcillaGuvastraM strIlokena BftaM tadADAnayogyaH sampuwakaH [Page037-b+ 51] or ADAraH.
Bandit, s. dasyuH, coraH, stenaH.
BANDIT: paripanTin (m); dasyuH v. Robber.
BANDIT , s. paripanTI m. (n), dasyuH, prasahyacOraH, cOraH, viplavakArI m. (n), sAraRikaGnaH.
Bandy, v. t. itastato vikzip 6 P. 2 vini-me 1 A; ‘b(andy) words’ vAcA uttaraM dA 3 U. [Bandy]-legged, a. prajYu, pragatajAnu. s. vakrAgrayazwi f.
BANDY (v. t.): I to exchange: q. v.: vinimayate (me, c. 1.).II to agitate: q. v.

To BANDY , v. a. (To toss to and fro) itastataH or itaScetaH kzip (c. 6. kzipati, kzeptuM). — (To give and take reciprocally) nime (c. 1. -mayate -mAtuM), vinime, parivft in caus. (-varttayati -yituM).
BANDY-LEGGED: (1) praYju (mfn.);(2) pragatajAnu (mfn.).
BANDY-LEGGED , a. prajYuH -jYuH -jYu, pragatajAnuH -nuH -nu, viralajAnuH -nuH -nu.
Bane, s. garaH-raM, vizaM. 2 (fig.) nASa-anarTa-mUlaM, kzayakAraRaM, vinASahetuH, ADiH; vAmAH kulasyADayaH (S. 4). ‘are a b(ane) to the family’. [Bane]ful, a. vizAnvita, saviza, vinASin, vinASana.

BANE: I Poison: q. v. vizam.II Any fatal cause of mischief: Ph. he became the b. of India *BAratavarzasya kAlarUpo or kAlo baBUva; prosti- tution is the b. of society *veSyAvfttiH samAjasyAnarTa- mUlam.III Ruin, destruction: q. v.
BANE , s. (Poison) vizaM, garaH -raM, halAhalaH. — (Ruin) nASaH, vinASaH, atyayaH, dUzaRaM. — (Causing ruin) dUzakaH.

BANEFUL , a. (Poisonous) vizaDaraH -rA -raM, garalI -linI -li (n). vizAnvitaH -tA -taM, vizatulyaH -lyA -lyaM. — (Destructive) nASI -SinI -Si (n), vinASakaH -kA -kaM, AtyayikaH -kI -kaM, dUzakaH -kA -kaM, hiMsraH -srA -sraM.
BANEFULNEES , s. vizAlutA, nASitvaM, hiMsratA, sagaratA.
Bang, v. t. prahf 1 P, taq 10, aBi-prati-han 2 P. s. AGAtaH, prahAraH, karAGAtaH.
BANG (v.): v. To beat, strike. Ph. the door b. s virOti kapAwaH Mr.
BANG (subs.): Ph. opened the door with a b. mahASabdapUrvakaM kapAwamapAvftavAn: v. Explosion; v. Also blow, stroke.
To BANG , v. a. (To beat, thump) taq (c. 10. tAqayati -yituM), prahf (c. 1. -harati -harttuM), tud (c. 6. tudati -tottuM), Atud.
BANG , s. AGAtaH, aBiGAtaH, prahAraH, muzwipAtaH, karAGAtaH.
Bangle, s. valayaH-yaM, kaMkaRaM.
BANIAN-TREE: (1) vawaH;(2) nyagroDaH, its berry: nEyagroDam.

Banish, v. t. vi-nir-vas c., pravraj c. 2 nirAkf 8 U, niH-ut-sf c., apAnud 6 P, niras 4 P; ‘the thought was b(anish)ed from his mind’ sA ciMtA manaso nirastA. [Banish]ment, s. vivAsanaM, nirvAsanaM, pravrA(vra)janaM. 2 nirAkaraRaM, nirasanaM.

BANISH (v. t.): I To condemn to exile:(1) nir-vAsayati (c. of vas), first of all, Fivasiddhi was b. ed from the city AdAveva jIvasiDirnagarAnni- rvAsitaH Mu. ii.;(2) vi-vAsayati (c. of vas) M. viii. 123;(3) nir-asyati (as, c. 4.) b. ed Fānaki from his house, but not from his mind gfhAnnirastA na tena vEdehasutA manastaH, R. xiv. 84. v. To drive away.(4) pra-vrAjayati (c. of vraj) (rare) M.II Fig. To drive away, remove: q. v. shame was b. ed (from their minds) trapA nirastA, Ki. x. 58.

To BANISH , v. a. (To another country) vivas in caus. (-vAsayati -yituM), nirvas, pravas, vipravas, pravraj in caus. (-vrAjayati -yituM), deSAntarIkf. — (To drive away) nirAkf (c. 8. -karoti -karttuM), vahizkf or vahiH kf, niHsf, in caus. (-sArayati -yituM), utsf; apAnud (c. 6. -nudati -nottuM), niras (c. 4. -asyati -asituM).
BANISHED , p. p. pravAsitaH -tA -taM, vivAsitaH -tA -taM, niHsAritaH -tA -taM, vahizkftaH -tA -taM, nirastaH -stA -staM, nirAkftaH -tA -taM, niHkAsitaH -tA taM, avakfzwaH -zwA -zwaM.
BANISHMENT: (1) nirvAsanam;(2) vivAsanam;(3) pravAsanam.
BANISHMENT , s. (The act) pravAsanaM, vivAsanaM, nirvAsanaM, pravrAjanaM, niH- sAraRaM, nirasanaM, apanodanaM, nirAkaraRaM. — (The state) pravAsaH, vivAsaH.
BANISTER: *sopAnastamBaH.
BANISTER , s. sopAne uBayataH sTApitA kzudrastamBapaNktiH.
Bank, s. tIraM, kUlaM, tawaM-wI, roDas n., kacCaH; ‘the other b(ank)’ pAraM; ‘sand b(ank)’ sEkataM. 2 DanAgAraM. v. t. kUlena parivezw 1 A or c. [Bank]er, s. DanAgArapatiH; SrezWin m., kusIdikaH.

BANK (subs.): I For dealing in money: *DanAgAram, the affairs of the b. were wound up *DanAgArakAryARi saMhftAni; the b. failed *DanAgAramava- sasAda or kzayaM jagAma.II Of a river etc.:(1) tIram;(2) tawam;(3) kUlam;(4) pratIram;(5) roGas (n.);(6) kacCaH (rare). The opposite b. pAram. The near b. apAram. A sand b. sEkatam. B. of a hill vapram.III A mound: q. v.(1) cayaH; (2) vapra (mn.).
BANK (v. i.): (GanAgAreRa) vyavaharati (hf, c. 1.) (?).

BANK , s. (Of a river) tIraM, tawaM -waH, kUlaM, pratIraM, kacCaH, roDaH n. (s); ‘the opposite bank,’ pAraM, tIrAntaraM; ‘the near bank,’ avAraM. — (Any heap) cayaH, kUlaM, piRqanaH, vapraH; ‘sand-bank,’ sEkataM. — (A place where money is laid up) DanAgAraM, mudrAgAraM, nikziptaDanAgAraM, waNkAgAraM.

To BANK , v. a. (To inclose with a bank) kUlena or vapreRa parivezw (c. 1. -vezwate -vezwituM). — (To lay up money in a bank) DanAgAre DanaM nikzip (c. 6. -kzipati -kzeptuM) or nyas (c. 4. -asyati -asituM), kusIdikaM nikawe DanaM sTA in caus. (sTApayati -yituM).
BANK-BILL , BANK-NOTE, s. AnfRyapratijYApatraM or fRaSoDanapratijYApatraM yaddarSanAd mudrAgAre nikziptaDanaM pratidIyate, nikziptaDanavinimayena yat pratijYApatraM pracalIkriyate.
BANK-NOTE: *DanAgArapatram.
BANKER: (1) SrezWin (m.) (?);(2) *DanAgArapatiH; (3) kusIdaH; vArdDuzikaH (money-lender).
BANKER , s. (Keeper of a bank) DanAgArapatiH m., mudrAgArapatiH. — (Trader in money) kusIdikaH, kalopajIvI m. (n).
BANKER , s. DanavyavahArI m., DanavyApArI m. BANKING, s. DanavyavahAraH.
BANKING: (1) vyavahAraH P. i.;(2) arTavyavahAraH; (3) arTaprayogaH.
Bankrupt, s. fRadAna-fRaSoDana-akzamaH, sarvasvacyutaH, parikzIRaH, nirDanaH. [Bankrupt]cy, s. parikzIRatA, fRaSoDanAkzamatA, &c.
BANKRUPT (subs.): parikzIRo vaRik (after M.); fRaSoGanAkzamo vaRik (?) A fraudulent b. *prakASa- parikzIRaH; uttamarRapravaYcanAya yo gataviBavatAM prakASayati.
BANKRUPT , s. parikzIRaH, fRaSoDanAya akzama fRI (n) or aDamarRaH or fRavAn (t), asamarTarRaSoDanaH, aSaktAnfRyaH, gataviBavaH, sarvvasvacyutaH, nirDanaH, hatasampadaH.
BANKRUPTCY: parikzIRatA (?); fRaSoGanASaktiH (?): gataviBAvatA (?)
BANKRUPTCY , s. parikzIRatA, fRaSoDanASaktiH f., fRamokzAsAmarTyaM, nirDanatA.
Banner, s. DvajaH, patAkA, ketanaM, vEjayaMtI, ketuH.
BANNER: (1) DvajaH;(2) patAkA;(3) ketuH; (4) vEjayantI;(5) ketanam.
BANNER , s. patAkA, DvajaH or -jaM, ketanaM, vEjayantI f., DvajapawaH.
BANNERET: *iMlaRqIyopAGiviSezaH.
BANNOCK: pizwakaviSezaH.
Banns, s. vivAhaGozaRA.
BANNS , s. (Of marriage) vivAhaGopaRA, vivAhaGopaRapatraM.

Banquet, s. viSizwaBojanaM, svAdvannaBojanaM. v. t. mizwAnnEH Buj c. or saMtuz c. v. i. viSizwAnnaM Buj 7 A or Bakz 10; ‘the horses were b(anquett)ing upon the grass’ aSvAstfRaM yaTezwaM BakzayaMta Asata.
BANQUET (subs.): samBojanam (?); viSizwaBojanam (?).
BANQUET (v. t.): (1) sam-Bojayati (c. of Buj); (2) BojanaviSezEH sam-tozayati (c. of tuz), H.
BANQUET (v. i.): (1) BuMkte (Buj, c. (?));(2) aByava-harati (hf, c. 1.).
BANQUET , s. utsavaH, samBojanaM, svAdvannaBojanaM.

To BANQUET , v. a. svAdvannEH or mizwAnnEH or BojanaviSezEH or saviSezAnnEH Buj in caus. (Bojayati -yituM) or santup in caus. (-tozayati -yituM) [Page038-a+ 51] or saMvfD in caus. (-vardDayati -yituM) or tfp in caus. (tarpayati -yituM).
To BANQUET , v. n. utsavaM kf, viSizwAnnaM or svAdvannaM or BojanaviSezAn or saviSezAnnaM Buj (c. 7. BuMkte, BoktuM), viSizwarUpeRa AhAraM kf, Atma- mBariH -riH -ri as.
BANQUETER , s. utsavakarttA m. (rttf), viSizwAnnaBoktA m. (ktf), svAdvannasa- ntozitaH, svAdvannaBakzakaH.
BANQUETING , s. utsavakaraRaM, viSizwAnnaBojanaM, svAdvannaKAdanaM.
Banter, v. t. Barts 10 A, niMd 1 P, aDikzip 6 P. 2 ava-vi-upa-has 1 P. s. niMdA, aDikzepaH, avahAsaH, &c.
BANTER (v. t.): pari-hasati (has, c. 1.): v. To joke, mock.
BANTER (subs.): parihAsaH; v. Joke, jesting.
To BANTER , v. a. avahas (c. 1. -hasati -hasituM), apahas, vihas with acc.; avakzip (c. 6. -kzipati -kzeptuM), Barts (c. 10. Bartsagate -ti -yituM), nind (c. 1. nindati, nindituM).
BANTERER: (1) parihAsavedin (m.);(2) parihAsavettf (m.); v. Jester.
BANTERER , s. avakzepakaH, kzepakaH, nindakaH, parihAsavedI m. (n).
BANTLING: (1) qimBaH;(2) arBakaH; v. Infant.
BANTLING , s. bAlaH, -lA, bAlakaH, SiSuH m.
Banyan, s. vawaH, nyagroDaH.
BANYAN-TREE , s. vawaH, nyagroDaH, parkawI.
BAPTISM: *aBizekaH, a certificate of b. *aBizeka- nidarSanam.
BAPTISM , s. majjanaM, jalasaMskAraH, avagAhanaM.
BAPTISMAL: expr. by tat. comp, by font *aBizekakuRqam.
BAPTISMAL , a. majjanasambanDI -nDinI -nDi (n), jalasaMskAravizayaH -yA -yaM.
BAPTIST: I In gen.: *aBizektf (m.).II An anabaptist: q. v.
BAPTIST , s. majjayitA m. (tf), avagAhakaH, jalasaMskArakarttA m. (rttf).
BAPTISTERY , s. majjanasTAnaM, avagAhanasTAnaM, jalasaMskArakaraRasTAnaM.
BAPTIZE (v. t.): (1) *aBiziYcati (sic, c. 6.); (2) *kfzwaGarmaM grAhayati (c. of. graha).
To BAPTIZE , v. a. majj in caus. (majjayati -yituM), nimajj, avagAh in caus. (-gAhayati -yituM), jalasaMskAraM kf.

details.body: Bar, s. argalaM-lA, argalAbaMDaH. 2 pratyUhaH, aMtarAyaH. 3 SalAkA (of a cage). 4 daMqaH; ‘iron b(ar)’ lohadaMqaH, lohapiMqaH. 5 sEkataM. 6 nyAyasaBA. v. t. ni-pati-ruD 7 U, ni-prati-ziD 1 P, nirAkf 8 U, niras 4 P, nivf c. or nivAr 10. 2 argalena baMD 9 P.

BAR (subs.): I Of a door: argalam.II Of a cage etc.: SalAkA. v. Pole, beam.III A hindrance or obstruction: q. v.: pratyUhaH. IV A bank at the mouth of a river or harbour: banGaH (?). V. For prisoners in a court of justice, or an inn.: *vftiH.VI Any tribunal: q. v.: Ph. at the b. of public opinion *sADAraRamatasyAgre.VII The entire body of advocates: *aBiBAzakavargaH, uttaravAdinaH (m. pl.).VIII In music: lambaH (?).IX An ingot or wedge of metal: Perh. piRqaH.
BAR (v. t.): I To bolt: q. v.II To hinder, prevent: q. v.:(1) ni-ruRadDi (ruD, c. 7.); (2) prati-zeDati (siD, c. 1.).

BAR , s. (Of a door) argalaM. — (Of a cage) SalAkA. — (Any ob- stacle) viGnaH, avaroDaH -DakaM, vyAGAtaH, pratizwamBaH, bADakaH, pratibanDaH, pratyUhaH. — (A sand-bank) sEkataM. — (The place where criminals are tried) DarmmasaBA, vicArasTAnaM. — (A solid mass of metal) lohapiRqaH -RqaM, kuSI. — (In music) tAlaniyAmakA reKA. — (In a tavern) SuRqApAne madyakretfvikretroraByantare sTApitam avaroDakaM tatra ca tanmaDye vigaRanaM kriyate.

To BAR , v. a. (To fasten with a bar) argalena banD (c. 9. baDnAti, badDuM). — (To hinder) vf in caus. (vArayati -yituM), nivf, prativf; pratiruD (c. 7. -ruRadDi -rodDuM), niruD, viruD, pratibanD. — (To shut out from) nirAkf, niras (c. 4. -asyati -asituM). — (To exclude) vahizkf, nirAkf. — (To prohibit) pratiziG (c. 1. -seDati -sedDuM), niziD; antaHKyA (c. 2. -KyAti -KyAtuM).
Barb, s. karRaH, SUlAgraM. 2 aSvatanutraM. [Barb]ed, a. karRin
BARB (subs.): I A. horse: q. v.: vAjiH.II Of an arrow: karRaH (?).

BARB , s. (A species of horse brought from Barbary) videSa- jAtIyaH sutanukAyaviSizwas turagapraBedaH. — (A crooked point) PalaM, karRaH, SUlAgraM, SaraPalaM. — (Armour for horses) praKaraH, prakzaraH, aSvatanutraM, aSvasajjA.
BARBACAN , s. prAkArIyanagaropAnte nirmmitaM durgaM.
Barbarian, s. grAmyaH, asaByaH. 2 mlecCaH; yavanaH, kirAtaH. 3 videSin m., vEdeSikaH.
BARBARIAN (subs.): I An uncivilized person: (1) asaByaH (ByA, ByaM);(2) mlecCaH (properly one who is not a Hindu, but may be used in the sense of b.).II A cruel man: piSAcaH (?). v. Cruel.

BARBARIAN , s. mlecCaH, mlecCajAtiH m., SavaraH, kirAtaH, kzuDunaH, pulindaH. — (An uncivilized man) asaByalokaH, puruzapaSuH. — (A foreigner) videSI m. (n). — (A cruel tyrant) nirdayaH. — (The country of barbarians) pratyantaH.
BARBARIAN , BARBARIC, a. (Belonging to barbarians) mlecCI -cCinI -cCi (n). videSI -SinI -Si (n), vEdeSikaH -kI -kaM. — (Uncivi- lized) asaByaH -ByA -ByaM, asaMskftaH -tA -taM, aSizwaH -zwA -zwaM.
BARBARIC: i. e. foreign: q. v.: videSIyaH (yA, yaM)
BARBARISM: I Incorrect language: mlecCitam (?), gentlemen do not use b. s in their speech nAryAmlecCanti BAzAmiH, Mah.II An uncivilized condition: asaByatAIII Barbarity: q. v.
BARBARISM , s. (In grammar) mlecCitaM. — (Savageness of manners) krUratA, krUrAcAratA, mlecCatvaM, paSutA, durAcAratvaM.
BARBARITY (subs.): (1) nizWuratA;(2) krOryam: v. Ferocity, cruelty.
BARBARITY , s. (Cruelty) nizWuratA, nirdayatvaM, krUratA. — (Of manners) asaByatA, krUrAcAratA.
BARBARIZE (v. t.): *mlecCIkaroti (kf, c. 8.): v. To brutalize.

Barbarous, a. vEdeSika (kI f.). 2 aSizwa, asaBya, aSlIla. 3 nizWura, krUra, nirdaya. [Barbarous]ly, adv. krUraM, nizWuraM, nirdayaM, SvApadavat, paSuvat. Barbarity, s. nizWuratA, nfSaMsatA, kOryaM, asaByatA, aSizwatA.
BARBAROUS (adj.): I Uncivilized: q. v.: asaByaH (ByA, ByaM).II Cruel, ferocious: q. v.:(1) nizWuraH (rA, raM);(2) nfSaMsaH (sA, saM).

BARBAROUS , a. (Foreign) mlecCIyaH -yA -yaM, vEdeSikaH -kI -kaM. — (Sa- vage in manners) krUrAcAraH -rA -raM, kuSIlaH -lA -laM, durAcAraH -rA -raM, aSizwaH -zwA -zwaM, SOvApadaH -dI -daM. — (Cruel) nizWuraH -rA -raM, [Page038-b+ 51] nirddayaH -yA -yaM, krUraH -rA -raM.
BARBAROUSLY: I Without refinement:(1) asaByam (?);(2) aSlIlam (- coarsely, in- -decently).II Cruelly: q. v.: nirdayam.
BARBAROUSLY , adv. mlecCavat, asaByalokavat, paSuvat, SvApadavat. — (Cruelly) nirddayaM, nizWuraM, atikrUratayA.
BARBAROUSNESS: krOryam: v. Barbarity, bar- -barism.
BARBED (adj.): karRin (f. nI) (?).
BARBED , a. karRI -rRinI -rRi (n), PalayuktaH -ktA -ktaM, lOhAgrayuktaH -ktA -ktaM. — (Mailed) varmitaH -tA -taM, kavacI -cinI -ci (n), paridaMSitaH -tA -taM.
BARBEL: nAdeyamatsyaviSezaH.
BARBEL , s. nAdeyamatsyaviSezaH.
Barber, s. nApitaH, kzOrikaH, kzurin m.; ‘b(arber)ʼs wife’ nApitI; ‘b(arber)ʼs business’ nApityaM.
BARBER: (1) nApitaH;(2) kzurin (m.);(3) kzOrikaH;(4) muRqin (m.) A b. 's shop nApitaSAlA; b.'s business nApityam.
BARBER , s. nApitaH, kzurI m. (n), muRqI m. (n), kzOrikaH, antAvasAyI m. (n), divAkIrttiH m.; ‘a barber's business,’ nApityaM.
BARBERRY: gulmaviSezaH.
BARBES , s. pl. (A disease of horses) aSvIyarogaviSezaH.
BARBICAN: upadurgam, praveSaniroGanArTaM nagaropAntanirmito durgaviSezaH.
Bard, s. vaMdin m., vEtAlikaH.
BARD: I(1) mAgaDaH;(2) vEtAlikaH;(3) vandin (m.);(4) maGukaH.II A poet: q. v.: kaviH.
BARD , s. mAgaDaH, vandI m. (n), maDukaH. — (Poet) kaviH m., kAvyaSAstrajYaH.
BARDICK , a. mAgaDasambanDI -nDinI -nDi (n), kAvyaSAstrasambanDIyaH -yA -yaM.

Bare, a. anAvfta, SUnya. 2 kevala, mAtra in comp.; ‘on the b(are) ground’ avyavaDAnAyAM BUmAveva (Ka. 151). 3 vivastra; ‘b(are) footed’ pAdukAhIna, anAvftapAda; ‘b(are) headed’ anAvftaSiras; ‘b(are) faced’ nirlajja, Dfzwa; ‘thread b(are)’ (clothes). jIrRAni vAsAMsi. v. t. nagnIkf 8 U, vivastrIkf; ucCad 10. 2 utkfz 1 P. [Bare]ly, adv. mAtraM, kevalaM. 2 kaTamapi, kazwena, kfcCreRa. [Bare]ness, s. SUnyatA, vivastratA. 2 kzIRatA, dEnyaM.

BARE (adj.): I Uncoverd:(1) anAvftaH (tA, taM);(2) SUnyaH (nyA, nyaM);(3) kevalaH (lA, laM) (only of places and things), on the b. ground sTaRqila eva kevale, Ku. v. 12.II Destitute: q. v.: dInaH (nA, naM).III Simple, unadorned: q. v.IV Mere, alone: q. v. V. Thread- -bare: jIrRaH (rRA, rRaM).
BARE (v. t.): vivastrayati: v. To uncover, divest.

BARE , a. (Naked) nagnaH -gnA -gnaM. — (Without ornament) aBUzitaH -tA -taM, analaNkftaH -tA -taM, asaMskftaH -tA -taM. — (Unclothed) vivastraH -strA -straM. — (Uncovered) anAvftaH -tA -taM, vivftaH -tA -taM, apavftaH -tA -taM. — (Mere) kevalaH -lA -laM, mAtrakaH -kA -kaM, mAtraM. — (Thread- bare, worn) jIrRaH -rRA -rRaM; ‘the bare ground,’ kevalA BUmiH, pfTivItalaM, BUtalaM.
To BARE , v. a. (To strip, uncover) nagnIkf; vyaktIkf; ucCad (c. 10. -CAdayati -yituM), vivf (c. 5. -vfRoti -varituM -varItuM).
BARE-FACED (adj.): nirlajjaH (jjA, jjaM): v. Im- -pudent.
BARE-FACEDLY (adv.): nirlajjam: v. Impu- -dently.
BARE-FACEDNESS: nirlajjatA: v. Impudence, effrontery.
BARE-FOOT, BARE-FOOTED: SUnyapAdaH (dA, daM); (2) anAvftapAdaH (dA, daM).
BARE-HEADED: (1) anAvftaSiras (mfn.);(2) SUnyamastakaH (kA, kaM).
BARED , p. p. nagnIkftaH -tA -taM, vyaktIkftaH -tA -taM, vivftaH -tA -taM.
BAREFACED , a. (Shameless) nirlajjaH -jjA -jjaM, lajjAhInaH -nA -naM, DfzwaH -zwA -zwaM.
BAREFACEDNESS , s. nirlajjatvaM, DfzwatA, DArzwyaM, pragalBatA, prAgalByaM, vEyAtyaM.
BAREFOOT , a. nagnapAdaH -dA -daM, SUnyapAdaH -dA -daM, pAdukAhInaH -nA -naM.
BAREHEADED , a. nagnaSirAH -rAH -raH (s), SUnyamastakaH -kA -kaM, anA- vftaSirAH -rAH -raH (s).
BARELY: I Only: q. v. kevalam.II Scarcely: q. v. karTaYcit.
BARELY , adv. (Merely) mAtraM, kevalaM. — (Hardly) kazwaM, kazwena, kfcCreRa. — (Nakedly) — nagnaM, SUnyaM, AcCAdanavyatirekeRa. — (Without or- nament) alaNkAravyatirekeRa, BUzaRaM vinA.
BARENESS: I Nakedness: anAvftatvam.II Indigence: q. v.: dEnyam.
BARENESS , s. (Nakedness) nagnatvaM, SUnyatA, riktatA. — (Leanness, poverty) kzIRatA, daridratA, dEnyaM.

Bargain, s. saMvid f., samayaH, aByupagamaH, ‘a b(argain) was struck’ iti samayaH kftaH; ‘buy the horse, it is a good b(argain)’ stokamUlyena laByateyamaSvaH krIRIhi tAvadenaM; ‘in the b(argain)’ api, aparaMca. 2 paRaH, vipaRaH, krayavikrayaniyamaH. v. t. paR 1 A, vyavahf 1 P.
BARGAIN (subs.): I An agreement or stipu- -lation: q. v.(1) samayaH;(2) saMvid (f.).II. A gainful or satisfactory transaction: Ph. buy the house, it is a good b. *alpamUlyena laByaM gfhaM krIRIhi.
BARGAIN (v. i.); paRate (paR, c. 1.) (?): v. To agree, stipulate.

BARGAIN , s. (A contract, agreement) samayaH, niyamaH, saMvid f., upagamaH, aByupagamaH, saMSravaH, ASravaH, samADiH m., uddeSaH. — (Con- tract concerning the price of a thing sold) paRaH, vipaRaH, krayaniyamaH, krayavikrayaniyamaH, krayapatraM.
To BARGAIN , v. n. paR (c. 1. paRate, paRituM or paRAyati -yituM), paRaM kf, saNGaww (c. 1. -Gawwate -GawwituM), samayAkf, niyamIkf, krayavikrayaniyamaM kf.
BARGAINED , p. p. paRitaH -tA -taM, paRAyitaH -tA -taM, saNGawwitaH -tA -taM.
Barge, s. kelinOkA. 2 tarAluH, vahitraM. [Barge]-man, s. nAvikaH, potavAhaH.
BARGE: I A pleasure-boat: kelinOkA (?). II A large boat for the conveyance of passengers or goods:(1) tarAluH;(2) tarAnDuH; (3) vahitram.
BARGE , s. tarAluH m., tarAnDuH m., vahitraM. — (Pleasure-boat) kelinOkA.
BARGEMAN: (1) nAvikaH;(2) potavAhaH.
BARGEMAN , s. nAvikaH, potavAhaH, pUrvvoktanOkAkarRaDAraH, tarikaH.

Bark, v. tvac f., valkaM, valkalaH-laM. 2 potaH kzudranOH, tarIH. v. i. bukk 1 P, 10; ‘dogs b(ark) at the moon’ SvAnaH SaSinaM vIkzya bukkayaMti; Baz 1 P. v. t. tvacaM-valkaM-apanI 1 P, or nizkfz 1 P. [Bark]ing, s. bukkanaM, BazaRaM. [Bark]y, a. vAlkala (lI f.), tvaNmaya (yI f.).
BARK (subs.): I Of trees:(1) valkala (mn.); (2) valkam;(3) tvac (f.);(4) CalliH (f.) (rare). II Of dogs: bukkanam.III A small vessel (1) nOH;(2) tarI.
BARK (v. t.): (1) valkalaM nirharati (hf, c. 10.), apanayati (nI, c. 1.) etc;(2) tvacayati (nomi.); (3) tvakzati (tvakz, c. 1.).
BARK (v. i.): (1) bukkayati, te (bukk, c. 1.), b. ed at by dogs kukkurErbukkyamAnaH Mr. i:(2) Bazati (Baz, c. 1.), human dogs always b. thus Bazanti hEvaM SvanarAH sadEva, Mah.

BARK , s. valkalaH -laM, valkaM, tvak f. (c), tvacaM, CallI f., SalkaM, SalkalaM; ‘bark of a tree,’ tarutvak f. (c). — (Made of bark) tvaNmayaH -yI -yaM, tarutvaqnirmmitaH -tA -taM, vAlkalaH -lI -laM. — (Garment of) valkalaH. — (A small ship) potaH, kzudranOkA.

To BARK , v. a. (To strip trees of their bark) tvac (nom. tvacayati -yituM), valk (nom. valkayati -yituM), tvakz (c. 1. tvakzati, tvakzituM), valkam utkfz (c. 1. -karzati -krazwuM) or nizkfz. — (To enclose, as bark) valkalavat parivezw (c. 1. -vezwate -vezwituM).
To BARK , v. n. Baz (c. 1. Bazati, BazituM), bukk (c. 1. bukkati, bukkituM, c. 10. bukkayati -yituM), rE (c. 1. rAyati, rAtuM). — (To revile) AkruS (c. 1. -kroSati -krozwuM), muKarIkf.
BARKER , s. BazakaH. — (Reviler) AkroSakaH.
BARKING: Of dogs: (1) bukkanam;(2) Bazitam: v. Noise.
BARKING , s. (Of dogs) BazaRaM, bukkanaM, rAyaRaM, rutaM.
BARKY , a. vAlkaH -lkI -lkaM, vAlkalaH -lI -laM, tvaNmayaH -yI -yaM.
BARLERIA , s. (A flower) vARA, ArttagalaH, kuravakaH, sahacarI, kzuraH.
Barley, s. yavaH, pravewaH; ‘b(arley) broth’ yavasurA-raM; ‘b(arley) corn’ yavaH; ‘unripe b(arley)’ kulmAzaM; ‘b(arley) water’ udamaMTaH.
BARLEY: yavaH. Fit for producing b. yavakyaH (kyA, kyaM). made of b. yavamayaH (yI, yaM).

BARLEY , s. yavaH, yavakaH, tIkzRaSUkaH, pravewaH, SitaSUkaH; ‘unripe bar- ley,’ tokmaH, yAvakaH, kulmAzaM; ‘barley-meal,’ yavakzodaH; ‘bar- ley-water,’ udamanTaH; ‘made of barley,’ yavamayaH -yI -yaM; ‘sown with barley,’ yavyaH -vyA -vyaM.
BARLEY , s. sAktukaH, saktuH m. BARLEY-WATER, s. yavodakaM.
BARLEY-BROTH , s. yavasuraM, yavanirmmitaM pAnIyaM, yavarasaH.
BARLEY-CORN: yavaH. Fried b. DAnA.
BARLEY-CORN , s. yavaH, tiryyagyavodaraM.
BARLEY-MOW , s. lUnayavasaNgrahaRasTAnaM, yave lUne sati tatsaYcayanasTAnaM.
BARLEY-SUGAR: sitAKaRqaH (?).
BARLEY-SUGAR , s. yavarasakvaTita ikzusAraH, mAkzikaSarkarA, SuklopalA.
BARLEY-WATER: (1) udamanTaH;(2) yavodakam.
Barm, s. surA-madya-maMqaH.
BARM: maRqaH or (more fully) surAmaRqaH: v. Yeast.
BARM , s. surAmaRqaH, madyamaRqaH, kArottaraH, kArottamaH, aBizavaH.
BARMAID: *maRqaparakziRI.
Barn, s. kuSUlaH, DAnyAgAraM, DAnyasaMgrahasTAnaM.
BARN: (1) kuSUlaH;(2) GAnyakozWam,(3) GAnyA- gAram.
BARN , s. kuSUlaH, SasyaBARqaM, BARqAgAraH, DAnyAgAraH, DAnyakozWakaM, DA- nyasaNgrahasTAnaM.

sanskrit.slp1: yena turaNgo muKadeSe GriyamARo'Svacikitsakena cikitsituM Sakyate
sanskrit.word: येन तुरङ्गो मुखदेशे घ्रियमाणोऽश्वचिकित्सकेन चिकित्सितुं शक्यते
sanskrit.iast: yena turaṅgo mukhadeśe ghriyamāṇo'śvacikitsakena cikitsituṃ śakyate

details.body: BARNACLE: I A mollusc: SambUkaviSezaH.II A kind of goose haMsaviSezaH.III In farriery: yantraviSezaH; *nastagrahA.

BARNACLE , s. (A kind of shell-fish) nOkAkAzWajaH SambUkaviSezaH. — (An instrument to hold a horse by the nose) pASaviSezo yena turaNgo muKadeSe GriyamARo'Svacikitsakena cikitsituM Sakyate. — (A kind of bird) haMsajAtIyaH pakzipraBedaH.
Barometer, s. AkASatolanayaMtraM.
BAROMETER: *vAyumApaH.
BAROMETER , s. AkASatolanayantraM, AkASaparimARArTaM pAradapUritA kAca- nAlI.
BAROMETER , s. sAmAnyavAyumApakayantraM, vAyumApakayantraM, vAyumApakanAlaH, vAyugurutvasUcakayantraM, vAtonmAnaM.
BARON (subs.): *iMlaRqIyakOlInopADiBedaH.
BARON , s. kramAgatAnAM kulInapadAnAM maDye padapraBedaH, aDipatiH m., svAmI m. (n). — (Baron of beef) gopfzWaM, uBayapArSvIyapaYjarayuktaM gomAMsaM.
BARONAGE: I The whole body of barons: *beraRavargaH.II The rank of a baron *beraRapadam.
BARONESS: beraRavaDUH.
BARONESS , s. vakzyamARakulInapadasTitasya puruzasya patnI or BAryyA.

sanskrit.slp1: kramAgatAnAM kulInapadAnAM maDye avarapadaM yasya saH
sanskrit.word: क्रमागतानां कुलीनपदानां मध्ये अवरपदं यस्य सः
sanskrit.iast: kramāgatānāṃ kulīnapadānāṃ madhye avarapadaṃ yasya saḥ

details.body: BARONET: upAGiviSezaH: *upaberaRaH.
BARONET , s. kramAgatAnAM kulInapadAnAM maDye avarapadaM yasya saH.
BARONIAL (adj.): *beraRIyaH (yA, yaM).
BARONIAL , a. pUrvvoktakulInapadasambanDI -nDinI -nDi (n).
BARONY: *beraRasyAGipatyam; bEraRyam (?).
BARONY , s. pUrvvoktakulInapadasambanDIyam ADipatyaM or svAmyaM.
BARQUE: nOviSezaH.
Barrack, s. sEnyAvAsaH, sEnyAgAraM. v. t. sEnyAgAre sTA c. (sTApayati) or nivas c.
BARRACK: (nearest word) niveSaH; v. Camp.
BARRACK , s. sEnyAgAraM, sEnyAlayaH, ayudDasamaye sEnyanivAsasTAnaM, sEnyAvAsaH.
To BARRACK , v. a. sEnyAn sEnyAgAre pfTak pfTak sTA in caus. (sTApayati -yituM), or vas in caus. (vAsayati -yituM).
BARRACK-MASTER: *niveSADyakzaH, niveSAGikArin (m.).
BARRED , p. p. virudDaH -dDA -dDaM, pratibadDaH -dDA -dDaM, nizidDaH -dDA -dDaM, bADitaH -tA -taM.
BARRED , p. p. sArgalaH -lA -laM, argalayuktaH -ktA -ktaM.
Barrel, s. dIrGagolAkAraM kAzWapAtraM. 2 (Of guns) nAqi-qI f., nAli-lI f.
BARREL (subs.): I A kind of cask: BARqam (any vessel).II A cylinder or tube, as of a gun or watch: nAlA or nAlI (?)
BARREL (v.): BARqe niveSayati (c. of viS).
BARREL , s. (A small cask) dIrGagolAkAraM kAzWanirmmitaM pAtraM or BARqaM. — (A cylinder, as of a gun) nAqiH -qI f., nAlI or -lA.
To BARREL , v. a. (To put in a barrel) pUrvvIktapAtre niviS in caus. (-veSayati -yituM).
Barren, a. vaMDya (lit. and fig.). 2 vyarTa, moGa, nizPala. 3 (Ground) anurvara, aSasyaprada, marusTalaM-lI. 4 SUnya, rikta. [Barren]ness, s. vaMDyatvaM. 2 vEyarTyaM, SuzkatA.

BARREN: (1) banDyaH (nDyA, nDyaM) (Lit. and Fig.), a. b. woman banDyA K. b. whose anger is not b. abanDyakopaH (pA, paM), Ki. i. 33.;(2) nizPalaH (lA, laM) (not applied to females: v. unfruitful). Ph. b. soil anurvarA or aSasyapradA BUmiH.

BARREN , a. (Not prolific) banDyaH -nDyA -nDyaM, asutI -tinI -ti (n), aprasavI -vinI -vi (n), prajArahitaH -tA -taM. — Unfruitful) nizPalaH -lA -laM, aPalaH -lA -laM, avakeSI -SinI -Si (n), SuzkaH -zkA -zkaM, — (Useless) vyarTaH -rTA -rTaM, anarTakaH -kA -kaM, moGaH -GA -GaM. — (Empty) SUnyaH -nyA -nyaM, riktaH -ktA -ktaM; ‘a barren woman,’ banDyA, apasUtA; ‘a barren soil,’ marusTalaM or -lI.

BARREN , a. (As a woman) anapatyA, anapatyakA, ajAtApatyA, apra- jAtA. The Hindūs divide barren women into three classes, viz. 1. ‘She who has no offspring,’ banDyA; 2. ‘She who bears only one child,’ kAkabanDyA; 3. ‘She whose off- spring die,’ mftabanDyA.
BARRENNESS: (1) banDyatA;(2) banDAtvam (of females), Śr;(3) nizPalatA (fruitlessness).
BARRENNESS , s. banDyatA, nizPalatA, vEyarTyaM, SuzkatA, SUnyatA. — (In a female) banDyAtvaM.
Barricade, s. prAkAraH, vapraH-praM, prAcIraM. v. t. vi-prati-ruD 7 U; See Obstruct.
BARRICADE (subs.): vfkzAdinirmitaprAkAraH.
BARRICADE (v. t.): vfkzAdinA praveSamAgardIn avaruRadDi (ruD, c. 7.) v. To obstruct, block up.
BARRICADE or BARRICADO, s. prAcIraM, prAkAraH, vapraH -praM, avaroDakaM, paTAvaroDaH.
To BARRICADE or BARRICADO, v. a. and n. ruD (c. 7. ruRadDi, rodDuM), pratiruD, saMruD; pratibanD (c. 9. -baGnAti -badDuM); prAcIreRa paTam avaruD.
Barrier, s. vfti f., vapraH-praM, prAkAraH. 2 sIman f., sImA, paryaMtaH-taM. 3 viGnaH, pratyUhaH, aMtarAyaH, vyAGAtaH.
BARRIER: I Fence, enclosure: q. v. vftiH. II An obstacle: q. v.(1) pratibanDaH;(2) pratyUhaH.III A boundary: q. v.: sImA.

BARRIER , s. (A barricade) prAkAraH, prAcIraM, parikUwaM, vapraH. — (An obstacle) viGnaH, pratizwamBaH, avaroDakaM, pratiroDaH, pratibanDaH, sambADanaM. pratyUhaH. — (A boundary) sImA, paryyantaM, parisImA.
Barrister, s. uttaravAdin m., parArTaM vaktf m.; smftiSAstrakuSalaH.
BARRISTER: *aBiBAzakaviSezaH; vyavahArapaRqitaH.

BARRISTER , s. uttaravAdI m. (n), parArTaM vAdI m. (n), prativAdI m. [Page039-b+ 51] (n), parArTe vAdAnuvAdakarttA m. (rttf), mantrI m. (n), mantrakft, vyavasTA- nirUpakaH, vyavahArapaRqitaH, smftiSAstrajYaH, DIsacivaH.
Barrow, s. SUkaraH. 2 unnataBUBAgaH. 3 SakawikA.
BARROW: I A vehicle: hastacAlitayAnaviSezaH. II A castrated hog: utpAwitavfzaRaH SUkaraH (?). III A mound or hillock: q. v.
BARROW , s. (A kind of vehicle) hastapracAlitaM vAhanaM or yAnaM. — (A hog) SUkaraH. — (A mound) mfttikArASiH f., unnataBUBAgaH.
Barter, s. vinimayaH, pratidAnaM, pari(rI)vartaH. v. t. vini-me 1 A, parivft c.; ‘b(arter)ed for 5 cows’ paMcagu (gfhaM &c.). v. i. BAMqavinimayena vARijyaM kf 8 U, vyavahf 1 P.
BARTER (subs.): (1) vinimayaH;(2) nimeyaH (rare);(3) nEmeyaH (rare): v. Exchange.
BARTER: (v. t.): (1) ni-mayate, vini- (me, c. 1.); (2) pari-vartayati (c. of vft) Ph.: he b. ed a book for a cloth *sa pustakaM datvA vastraM jagrAha.
BARTER (v. i.): dravyARi vinimayate na vikriRIte.
To BARTER , v. n. (To trade) BARqavinimayena bARijyaM kf.

To BARTER , v. a. (To exchange one article for another) nime (c. 1. -mayate -mAtuM), vime, vinime, BARqavinimayaM kf, parivft in caus. (-varttayati -yituM), BARqaM prati BARqaM dA (c. 3. dadAti, dAtuM); ‘capable of being bartered,’ parivarttanIyaH -yA -yaM.

BARTER , s. BARqavinimayaH, nimeyaH, nEmeyaH, vimayaH, vinimayaH, vEmeyaH, pratidAnaM, paridAnaM, parivfttiH f., parIvarttaH, parivarttaH, nimayA, vyatihAraH; ‘any thing obtained by barter,’ ApamityakaM. — (Rule of bar- ter in arithmetic) BARqapratiBARqakaH.
To BARTER , v. a. l. 3. for BARqaM prati, read BARqAt prati.
BARTON , s. (A poultry-yard) grAmakukkuwAdirakzaRArTaM vftiH.
BASALT: prastaraviSezaH.
BASALT , s. lohasadfSa atidfQaH kfzRavarRaH prastaraviSezaH.
BASALTIC , pUrvvoktaprastarasambanDI -nDinI -nDi (n).

Base, a. nIca, anArya, Kala, duzwa, kadarya, jaGanya, aDama, ni-apa-kfzwa. 2 vijAta, hInajAti, anaBijAta, akulIna. 3 kfpaRa. 4 (Notes) DIra, gaMBIra; ‘b(ase) metal’ kupyaM. s. aDoBAgaH, mUlaM, talaM, upazwaMBaH. 2 mUrDan m., BUmi f. 3 vAstu n.; powaH; ‘based on’ ex. by mUla in comp.; ‘delusion b(as)ed on ignorance’ ajYAnamUlakA BrAMtiH. [Base]ly, adv. nIcatayA, aDamaM &c. [Base]less, a. nirmUlaka, nirADAra, amUla. [Base]ness, s. aDamatA, anAryatA, nikfzwatA; akulInatA, vEjAtyaM; gAMBIryaM.

BASE (adj.): I Of mean parentage:(1) anaBijAtaH (tA, taM);(2) akulInaH (nA, naM);(3) duzkulInaH (nA, naM). A b. man:(1) prAkftaH;(2) pfTagjanaH, Ki.II A bastard: vijanman (mfn.). III Mean, disingenuous:(1) nikfzwaH (zwA, zwaM);(2) apakfzwaH (zwA, zwaM);(3) kadaryaH (ryA, ryaM);(4) jaGanyaH (nyA, nyaM);(5) pAmaraH (rA, raM).IV Of musical tones: gamBIraH (rA, raM): v. Grave, deep. V. Of metals: nikfzwaH or apakfzwaH (zwA, zwaM). Ph. b. metal kupyam.
BASE (subs.): I The bottom of any thing: aDoBAgaH: v. Foot, foundation.II In geo.: BUH or BUmiH, Li.

BASE , a. (Mean, vile) nIcaH -cA -caM, aDamaH -mA -maM, nikfzwaH -zwA -zwaM, apakfzwaH -zwA -zwaM, KalaH -lA -laM, anAryyaH -ryyA -ryyaM, nirguRaH -RA -RaM, duzwaH -zwA -zwaM, tucCaH -cCA -cCaM, jaGanyaH -nyA -nyaM, kadaryyaH -ryyA -ryyaM, hInaH -nA -naM, kutsitaH -tA -taM; ‘a base man,’ kApuruzaH. — (Of mean parentage) akulaH -lA -laM, akulInaH -nA -naM. — (Of mean spirit) kfpaRaH -RA -RaM, duzwaBAvaH -vA -vaM; ‘base metal,’ kupyaM.
BASE or BASS, a. (As sound) gamBIraH -rA -raM, DIraH -rA -raM. — (A base sound) mandraH.

BASE , s. (The bottom of any thing) aDoBAgaH, mUlaM, talaM, upazwamBaH, upAntaM. — (In geometry) mUrdDA m. (n), BUmiH f. — (Base of a pillar) upazwamBaH, stamBasya aDoBAgaH. — (Base of a tree) tarutalaM. — (Foundation of a house) BittimUlaM, powaH.
BASE , s. (In geom.) BUH f., mahI, upastamBaH.
BASE-BORN , a. vihInayoniH -niH -ni, vijAtaH -tA -taM, kaluzayonijaH -jA -jaM, hInajAtiH -tiH -ti. — (Bastard) jArajaH, kuRqaH.
BASE-MINDED , a. duzwamatiH -tiH -ti, duzwacetAH -tAH -taH (s).
BASED , p. p. (Founded) mUlaH -lA -laM in comp.; ‘based on know- ledge,’ jYAnamUlaH -lA -laM.
BASED ON (as adj.): mUlaH (lA, laM) (in comp.), b. on knowledge jYAnamUlaH (lA, laM).
BASELESS: amUlakaH (kA, kaM): v. Groundless, imaginary.
BASELESS , a. nirmmUlaH -lA -laM, amUlaH -lA -laM.
BASELY , adv. apakfzwaM, nikfzwaM, nIcatayA, sadEnyaM, duzwajanavat, aDamaprakAreRa, kArpaRyena.
BASEMENT: (1) mittimUlam;(2) vAstu (n.):(3) powaH.
BASEMENT , s. (Foundation of a house) gfhasya BittimUlaM, vAstu n., powaH.
BASENESS: I Meanness: q. v.:(1) nikfzwatA; (2) kadaryatA;(3) anAryatA.II Of birth: duzkulInatA.III Bastardy: vijanmatA.IV Of sounds: gAmmIryam. V. Of metal:(1) nikfzwatA;(2) apakfzwatA.
BASENESS , s. (Meanness) nIcatA, duzwatA, nikfzwatA, dEnyaM, kadaryyatvaM, anAryyatA, KalatA. — (Of birth) hInajAtitA, vEjAtyaM. — (Of Sound) gAmBIryyaM. — (Of metal) malaM, kupyatvaM.
BASHAW , s. tarkIyadeSe KyAtiviSezaH, senAnIH m., senApatiH m., aDipatiH m.

Bashful, a. hrImat, lajjAvat, savrIqa, trapita, salajja, SAlIna, satrapa, vinIta, BIru. [Bashful]ly, adv. salajjaM, satrapaM, savrIqaM; ‘his face b(ashfully) bent down’ lajjAvanatamuKaH, trayADomuKaH. [Bashful]ness, s. lajjA, trapA, hrIH; vrIqA, SAlInatA, vinayaH, BIrutA.
BASHFUL (adj.): (1) lajjASIlaH (lA, laM) (applied only to persons);(2) lajjAlu (mfn.);(3) lajjAvat (f. tI): v. Modest, shamefaced.
BASHFUL , a. hrImAn -matI -mat (t), lajjAvAn -vatI -vat (t), apatrapizRuH -zRuH -zRu, trapitaH -tA -taM, trapAyuktaH -ktA -ktaM, krIqitaH -tA -taM, SAlInaH -nA -naM. — (Timorous) BIruH -ruH -ru.
BASHFUL , l. 2. for krIqitaH, read vrIqitaH.
BASHFULLY: (1) salajjam;(2) savrIqam;(3) satrapam.
BASHFULLY , adv. lajjayA, satrapaM, savrIqanaM. — (Timorously) sacakitaM, saBayaM.
BASHFULNESS: (1) lajjASIlatA;(2) SAlInatA: v. Modesty.
BASHFULNESS , s. hrIH f., lajjA, trapaH -pA, apatrapA, vrIqA, vrIqanaM, SAlInatvaM, mandAkzaM. — (Timidity) BIrutA.
Basil, s. tulasI, kuWerakaH, parRAsaH.
BASIL: tulasI (the holy b.).
BASIL , s. (A plant) tulasI, maruvakaH, samIraRaH, prasTapuzpaH, PaRiJakaH, parRAsaH, jamBIraH, kaWiYjaraH, kuWerakaH, arjjakaH.
BASILICA: GarmaSAlA (?).
BASILICA , s. (The middle vein of the arm) bAhumaDyasTA vfhannAqiH f.
BASILICK , s. vfhatpUjASAlA.
BASILISK: sarpaBedaH; *takzakaH.
BASILISK , s. (A kind of serpent) cUqAyuktaH sarpaBedaH.
Basin, s. BAMqaM, droRI. 2 jalASayaH, taqAgaH, kAsAraH. 3 AlavAlaM, ADAraH, AvApaH, AvAlaM. 4 KAtaM. 5 sarittawapradeSaH, rayapaTaH.

BASIN: I A vessel for washing etc.:(1) droRI;(2) BARqam (any vessel) in a. b. of indigo nIlIBARqe, H. iii.II A reservoir:(1) jalASayaH;(2) taqAgaH;(3) kAsAraH.III A b. round the root of a tree: AlavAlam.IV dock: q. v. V. Geog. t. t.: *jalAGAraH.
BASIN , s. taqAgaH, jalASayaH, jalADAraH, KAtaM. See Bason.
Basis, s. mUlaM; yoni f.; ADAraH.
BASIS (subs.): mUlam: v. Base, foundation.

BASIS , s. (Foundation of any thing) mUlaM, aGoBAgaH, upazwamBaH, talaM. — (Basis of a pillar) stamBasya aDoBAgaH. — (The ground- work of any thing) mUlaM, vastu n., yoniH m.; ‘prosperity has virtue for its basis,’ DarmmamUlA sampattiH; ‘the basis or ma- terial of cloth,’ vastrayoniH,
Bask, v. t. sUryAtapaM ni-A-sev 1 A; ‘b(ask)s in the morning sun’ bAlAtapaM nizevate.
BASK: AtapaM sevate, A-, ni-, (sev, c. 1.), is b. ing in the morning sun bAlAtapaM sevate, v. t.
To BASK , v. n. sUryyAtapaM or sUryyatejaH sev (c. 1. sevate, sevituM), pratisUryyaM SI (c. 2. Sete, SayituM) or saMviS (c. 6. -viSati -vezwuM).
Basket, s. maMjUzA, pi(pe)wakaH, karaMqaH, kaMqolaH. [Basket]-maker, s. vERavaH, vEdalakAraH. [Basket]-work, s. vEdalaM.

BASKET: (1) pewakaH or maYjUzA (=a large b. or box for keeping clothes etc.);(2) karaRqaH (a small b. for gathering flowers etc.); (3) qallakam (=a moderate sized portable b.); (4) vidalam or vEdalam (any b. work).
BASKET , s. piwakaH, pewakaH, pewA, qalakaM, qallakaH, karaRqaH, maYjUpA, kaRqolaH; ‘basket-maker,’ vERavaH, vEdalakAraH; ‘basket-work,’ vEdalaM.
BASKING (subs.): (1) AtapasevA;(2) Atapa- nizevanam.

BASON or BASIN, s. (Reservoir) taqAgaH, jalASayaH, veSantaH, palvalaH -laM, alpasaraH n. (s), KAtaM, krIqAsaraH n. (s). — (Round the foot of a tree) AlavAlaM, AvAlaM, AvApaH. — (Vessel to hold wa- ter) droRI, pAtraM, BARqaM, jalADAraH, kAzWAmbuvAhinI. — (Harbour) KAtaM, potabanDanasTAnaM. — (Scale of a balance) tulAGawaH.
Bass, s. See Base 4. 2. kawaH; ‘b(ass) relief’ praticCAyA.
BASS: in music: gamBIraH (rA, raM): v. Base.
BASS, BAST (subs.): kawaH: v. Mat.
BASS , s. (Mat) kawaH, tfRapUlI, talAcI, pAdapASI.
BASSO-RELIEVO or BASS-RELIEF s. pratiCAyA, praticCandaH, uccEHprakAreRa takzitA citraleKA.
BASSOON: vaMSIviSezaH.
BASSOON , s. SuziraviSezaH, SuziravAdyapraBedaH.
Bastard, a., s. jAraja, kuMqa, kulawotpanna; kOlaweya, kAnIna, vijanman, dAsIputraH (trI f.), vijAta.

BASTARD: (1) jArajaH (jA, jaM) (=child of a woman by her gallant);(2) kAnInaH (nA, naM) (child of an unmarried woman); (3) kOlaweyaH (yI, yaM) or kOlaweraH (rI, raM) = (child of a lewd woman);(4) kuRqaH (a b. son born when the husband is alive);(5) golakaH (a b. son born after the death of the husband);(6) vijanman (mfn.) (not born in lawful wedlock).
BASTARD , s. jArajaH, asatIsutaH, kuRqaH -RqI m. (n), upastrIjAtaH, dAsIputraH, kOlaweraH, kOlaweyaH, banDulaH, bAnDakineyaH. — (Born after the death of a husband) golakaH.
BASTARD , a. (Illegitimate) vijanitaH -tA -taM, vijAtaH -tA -taM. — (Spurious) kftrimaH -mA -maM, kalpitaH -tA -taM.
BASTARDY: (1) jArajatvam: v. Bastard;(2) vijanmatA.
BASTARDY , s. jArajAtatA, jArajatvaM, kuRqAvasTA, upastrIjAtadaSA.
Baste, v. t. laguqena taq 10 or prahf 1 P or Ahan 2 U. 2 siv 4 P. Bastinade, s. laguqAGAtaH, gadAprahAraH, tAqanaM.
BASTE (v. t.): I To beat with a stick:(1) yazwyAGAtaM karoti;(2) laguqena tAqayati (c. of taq) : v. To beat.II To pour butter etc. over : siYcati, ni-, (sic c. 6.).

To BASTE , v. a. (To beat with a stick) laguqena or gadayA taq (c. 10. tAqayati -yituM), or prahf (c. 1. -harati -harttuM), or aBihan (c. 2. -hanti -hantuM), or tud (c. 6. tudati, tottuM). — (To sprinkle meat that is roasting) pacyamAnaM or SUlAkftaM mAMsaM Gftena sic (c. 6. siYcati, sektuM). — (To sew) sIv (c. 4. sIvyati, sevituM).
Bastile, s. prAkArayuktaM durgaM.
BASTILE , s. prAkArayuktaM kArAgAraM, durgaM, durgaparigataM pariKAprAcIrAdi.
BASTINADE (v. t.): *pAdatale laguqena tAqayati (c. of taq): v. To beat.
BASTINADE or BASTINADO, s. laguqena tAqanaM, daRqAGAtaH, gadAprahAraH.
BASTINADO (subs.): *laguqena or yazwinA pAdatalatAqanam.
BASTING , s. daRqAGAtanaM, laguqapAtanaM, gadApraharaRaM, aBiGAtaH, tAqanaM.
Bastion, s. vapraH-praM.
BASTION: no equiv.: use vapra (mn.).
BASTION , s. vapraH -praM, durgavahiHpArSve rASIkftA mfttikA or upacito vapraH.
Bat, s. jatukA, ajinapatrA, parozRI, tElapAyikA. 2 yazwi f., gadA, laguqaH.
BAT: I An animal:(1) BaNgArI,(2) carmacawI; (3) jatukA.II A club for playing: yazwiH (?)
BAT , s. jatukA, jatUkA, ajinapatrA, carmmacawakA, carmmacawI, BaNgArI. — (A club) gulikAkrIqAyAM gulikApraRodArTaM yazwiH m. or gadA or laguqaH.
BAT-FOWLER , s. rAtrikAle jatukAdivyADaH or pakzigrAhakaH.
BAT-FOWLING , s. pradozakAle or rAtrisamaye pakzigrahaRaM.
Batch, s. gaRaH, saMGaH, samUhaH.
BATCH: I Of things:(1) gaRaH;(2) saMGaH :- II Of bread: *ekakAlapakvaH sanDitApUpasaMGaH.
BATCH , s. (A number of things) gaRaH, saNGaM, saNGAtaH. — (A single baking) ApUpikaM, pEzwikaM, SAzkulikaM, yatpizwakapUpAdi ekakAle pacyate.
BATCHELOR , s. avivAhitaH, akftadAraH, akftavivAhaH.
To BATE , v. a. nyUnIkf, alpIkf, hras in caus. (hrAsayati -yituM), kan (nom. kanayati -yituM), laG (nom. laGayati -yituM), Sam in caus. (Samayati -yituM), udDAraM kf.
To BATE , v. n. kzi in pass. (kzIyate), nyUnIBU, alpIBU, hras (c. 1. hrasati, hrasituM), Sam (c. 4. SAmyati, SamituM).
BATEFUL , a. kalahakArI -riRI -ri (n), vivAdaSIlaH -lA -laM.
BATEMENT , s. nyUnIkaraRaM, alpIkaraRaM, nyUnatA, udDAraH, udDaraRaM.
Bath, s. snAnAgAraM, snAnakuMqa, avagAhanasTAnaM.
BATH: I A receptacle for bathing: *snAna- pAtram, is the b. ready *api prastutaM snAnapAtram.II Public b. s: snAnaSAlA. Ph.: to take a cold shower b. *SItalAsArodakEH snAti (snA, c. 2).
BATH , s. snAnakuRqaM, snAnAgAraM, snAnaSAlA, avagAhaH, avagAhanasTAnaM.

Bathe, v. i. snA 2 P, masj 6 P (loc.); gAh 1 A, vi-ava-gAh (with acc.). v. t. snA c. (snA-sna-payati); prakzal 10, DAv 10; aBizic 6 P, nimasj c. (majjayati). [Bath]ing, s. snAnaM, nimajjanaM, avagAhanaM, aBizekaH. a. snAnIya; ‘b(athing) cloth’ snAnIyavastraM.

BATHE (v. i.): (1) snAti (snA, c. 2.);(2) aBizekaM karoti (by pouring water);(3) majjati, ni-, (majj, c. 6.) (by plunging);(4) avagAha (gAh, c. 1.) (by immersing, diving) (with acc.), to b. in the waters payovagAQum, Ki. viii. 27.;(5) A-plavate (pla, c. 1.) (Perh. by swimming).
BATHE (v. t.): (1) snapayati (c. of snA);(2) aBi - ziYcati (sic, c. 6.) (by pouring water) (3) nimajjayati (c. of masj) (by plunging).

To BATHE , v. a. snA in caus. (snApayati -yituM), DAv (c. 1. DAvati, DAvituM or caus. DAvayati -yituM), praDAv in caus., kzal (c. 10. kzAla- yati -yituM), prakzal, nimajj in caus. (-majjayati -yituM), Aplu in caus. (-plAvayati -yituM).

To BATHE , v. n. snA (c. 2. snAti, snAtuM), nimajj (c. 6. -majjati -majjituM), avagAh (c. 1. -gAhate -gAhituM -gAQuM), Aplu (c. 1. -plavate -plotuM), aBizekaM kf. — (With one's clothes on) sacelaH snA.
BATHED , p. p. snAtaH -tA -taM, kftasnAnaH -nA -naM, avagAhitaH -tA -taM, ava- gAQaH -QA -QaM, AplutaH -tA -taM, nimagnaH -gnA -gnaM, DOtaH -tA -taM, jalaSuciH -ciH -ci.
BATHER: (1) snAtf (m.);(2) snAyin (m.).
BATHER , s. snAyI m. (n), kftasnAnaH, snAtA m. (tf), AplavakaH, nimajjanakft.
BATHING (subs.): (1) snAnam;(2) aBizekaH ; (3) majjanam, nimajjanam;(4) avagAhanam;(4) AplAvaH v. To bathe. Relating to b.: snAnIya (yA, yaM).

BATHING , s. (Act of) snAnaM, majjanaM, nimajjanaM, AplavaH, AplAvaH, ava- gAhanaM, aBizekaH. — (Religious bathing) savanaM, aBizavaH, sUtyA. — (Relating to bathing) snAnIyaH -yA -yaM. — (Bathing-gown) snAnavastraM.
Bathos, s. nIcatA. 2 gAMBIryaM.
BATHOS: *avatAraH.
BATHOS , s. vAkyAlaNkAraviSezaH, gamBIratA, gAmBIryyaM, nIcatA.
BATING , prep. varjjayitvA, varjjaM, fte, apAsya, vyatiriktaM, vyatirekeRa.
Batlet, s. rAjakaprayuktaH kAzWamudgaraH.
BATLET , s. vastraDAvane rajakEH prayuktaS catuzkoRaH kAzWamudgaraH.
BATLLE-FIELD: (1) raRaBUmiH;(2) raRANganam;(3) yudDaBUmiH;(4) praDanakzitiH.
Baton, Batoon, s. daMqaH, gadA, yazwi f., laguqaH.
BATON, BATOON (subs.): daRqaH.
BATOON , s. daRqaH, gadA, laguqaH, yazwiH m., vetraM.
Battalion, s. gulmaH-lmaM, vAhinI, sEnyadalaM.
BATTALION: *dalam. Five b. s of infantry pattInAM paYca dalAni.
BATTALION , s. vAhinI, sEnyadalaM, gulmaH, vyUhaH, senAmuKaM.

sanskrit.slp1: yaH kaScid vyayo rAjavidyAlaye antevAsinA kriyate tadgaRanApatraM
sanskrit.word: यः कश्चिद् व्ययो राजविद्यालये अन्तेवासिना क्रियते तद्गणनापत्रं
sanskrit.iast: yaḥ kaścid vyayo rājavidyālaye antevāsinā kriyate tadgaṇanāpatraṃ

details.body: BATTEL , s. yaH kaScid vyayo rAjavidyAlaye antevAsinA kriyate tadgaRanApatraM.
Batten, v. i. ApyE 1 A, sPAy 1 A; ‘the wolf b(atten)s on the lamb’ ajA (mAMsa) BakzaRenAtmAnamApyAyayati; udaraM Bf 3 U. v. t. pyE c., saMvfD c. pIna a. kf 8 U.
BATTEN (v. t.): ApyAyayati (c. of pyE): v. To fatten.

To BATTEN , v. a. (To make fat) pyE in caus. (pyAyayati -yituM), sPAy in caus. (sPAvayati -yituM), saMvfD in caus. (-varDayati -yituM), tfp in caus. (tarpayati -yituM), pInaM -nAM -naM kf. — (To fertilize) saPala (nom. saPalayati -yituM).
To BATTEN , v. n. (To grow fat) pyE (c. 1. pyAyate, pyAtuM), sPAy (c. 1. sPAyate, sPAyituM), saMvfD (c. 1. -varDate -varDituM), AtmamBariH -riH -ri or udaramBariH -riH -ri as.
Batter, v. t. mfd 9 P, cUrR 10, maMT 9 P, nizpiz 7 P, praBaMj 7 P. [Batter]y, s. mardanaM, pezaRaM. 2 kAmAnaSreRI.
BATTER (v. t.): (1) mfdrAti (mfd, c. 9);(2) maTnAti (manT, c. 9);(3) Banakti (BaYj, c. 7)
BATTER, BATSTER: in cricket: *yazwiDaraH.

To BATTER , v. a. (To shatter) mfd (c. 9. mfdnAti, marddituM) avamfd, pramfd; cUrR (c. 10. cUrRayati -yituM), pracUrR, maT (c. 9. maTnAti, manTituM or maTituM), vimaT, piz (c. 7. pinazwi, pezwuM), nizpiz, pratipiz; cUrRIkf, BaYj (c. 7. Banakti, BaMktuM), praBaYj; taq (c. 10. tAqayati -yituM), tud (c. 6. tudati, tottuM).
BATTERED , p. p. mfditaH -tA -taM, mardditaH -tA -taM, vimaTitaH -tA -taM, cUrRitaH -tA -taM, BagnaH -gnA -gnaM, tAqitaH -tA -taM, nizpizwaH -zwA -zwaM.
BATTERING-RAM: mezaH; mezAkAralOhamuKaH prAcIraBaYjakaH prAkkAlInayudDayantraviSezaH
BATTERING-RAM , s. durgaBittimarddane or nagaraprAcIraBaYjane pUrvvakAlInayoGEH prayukto mezamastakAkArAgro vfhaddaRqaH.

BATTERY: I Assault:(1) tAqanam;(2) prahAraH. II The act of battering(1) mardanam;(2) vimardanam;(3) manTanam;(4) BaYjanam.III A line of cannon: *kAmAnacakram.IV Galvanic b.: *pracalavidujjananI GawaSreRI.
BATTERY , s. (The act of battering) marddanaM, pezaRaM, BaYjanaM, AGAtanaM. — (In law) daRqapAruzpaM. — (A line of cannon) yudDayantraSreRI.

Battle, s. yudDaM, raRaH-RaM, samaraH, saMgrAmaH, saMKyaM, praDanaM, AhavaH, Aji f. samiti f., yuD f., ‘b(attle) array’ vyUhaH, sEnyavinyAsaH; ‘b(attle) axe’ paraSuH; ‘b(attle) cry’ siMhanAdaH, kzveqitaM; ‘b(attle) field’ raRa-samara- &c. BUmi f., raRAMgaRaM. v. i. yuD 4 A. [Battle]ment, s. sacCidraH prAkAraH, Bitti f.
BATTLE: (1) yudDam;(2) raRaH;(3) samaraH;(4) saMgrAmaH;(5) AhavaH;(6) AyoDanam;(7) AjiH; (8) praDanam;(9) saMyat (f.);(10) saMyugaH.

BATTLE , s. yudDaM, raRaH, raRaM, saNgrAmaH, samaraH -raM, vigrahaH, saMyugaH, AhavaH, AyoDanaM, prayudDaM, praDanaM, saMKyaM, saNgaraH, kalahaH, praGAtaH, prAGAtaH, samAGAtaH, mfDaM, samparAyaH -yakaM, sAmparAyikaM, yut f. (D), kaliH m., samprahAraH, pravi- dAraRaM, samudAyaH, samit f., samitiH, samIkaM, janyaM, saMyat f., saMsPowaH, aBisampAtaH, aByAmarddaH, aByAgamaH, AjiH f. — (Close fight) niyudDaM, bAhuyudDaM. — (Mingled fight) tumulaM, raRasaNkulaM. — (Battle-cry) siMha- nAdaH, kzveqitaM; ‘field of battle,’ raRaBUmiH f.
To BATTLE , v. n. yuD (c. 4. yuDyate, yodDuM), kalah (nom. kalahAyate); ‘to desire battle,’ yuD in des. (yuyutsate) raRakAmy (nom. raRakAmyati).
BATTLE-ARRAY: (1) vyUhaH;(2) balavinyAsaH;(3) yudDArTaM sEnyasanniveSanam; To draw up in b.;(1) vyUhate (Uh, c. 1):(2) yudDArTaM vinyasyati or viracayati.
BATTLE-ARRAY , s. sEnyavyUhaH, sEnyavinyAsaH, balavinyAsaH, vyUQiH f., yodDfSreRI.
BATTLE-AXE: (1) paraSuH;(2) paraSvaDaH. Armed with b.(1) paraSuDaraH;(2) pAraScaDika.
BATTLE-AXE , s. paraSvaDaH, paraSuH m. — (Armed with) pAraSvaDikaH.
BATTLE-CRY: (1) siMhanAdaH;(2) kzveqitam;(3) kzveqA.
BATTLE-DOOR: *kandukatAqanI.
BATTLE-FIELD , s. raRaBUmiH f., AyoDanaM, raRaH, raRANgaRaM, raRAjiraM, mallaBUH f., mallaBUmiH f., raNgaH, raNgaBUmiH f.
BATTLEDOOR , s. gulikAkrIqAyAM daRqo yaddvArA gulikA praRudyate or Ahanyate, [Page041-a+ 51] kandukapraharaRArTaM yazwiH.
BATTLEMENT: vapraviSezaH; danturavftiH.
BATTLEMENT , s. BittiH f., CidrayuktaH prAkAraH, vARAdiprakzepArTaM prAkAraCidraM.
BATTOLOGIST , s. yena nirarTakA punaruktiH kriyate saH, nirarTakavaktA m. (ktf).
BATTOLOGY , s. nirarTakA punaruktiH or muhurBAzA, nirarTakavAkyaM.
Battue, s. saMkulavaDaH-nizUdanaM.
Bauble, s. alpamUlyaM ABaraRaM, alpArDaM krIqanakaM.
BAUBLE: *sudfSyamakiYcitkaradravyam.
BAVIN , s. inDanayogyaM SuzkakAzWaKaRqaM, SuzkakAzWaM.
BAWBLE , s. alpamUlyakam ABaraRaM or kaNkaRaM, alpArGaM krIqAdravyaM, kaNkaRaM, kiNkiRI, kadarTadravyaM.
Bawd, s. kuwwinI, dUtI, SaMBalI. [Bawd]ry, s. dUtIkAryaM; kuwwinIkarman n. [Bawd]y, a. garhita, aSudDa, avinIta, nIca, ‘bawd-house’ veSyASramaH, veSaH.
BAWD: (1) kuwwinI;(2) SamBalI: v. Procuress.
BAWD , s. kuwwanI, kuwwinI dUtI, cundI, SamBalI, GawadAsI, veSyAcAryyaH m.
BAWDILY , adv. aSudDa lampawavat, vEyAtyena, gahita, garhyaprakAreRa.
BAWDINESS , s. avAcyatA, garhyatA, anakzaraM, vEyAtyaM, lampawatA.
BAWDRY: kuwwinIvyavasAyaH and sim. comp. s.
BAWDRY , s. kuwwanIkarmma n. (n), veSyAkarmma n. (n), dUtIkAryyaM.
BAWDY , a. avAcyaH -cyA -cyaM, avaktavyaH -vyA -vyaM, akaTyaH -TyA -TyaM, garhitaH -tA -taM, garhyaH -rhyA -hyaM, nIcaH -cA -caM, aDamaH -mA -maM, aSudDaH -dDA -dDaM, avinItaH -tA -taM.
BAWDY-HOUSE , s. veSyAjanasamASrayaH, veSyAgfhaM, veSyASrayaH, gaRikAgfhaM, veSaH.
Bawl, v. i. A-ut-kruS 1 P, uccEH-tArasvareRa SabdAyate (D.); rad 1 P, nad 1 P, udGuz 10. [Bawl]er, s. A-ut-kozwf m., udGozakaH. [Bawl]ing, s. utkroSaH, udGozaRaM.
BAWL (v. i.): (1) ut-kroSati (kruS, c. 1); (2) uccEH SabdAyate (nomi.);(3) rasati (ras, c. 1).

To BAWL , v. n. utkruS (c. 1. -kroSati -krozwuM), prakruS, vikruS, nad (c. 1. nadati, nadituM), praRad, vinad; udGuz (c. 10. -Gozayati -yituM), citkAraM kf; cIt SabdaM kf, ras (c. 1. rasati, rasituM).
BAWLER , s. utkrozwA m. (-zwf), vikrozwA m. (-zwf), GozakaH, udGozakaH.
BAWLING (subs.): (1) utkroSaH;(2) vikroSaH; (3) citkAraH.
BAWLING , s. vikroSanaM, utkroSanaM, GozaRaM, citkAraSabdaH, rAsaH.
Bay, a. piMga, piMgala. v. i. See Bark. s. KAtaM, vaMkaH; ‘turn to b(ay)’, ‘stand at b(ay)’ SatroraBimuKa sTA 1 P; ‘b(ay) salt’ samudralavaRaM, sEMDavaM.
BAY (adj.): piNgaH (NgA, NgaM) (?). A b. horse: ukAnahaH (very rare).
BAY (subs.): I An arm of the sea: *KAtam. II A Tree: vfkzaviSezaH.III In. pl., gar- -lands made of its branches: *jayamAlA.
