Bonnet, s. strIDftaM SirovezwanaM, SiraskaM.
BONNET: (strIlokaBftaM) Sirastram.
BONNET , s. strIlokaBftaM SiraskaM or SirastraM or SirovezwanaM or mastakABaraRaM.
BONNILASS , s. sundarI, rUpavatI, pramadA, sumuKI, mugGA, surUpI.
BONNILY , adv. hfzwavat, hfzwapuzwavat, suzWu, sundaraM, ramaRIyaprakAreRa, sADu.
Bonny, a. suMdara (rI f.); rUpavat See Beautiful. 2 hfzwa, suprIta, pramudita. 3 hfzwapuzwa, sulalita.
BONNY (adj.): sundaraH (rI, raM): v. Handsome, pretty.

BONNY , a. (Pretty) sundaraH -rI -raM, rUpavAn -vatI -vat (t), surUpaH -pI -paM, sudfSyaH -SyA -SyaM, cAruH -rvvI -ru. — (Cheerful) hfzwaH -zwA -zwaM, hfzwahfdayaH -yA -yaM. — (Plump) hfzwapuzwaH -zwA -zwaM, sulalitaH -tA -taM.
Bonton, s. vinItAcAraH, sujanatA.
Bonus, s. vetanADikaM dAnaM.
Bonvivant, s. suKEkavftti m.
BONY: (1) asTimat or asTivat (f. tI) (=having bones);(2) asTimayaH (yI, yaM) (=made of or full of bones): v. Also robust, strong.
BONY , a. (Having bones) asTimAn -matI -mat (t). — (Strong) dfQANgaH -NgI -NgaM. — (Made of bone) asTimayaH -yI -yaM. — (Full of bones) asTipUrRaH -rRA -rRaM.
Booby, s. maMdabudDiH, mUQaH, mUrKaH.
BOOBY: sTUlabudDiH: v. Blockhead, fool.
BOOBY , s. mandabudDiH m., durmatiH m., durbudDiH m., mUQaH, mUrKaH, sTUlaDIH m. — (A kind of bird) vakaH.

Book, s. pustakaM, graMTaH; ‘part of a b(ook)’ aDyAyaH, parvan n.; ‘b(ook) case’ graMTADAraH, graMTakuwA; ‘b(ook) mate’ sahADyAyin m.; ‘b(ook) worm’ graMTavAcanAsaktaH. v. t. leKye Aruh c. [Book]ish, a. pustakapaWanAllabDaH; vyavahAravisaMvAdin, avyavahArya.

BOOK (subs.): I Any literary work:(1) pustakam, a printed b. *mudritapustakam;(2) granTaH (= work: q. v.)II A division of a literary work:(1) aDyAyaH, S.:(2) parvan, (n.) (sp. of the b. s of the Mahābhārata):(3) kARqaH (sp. of the b. s of the Rāmāyaṇa;(4) sargaH (=canto), N. Ph.: account-b. gaRanApatrikA, Raj.; “I was so much in his b. s” tasyAhametAdfSa- manugrahaBAjanamAsam; without b. (=without autho- -rity) pramARaM vinA; without b. (=by memory q. v.): pustakavyatirekeRa (?).
BOOK (v. t.): patrikAyAM sanniveSayati (c. of viS) or Aropayati (c. of ruh).

BOOK , s. pustakaM -kI, granTaH, patraM, patrikA, pustaM -stI; ‘a book of science,’ SAstraM. This last may be used in connexion with some other word to limit its application; as, ‘a book on law,’ DarmmaSAstraM; ‘a poetical book,’ kAvyaSAstraM. — (A manu- script, written book) leKyaM, liKitaM.
To BOOK , v. a. granTe or pustake or leKye samAruh in caus. (-ropayati -yituM) or aBiliK (c. 6. -liKati -leKituM); ‘booked, committed to writing,’ leKyArUQaH -QA -QaM.
BOOK-CASE: *pustakarakziRI; pustakADAraH.
BOOK-KEEPER: gaRanApatrikApAlaH (?): v. Accoun- -tant.
BOOK-KEEPING: gaRanApatrikAvidyA.
BOOK-SELLER: (1) pustakavikretf (f. trI);(2) pustaka vikrayin (f. RI).
BOOK-WORM: I A person extremely fond of books: pustakacuYcuHII A worm that eats b. s: DuRaH; pustakaKAdakakIwaH.
BOOKBINDER: *pustakabanDanakArIH v. Binder.
BOOKBINDER , s. carmmAdinA granTapatrasambanDA m. (nGf), granTAcCAdanakft.
BOOKBINDING: pustakabanDanaSilpam; or sim. pustaka- banDanam.
BOOKCASE , s. granTakuwI, granTakozWaH, granTaBARqaM, granTAGAraH.
BOOKISH: (1) granTapriyaH (yA, yaM) (?);(2) pustakAsaktaH (ktA, ktaM) (?).
BOOKISH , a. granTI -nTinI -nTi (n), pustakI -kinI -ki (n), SAstrajYaH -jYA -jYaM.
BOOKKEEPER , s. gaRanADyakzaH, granTasamAropaRakft, gaRitaleKakaH.
BOOKMATE , s. sahADyAyI m. (n).
BOOKSELLER , s. granTavikretA m. (tf), granTavikrayI m. (n), pustakavikretA m. (tf).
BOOKWORM , s. granTaKAdakaH kIwaH. — (Too closely given to books) granTI m. (n), granTAsaktaH, granTaparaH, SAstragaRqaH, granTacumbakaH.
Boom, s. vAtavasanayazwi f. 2 nOkASrayadvArA-varoDakaM.
BOOM (v. i.): praDvanati (Dvan, c. l): v. To echo.
BOOM (subs.): I For extending the bottom of sails: *vAtavasanaprasAraRadaRqaHII A chain or line of spars to obstruct navigation etc.: banDaH.
BOOM , s. (A long pole) vAtavasanaprasAraRArTaM dIrDayazwiH or daRqaH. — (A bar of wood laid across a harbour) pArakyanOkApraveSanivAra- RArTaM potabanGanaKAte sTApitam avaroDakaM.
To BOOM , v. n. Urmmivat praluW (c. 1. loWati -loWituM) or ucCal (c. 1. -Calate -CalituM) or pAtotpAtaM kf.
Boon, s. varaH, prasAdaH, anugrahaH. a. hfzwa, vilAsin, udAra, pramudita. ‘b(oom) companion’, s. sahapAyin m., sahaBojin m.
BOON (subs.): I Favour, gift: q. v. anugrahaH. II A prayer, petition: q. v.: prArTanA.
BOON , s. varaH, prasAdaH, dAnaM, pradAnaM, varadAnaM, upakftaM, hitaM, anugrahaH; ‘granting boons,’ varadaH -dA -daM.
BOON , a. (Gay) hfzwaH -zwA -zwaM, hfzwahfdayaH -yA -yaM, hAsI -sinI -si (n), — (Boon-companion) sahapAyI m. (n).
Boor, s. grAmyaH janaH, grAmyikaH, vfzalaH. [Boor]ish, a. grAmya, aSizwa, asaBya.
BOOR: I A peasant, a rustic: q. v.II A rude man: avinItaH or nirmaryAdaH.
BOOR , s. grAmI m. (n), grAmyajanaH, grAmavAsI m. (n), grAmikaH, kzetrikaH, vfzalaH.
BOORISH: (1) grAmyaH (myA, myaM);(2) aSizwa; (zwA, zwaM).
BOORISH , a. grAmyaH -myA -myaM, grAmIyaH -yA -yaM, grAmikaH -kI -kaM, kzetrikaH -kI -kaM, asaByaH -ByA -ByaM, aSizwaH -zwA -zwaM, prAkftaH -tA -taM, asaNgataH -tA -taM.
BOORISHLY: grAmyajanavat: v. Also coarsely.
BOORISHLY , adv. grAmyajanavat, vfzalavat, asaByajanavat, asaByaM, aSizwaM, asaNgataprakAreRa.
BOORISHNESS: (1) grAmyatA (=rusticity);(2) aSizwatA (=coarseness: q. v.).
BOORISHNESS , s. grAmyatvaM -tA, asaByatA, aSizwatA, asaNgatiH f., vfzalatvaM.
Boot, v. t. or s. See Avail. s. upAnah f., pAdukA, pAdatraM. [Boot]less, a. nizPala, vyarTa, nirarTaka, moGa, nirguRa.
BOOT, TO: i. e. in addition: exp by the adj. atiriktaH (ktA, ktaM).
BOOT (subs.): (1) pAdukA (=shoe: q. v.);(2) unnatapAdukA (?).
BOOT , s. pAdukA f., pAdUH f., upAnat f. (h), pannadDA f., pannadDI, anupadInA, jaNGAtrARaM, pAdatraM, pAdarakzaRaM, pAdaraTaH. — (Profit) PalaM, lABaH, arTaH.
To BOOT , v. a. (To profit) PalAya or lABAya BU, PalaM or lABaM dA (c. 3. dadAti, dAtuM), upakf (c. 8. -karoti -karttuM).
To BOOT , v. n. (To put on boots) pAduke aDiruh (c. 1. -rohati -roQuM) or Aruh or pariDA (c. 3. -daDAti -Datte -DAtuM).
BOOT-TREE: pAdukAnAM carmaSiTilIkaraRAya jaMGAkftikAzWa- yantram; kAzWapAdukA.
BOOT-TREE , s. pAdukAnAM carmmaSiTilIkaraRayogyaM jaNGAkfti kAzWayantraM.
BOOTED , a. sapAdukaH -kA -kaM, upAnadgUQapAdaH -dA -daM, pAdukArUQaH -QA -QaM.
Booth, s. pawamaMqapaH, upakAryA, pawaBavanaM.
BOOTH: (1) parRaSAlA (=hut);(2) dUzyam (=tent): (3) upakAryA (rare).
BOOTH , s. maRqapaH -paM, pawamaRqapaH, dUzpaM, OpakAryyA.
BOOTJACK: *unnatapAdukAniHsAriRI.
BOOTLESS: nizPalaH (lA, laM): v. Fruitless, un- -availing.
BOOTLESS , s. nirarTakaH -kA -kaM, anarTakaH -kA -kaM, vyarTaH -rTA -rTaM, nizPalaH [Page059-a+ 51] -lA -laM, viPalaH -lA -laM, nizprayojanaH -nA -naM, anAmizaH -zA -zaM.
BOOTLESSLY: nirarTakam: v. In vain.
BOOTMAKER , s. pAdukAkAraH, pAdukAkft, pannadDAkft, pannadDAkAraH, pAdUkft m.
Booty, s. loptraM, luMWitaM, luMWanaM.
BOOTY: luRWitam or luRWitAni (n. pl.): v. Plunder.
BOOTY , s. loptraM, lotra or -taM, luptaM. — (In cattle) gograhaH.

sanskrit.iast: svamukhagopanaṃ kṛtvā paścāt santrāsanārtham akasmād bālakamukhanirīkṣaṇaṃ

details.body: BOPEEP , s. pitfputrakayoH krIqAviSezo yatra pitA bAlavinodArTaM santrasta iva svamuKagopanaM kftvA paScAt santrAsanArTam akasmAd bAlakamuKanirIkzaRaM karoti.
BORABLE , a. veDyaH -DyA -DyaM, vyaDyaH -DyA -DyaM, CidraRIyaH -yA -yaM.
BORACHIO , s. surABAjanaM, madyaBAjanaM, kutUH f. — (Drunkard) pAnarataH.
BORAGE , s. Kilaruha ozaDipraBedaH.
Borax, s. rasaSoDanaH, biqaM.
BORAX: (1) waNkanam;(2) DAtudrAvakam.
BORAX , s. rasaSoGanaH, lohadrAvI m. (n), lohaSlezaRaH, viqaM, DAtumAriRI.
BORDEL , s. veSyAjanasamASrayaH, veSyAgfhaM, gaRikAgfhaM, veSyASrayaH.

Border, s. paryaMtaH-taM, prAMtaH, parisaraBUmi f., utsaMgaH, upAMtaH. 2 (Of a garment) aMcalaH, daSA. 3 samaMtaH, sImA, sAmaMtaM. 4 tIraM, kUlaM, tawaM (of a river); ‘b(order) of a forest’ vanAMtaH. v. i. (on, upon) Ex. by vft 1 A, sTA 1 P, with (s.); janasTAnaparyaMtAni dIrGAraRyAni (U. 2) ‘large forests b(order)ing on Janasthāna’; ‘his age b(order)s on 20’ viMSativarzavayovasTAM spfSati, viMSativarzadeSIyosO. 2 kalpa, prAya, in comp.; ‘his condition b(order)s on poverty’ tasya daSA dAridryAtkiMcidUnA, dAridryakalpA. v. t. prAMtayati (D.), paryaMtaM kf 8 U; paryaMte niviS c.; ‘garment b(order)ed with silk’ nirmitakOSeyaprAMtaM vasanaM. [Border]ing, a. pratyaMta, paryaMtasTa, nikawasTa.

BORDER (subs.): (1) paryantaH, whose b. s were carved with flowers kusumalavacCuritaparyantaH (ntA, ntaM) D. ii.; from the b. of the disk of the sun paryantAdahimamayUKamaRqalasya; Ki. vii. 9.;(2) prAntaH, Ku. iii. 43.;(3) upAntaH, on whose b. yasyo- pAnte, Me. ii. 14.;(4) antaH, on the b. of a forest vanAnte. B. of a garment:(1) aYcalaH; (2) daSA.
BORDER (v. t.): paryantaM or prAntaM vidaDAti (DA, c. 2) or nirmAti (mA, c. 2) (with gen.) (?).

BORDER , s. (Of a river, &c.) tIraM, kUlaM, tawaM, kacCaH, kacCAntaH — (Edge of any thing) prAntaH, antaH -ntaM, upAntaM, samantaH, paryyantaM, sImA, utsaNgaH, DAraH. — (Frontier) samantaH, sAmantaM, paryyantaM, sImA; ‘dwelling on the border,’ sAmantavAsI -sinI -si (n), paryyantasTaH -sTA -sTaM; ‘the border of a wood,’ vanAntaM; ‘of a city,’ nagaropAntaM; ‘along the border,’ prAntatas. — (Of a garment) aYcalaH, vastrAYcalaM. — (A garden-bed) sTalaM.
To BORDER , v. a. (To surround with a border) prAnta (nom. prAntayati -yituM), samanta (nom. samantayati -yituM), paryyantaM kf.

To BORDER , UPON, v. n. prAntatas or paryyante or nikawe or samIpaM sTA (c. 1. tizWati, sTAtuM) or vft (c. 1. varttate, varttituM) or vas (c. 1. vasati, vastuM), spfS (c. 6. spfSati, sprazwuM). — (To approach nearly to, re- semble) kalpaH -lpA -lpaM as in comp., sadfSaH -SI -SaM as.
BORDER , s. kowiH f.; ‘of a garment,’ vastiH m., tarI, daSA.

BORDER ON or UPON: I Lit., expr. by the subs.: lands b. ing on the Kailāsa kElAsaparyanta- BUmayaH or kElAsaparisarAH; Bengal, on the south b. s on the sea vaNgAnAM dakziRasImA sAgaraH: v. To adjoin.II Fig.: To resemble closely: vanity b. s on insolence garvo DAzWaryAnnAtidUraH.
BORDERED , p. p. prAntitaH -tA -taM, samaryyAdaH -dA -daM, valayitaH -tA -taM.
BORDERER , s. sAmantavAsI m. (n), sImAvAsI m. (n), nikawavarttI m. (n), samIpavAsI m. (n), prativAsI -sinI -si (n).
BORDERING , a. pratyantaH -ntA -ntaM, sAmantaH -ntA -ntaM, paryyantasTaH -sTA -sTaM.
Bore, s. CidraM, raMDraM. 2 veDanI. 3 suziraM, CidravyAsaH. 4 velormi f., velAtaraMgaH. v. t. vyaT 4 P, CidraM kf 8 U. [Bor]er, s. veDakaH.
BORE (subs.): I That which bores:(1) veDanI;(2) veDanikA;(3) AviDaH.II A hole made by boring:(1) Cidram;(2) ranDram.III Calibre: q. v.IV A high tide: vAnam. v. A troublesome fellow: udvejakaH (?).
BORE (v. t.): I To perforate:(1) viDyati, A-, (vyaD, c. 4);(2) sPowayati (sPuwa, c. 10); (3) Cidrayati (Cidr, c. 10).II To vex, worry, harass: q. v.
BORE , s. (Hole made by boring) CidraM, ranDraM. — (The instrument of boring) veDanI, veDanikA. — (Diameter of a hole) suziraM, SuziraM, CidraM, vyAsaM, CidravyAsaM. — (A swelling tide) vAnaM.
To BORE , v. a. vyaD (c. 4. viDyati, vyadDuM), Cidr (c. 10. Cidrayati -yituM), SuzirIkf.
Boreal, a. udIcIna, uttara.
BOREAL , a. uttaraH -rA -raM, udaN -dIcI -dak (c), udIcInaH -nA -naM.
Boreas, s. uttaravAyuH.
BOREAS , s. uttaravAyuH m., udIcInavAtaH.
BORED , p. p. (Pierced) vidDaH -dDA -dDaM, CidritaH -tA -taM, SuziraH -rA -raM; ‘having the ears bored,’ CidrakarRaH -rRA -rRaM.
BORER , s. veDakaH, CidrakarttA. — (An instrument) veDanI, veDanikA.
BORING: (1) veDaH, b. of the ears (a religious ceremony), karRaveDaH;(2) sPowanam.
BORN: (1) jAtaH (tA, taM);(2) prasUtaH (tA, taM);(3) udBUtaH (tA, taM);(4) jaH (jA, jaM), in. comp., b. of a different father anyapitfjaH (jA, jaM), K. b.

BORN, BE: (1) jAyate (jan, c. 4), b. of the race of Manu manoH kule jAtam, Si. i. 67;(2) udBavati (BU, c. l) the child was b. of me bAlo mayyudaBUt, D. iv.;(3) sUyate, pra, (pass. of sU);(1) utpadyate (pad, c. 4) (with loc.). Ph. the son b. of a Śudra by a slave girl yaH SUdrasya suto dAsyAM Bavet, M. ix. 179.
To be BORN , v. pass. jan (c. 4. jAyate, janituM), aBijan, saYjan, utpad (c. 4. -padyate -pattuM), prasu in pass. (-sUyate), samBU (c. 1. -Bavati -BavituM).

BORN , p. p. jAtaH -tA -taM, janitaH -tA -taM, upajAtaH -tA -taM, utpannaH -nnA -nnaM, utpAditaH -tA -taM, samBUtaH -tA -taM, prasUtaH -tA -taM, praBavaH -vA -vaM, kftajanmA -nmA -nma (n), utpatitaH -tA -taM; ‘born blind,’ jAtyanDaH; ‘a born slave,’ garBadAsaH.

BORNE , p. p. soQaH -QA -QaM, UQaH -QA -QaM, kzAntaH -ntA -ntaM; ‘easy to be borne,’ susahaH -hA -haM, suvahaH -hA -haM; ‘grass borne along by the wind,’ vAtyApreritatfRaM; ‘it is borne on the shoulder,’ skanDena samuhyate
BORON: *voraRaH; DAtuviSezaH.
BOROUGH: nagaram (=town); *briwanIyamahAsaBAyAM pratiniDipreraRADikAri nagaram.
BOROUGH , s. nagaraM -rI, puraM -rI, prajApratiniDisaBAyAM sAmAjikajanaprera- RADikArayuktA nagarI.
Borrow, v. t. fRaM kf 8 U, or prArT 10 A or grah 9 P. 2 anyasmAd grah or AdA 3 A, or laB 1 A. [Borrow]er, s. fRakartf-gfhItf m., fRayAcakaH.

BORROW: I To b. money, etc.:(1) fRaM karoti (kf, c. 8), should eat ghee (even) by b. ing fRaM kftvA GftaM pibet, D. s.;(2) fRaM gfhvAti (grah, c. 9) or Adatte (dA, c. 3);(3) DAraM karoti (?).II To take from another: Ph. this sentence is b. ed from Kālidāsa *vacanamidaM kAlidAsAd gfhItam.III Assume, imitate: q. v.
To BORROW , v. a. fRaM grah (c. 9. gfhlAti, grahItuM), fRaM prArT (c. 10. -arTayate -ti -yituM), yAc (c. 1. yAcati, yAcituM), fRaM pariyAc nirUpitakAlaparyyantaM paradravyaprayogaM prArT
BORROW , s. (The thing borrowed) yAcitakaM, pratideyaM.
BORROWER: (1) fRakartA;(2) fRagrahItA;(3) fRagrAhI;(4) KAdakaH.
BORROWER , s. fRagrAhI m. (n), fRagrahaH, fRaprArTakaH, fRaprArTayitA m. (tf), yAcakaH, fRayAcakaH.
BORROWING (subs.): (1) fRagrahaH, -Ram;(2) fRakaraRam.
BORROWING , s. fRagrahaH -haRaM, fRayAcanA, yAcanA, fRaprArTanaM.
BOSKY , a. tarugulmAvftaH -tA -taM, vArkzaH -rkzI -rkzaM.
Bosom, s. vakzas n., uras n., kroqaM, vakzaHsTalaM. 2 garBaH, aByaMtaraM. 3 hfdayaM, cittaM, manas n.; ‘b(osom) friend’ hfdayaMgamaH saKA, priyasuhfd. 4 stanaH, kucaH, vakzojaH.

BOSOM (subs.): I The breast:(1) vakzas (n.), pressed (him) to his bosom nizpipeza pariraBya vakzasA. Ki. xviii. 13;(2) uram (n.), and beat her b. uro jaGAna ca, Ku. iv. 26;(3) vakzaHsTalam; (4) BujAntaram (poet).II Fig.: The heart: q. v. hfdayam, b. friend hfdayaNgamaH saKA Ku. iv. 24.III The interior: garBaH, the b. of the earth BUgarBaH.
BOSOM (v. t.): I To take to heart: hfdi DArayati (Df, c. l) or nidaDAti (DA, c. 3).II To conceal: q. v.

BOSOM , s. uraH n. (s), kroqaM -qA, aNkaH, vatsaM, vakzaH n. (s), vakzassTalaM, BujAntaraM. — (Female breast) stanaH, stanO m. du., kucaH, kucatawaM, vakzoruhaH, vakzojaM, urasijaH, urasiruhaH, stanakuwmalaM. — (The heart) hfdayaM, antaHkaraRaM, cittaM, manaH n. (s), marmma n. (n). — (A secret receptacle) garBaH.
Boss, s. gaMqaH. 2 niyAmakaH. [Boss]ed, a. gaMqAnuvidDa.
BOSS: gaRqaH (?): v. Stud, knob.
BOSS , s. gaRqaH, uccEHprakAreRa Kacita alaNkAraH, piRqaH.
BOSSED or BOSSY, a. gaRqaKacitaH -tA -taM, gaRqAnuvidDaH -dDA -dDaM.
BOTANIC, -AL: udBidvidyAvizayakaH (kA, kaM); B. garden *udBidudyAnam.
BOTANIC , BOTANICAL, a. udBidvidyAvizayaH -yA -yaM, vfkzAdividyAsambanDakaH -kA -kaM.
BOTANIST: *udBidvid (mfn.); udBidvidyAviSAradaH (dA, daM).
BOTANIST , s. udBidvidyAjYaH, vfkzAdividyAtattvajYaH, vfkzAdiSAstrapaRqitaH.
BOTANIZE: *parIkzAyE tarulatAdIn gavezayati (gavez, c. 10).

BRANDED , p. p. apamAnacihnANkitaH -tA -taM, aBiSastANkacihnitaH -tA -taM, kftANkaH -NkA -NkaM; ‘branded with infamy,’ durnAmagrastaH -stA -staM.
Brandish, v. t. pari-Bram c. (Bramayati), viDU 5, 9 U.
BRANDISH: (1) lAsayati (c. of lasa);(2) Bramayati (c. of Bram), b. ed the pikes SUlAni BramayAMcakruH. B. xiv. 9. Ph. b. ed their bows DanUMzyAsPAlitAni (after Śi.).

To BRANDISH , v. a. Bram in caus. (Bramayati or BrAmayati -yituM); ‘they brandished their pikes,’ SUlAni BramayAYcakruH; viDU (c. 5. -DUnoti -DavituM), ucCal in caus. (-CAlayati -yituM), vyAvyaD (c. 4. -viDyati -vyadDuM)
BRANDISHED , p. p. udBrAntaH -ntA -ntaM, avaDUtaH -tA -taM, ucCAlitaH -tA -taM.

sanskrit.slp1: kfmipraBedaH sa ca matsyapraloBArTaM kadAcid vaqiSe niveSyate
sanskrit.word: कृमिप्रभेदः स च मत्स्यप्रलोभार्थं कदाचिद् वडिशे निवेश्यते
sanskrit.iast: kṛmiprabhedaḥ sa ca matsyapralobhārthaṃ kadācid vaḍiśe niveśyate

details.body: BRANDLING , s. kfmipraBedaH sa ca matsyapraloBArTaM kadAcid vaqiSe niveSyate.
Brandy, s. surA, AsavaM, vAruRI, sIDu f.
BRANDY: madirAviSezaH; vAruRI.
BRANDY , s. madyaSuRqA, madyAsavaM, surA, AsavaM, SIDuH m., vAruRI.
Brangle, s. kalahaH, vyAkroSaH.
BRANGLE , s. (Squabble) vyAvakroSI, vyavakroSanaM, uccErBAzaRaM, kalahaH, vipralApaH.
BRANNY , a. tuzAkftiH -tiH -ti, tuzamayaH -yI -yaM, DAnyatvaNmayaH -yI -yaM.
BRASH (adj.): aDIraH (rA, raM): v. Impetuous.
BRASIER: A pan for coals: (1) aNgAraSakawI; (2) aNgAraDAnikA.
BRASIER or BRAZIER, s. (Worker in brass) tAmrakAraH, kAMsyakAraH, kAmanDamI m. (n). — (A pan to hold coals) aNgAraSakawI, aNgArapAtraM.
BRASIERY , s. kupyaSAlA, sanDAnI.
Brass, s. pittalaM, ArakUwaH-waM, rIti-tI f. [Brass]y, a. pittalamaya (yI f.). Efflorescence, s. rItipuzpaM, puzpaketu, puzpakaM, kusumAMjanaM. // why is this entry under 'Brass' ???
BRASS: (1) pittalam;(2) ArakUwam (rare). Oxide of b. rItipuzpam. A.
BRASS , s. rItiH f., retyaM, AraH, tAmraM, kAMsyaM -syakaM, pittalaM, pItalohaM, pItalaM -lakaM, ArakUwaH -waM. — (Impudence) nirlajjatA, DArzwyaM, pragalBatA.
BRASSY: comp. with pittala-.: v. Brazen.
BRASSY , a. rEtyaH -tyI -tyaM, kAMsyamayaH -yI -yaM, pittalaguRaviSizwaH -zwA -zwaM.
Brat, s. SiSuH, bAlaH, bawuH.
BRAT: armakaH: v. Child.
BRAT , s. SiSuH m., bAlakaH, bAlaH, putrakaH, SAvakaH.
BRAVADO , s. vikatTA, ahaNkAravAkyaM, AtmaSlADA, AhopuruzikA, ahamahamikA.

Brave, v. t. Barts 10 A, tarj 10 A. 2 Dfz 5 P; A-samA-hve 1 A. a. vIra, SUra, vikrAMta, DIra, parAkramavat, vIrya-vikrama-SAlin, sAhasika (kI f.); udAra, tejasvin ‘fortune favours the b(rave)’ sAhase SrIH prativasati. s. SUraMmanyaH. 2 samAhvAnaM. [Brave]ly, adv. saDEryaM, nirBayaM, savikramaM, SUra-vIra-vat. [Brave]ry, s. vIryaM, SOryaM, DEryaM, parA-vi-kramaH, sAhasaM. 2 (Bravado) vikatTanaM, AtmaSlAGA.

BRAVE (adj.): I Courageous:(1) sAhasikaH (kI, kaM) (=bold, daring);(2) vikrAntaH (ntA, ntaM) (=valorous);(3) nirBayaH (yA, yaM) (=fear- -less);(4) tejasvin (f. nI) (=spirited). Ab. man: i. e. a hero:(1) vIraH;(2) SUraH Ph.: fortune favours the b. sAhase SrIH prativasati. Mr. iv.II Excellent, noble, grand: q. v.

BRAVE , a. SUraH -rA -raM, vIraH -rA -raM, pravIraH -rA -raM, parAkrAntaH -ntA -ntaM, vikrAntaH -ntA -ntaM, nirBayaH -yA -yaM, DfzwaH -zwA -zwaM, sAhasikaH -kI -kaM, udDataH -tA -taM. — (Excellent) sADuH -DuH -Du, uttamaH -mA -maM, praSastaH -stA -staM. — (Noble) udAraH -rA -raM.
BRAVE , s. (A bully) SUrammanyaH, damBI m. (n). — (Defiance) samAhvAnaM, krandanaM, AsyardDA.

To BRAVE , v. a. (To menace) Barts (c. 10. Bartsayate -yituM), aBiBarts, avaBarts, pariBarts, tarj (c. 1. tarjati, tarjituM). — (To challenge) Ahve (c. 1. -hvayate -hvAtuM), samAhve, krandanaM kf, sparD (c. 1. sparDate, sparDituM).
To BRAVE , v. n. (To carry a boasting appearance) dAmBikavad vft (c. 1. varttate, varttituM) or car (c. 1. carati, carituM), Gfz (c. 5. GfzRoti, DarzituM), dfp (c. 4. dfpyati, draptuM).
BRAVED , p. p. (Challenged) AhUtaH -tA -taM, samAhUtaH -tA -taM.
BRAVELY: (1) nirBayam v. Fearlessly;(2) kfta- sattvavegaH (gA, gaM), Ki. xvii. 15.;(3) saDEryam (=with fortitude).
BRAVELY , adv. (In a brave manner) savIryyaM, SUravat, vIravat, aBItavat, saparAkramaM, SOryyeRa, nirBayaM, prasaBaM. — (Excellently) sAGu, praSastaM, su prefixed.
BRAVERY: I Courage:(1) SOryam;(2) sAhasam (=boldness);(3) vikramaH (=valour)(4) nirBIkatA (fearlessnesfearlessness).II Splendour, magnificence: q. v.

BRAVERY , s. SUratA, SOryyaM, vIratA, vIryyaM, parAkramaH, vikramaH, kArpaRyarAhityaM; ‘to show bravery in battle,’ parAkram (c. 1. -kramati -kramituM), vikram. — (Bravado, boast) vikatTA, AspardDA. — (Magnificence) pratApaH, tejaH n. (s).
BRAVINGLY , adv. dAmBikavat, sadamBaM, AhvAnapUrvvakaM, samAhvAnakrameRa.
Bravo, interj. sADu, sADu sADu. s. GAtakaH, AtatAyin m.
BRAVO: I Interjec.: sADu. or sADu sADu.II Subs.: v. Assassin.
BRAVO , interj. sAGu. — (A murderer) GAtakaH, dasyuH m., AtatAyI m. (n).
Brawl, s. kaliH, kalahaH, vivAdaH, dvaMdvaM, vipratipatti f. v. i. vivad 1 A, kalahaM kf 8 U, kalahAyate (D.).
BRAWL (v. i.): vyAkroSati (kruS, c. l.): v. To wrangle, quarrel.
BRAWL, BRAWLING (subs.): vyAkroSaH. v. Wrangling, quarrel.
To BRAWL , v. n. vyavakruS (c. 1. -kroSati -krozwuM), kalaha (nom. kalahAyate -yituM), vEra (nom. vErAyate -yituM), vivad (c. 1. -vadati -vadituM), vipralap (c. 1. -lapati -lapituM).
BRAWL , s. kalahaH, vyavakroSaH, vyAvakroSI, AkroSaH, uccErBAzaRaM, uccErGuzwaM, vyAvaBAzI, vivAdaH, vAgyudvaM, vipralApaH, dvandvaM, saMrAvaH.
BRAWLER , s. kalahakAraH -rI m. (n), kalahapriyaH, viroDI m. (n), kalipriyaH, yuyutsuH m.
BRAWLING (adj.): kalahapriyaH (yA, yaM): Quarrel- -some, noisy.
Brawn, s. SUkaramAMsaM. 2 snAyuH; bAhuH. [Brawn]y, a. mAMsala; dfQAMga (gI f.); saMnadDaSarIra.
BRAWN: I The flesh of a boar:(1) SUkara- mAMsam;(2) vallUram.II Muscle, strength: q. v.
BRAWN , s. (The flesh of a boar) SUkaramAMsaM. — (The musculous part of the body) snAyuH f., snasA. — (The arm) bAhuH m. — (A boar) SUkaraH, varAhaH.
BRAWNINESS , s. mAMsalatvaM, dfQANgatA, SarIradfQatA, draQimA m. (n).
BRAWNY: mAMsalaH (lA, laM): v. Muscular, strong.
BRAWNY , a. mAMsalaH -lA -laM, snAyumAn -matI -mat (t), dfQANgaH -NgI -NgaM.
Bray, v. t. cItkAraSabdaM kf 8 U, Araw 1 P. v. t. cUrR 10, piz 7 P. [Bray]ing, s. cI(ci)tkAraH, KaranAdaH.
BRAY (v.): I To pound: q. v.: pinazwi (piz, c. 7.).II To utter a harsh cry:(1) citkAraM karoti (kf, c. 8.);(2) virOti (ru, c. 2.).
BRAY, BRAYING (subs.): (1) citkAraH;(2) KaranAdaH (=b. of an ass): v. Noise.
To BRAY , v. a. (To pound) cUrR (c. 10. cUrRayati -yituM), pracUrR, vicUrR, piz (c. 7. pinazwi, pezwuM), nizpiz, vinizpiz, utpiz.
To BRAY , v. n. (Like an ass) garddaBavad ru (c. 2. rOti, ravituM) or citkAraM kf or nad (c. 1. nadati, nadituM).
BRAY , s. KaranAdaH, garddaBanAdaH, garddaBarAvaH, citkAraH, KaraSabdaH, nAdaH.
BRAYER , s. (One that brays like an ass) KaranAdI m. (n), nAdI m. (n), citkArakft. — (One that pounds) cUrRakaH, nizpezwA m. (zwf), peSvaraH.
BRAYING (subs.): i. e. pounding; q. v.: pezaRam.
Braze, v. t. pittalena saMDA 3 U. [Braz]en, a. pittalamaya (yI f.). 2 nirlajja, Dfzwa, nistrapAvaraRa. v. t. Dfz 5 P. [Braz]ier, s. tAmra-kAMsya-kAraH, kAmaMDamin m. 3 aMgArapAtraM.
BRAZEN: I Made of brass:(1) pittalamayaH (yI, yaM);(2) by comp., b. vessel pittalapAtram.II Shameless, impudent; q. v. nirlajjaH (jjA, jjaM).
To BRAZEN , v. n. Dfz (c. 5. GfzRoti, DarzituM), aBiBarts (c. 10. -Bartsayate -yituM).
BRAZEN , a. rEtyaH -tyI -tyaM, pittalamayaH -yI -yaM, tAmrikaH -kI -kaM. — (Impudent) nirlajjaH -jjA -jjaM, DfzwaH -zwA -zwaM.
BRAZEN-FACED , a. nirlajjamuKaH -KI -KaM, lajjAhInaH -nA -naM, svalpavrIqaH -qA -qaM.
BRAZENNESS , s. rEtyatvaM. — (Impudence) nirlajjatA, DfzwatA, pragalBatA.
BRAZIER: kAMsyakAraH.
BRAZIER , s. tAmrakAraH, kAMsyakAraH. See BRASIER.
BRAZIL-NUT: PalaviSezaH:
BRAZIL-WOOD: raNgado raktavarRakAzWaviSezaH.
Breach, s. CidraM, raMDraM. 2 BaMgaH, BedanaM; atikramaH, laMGanaM; ‘b(reach) of promise’ pratijYABaMgaH; AjYABaMgaH. 3 BedaH (suhfdBedaH); ‘b(reach) in a wall’ saMDiH, suraMgA.

BREACH: I Fracture: q. v.II A gap made by breaking:(1) Cidram;(2) ranDramIII Vio- -lation: q. v.: Ph. b. of peace SAntiBaNgaH (?); b. of promise pratijYABaNgaH; b. of agreement samaya- BedaH; b. of faith viSvAsaGAtaH.IV. B. of union: BedaH; a b. between friends suhfdBedaH.

BREACH , s. BaNgaH, BedaH, CedaH, KaRqaM, ranDraM, CidraM. — (The act of break- ing) BaYjanaM, BedanaM, KaRqanaM. — (A gap in a wall) sanDiH m., gfharanDraM, KAnikaM, suruNgA, kuqyacCedaH. — (Violation) atikramaH, laNGanaM, ullaNGanaM. — (Violation of a law) vyavasTAtikramaH, vyavasTAlaNGanaM. — (Breach of promise) pratijYABaNgaH. — (Breach of confidence) viSvAsaBaNgaH. — (Separation of friendship) suhfdBedaH, viroDaH, vicCedaH.
Bread, s. apUpaH, pizwakaH, kAMdavaM. 2 annaM, AhAraH.
BREAD: I Lit.: rowI, Bha. Unleavened b. apUpaH.II Sustenance, living: q. v.: annaM or annajalam (=b. and water).
BREAD , s. apUpaH, pUpaH, pizwakaH, kAndavaM, aByuzaH. — (Food in general) annaM, AhAraH, BojanaM.
BREAD , s. upajIvyaM; ‘bread and water,’ annajalaM, annodakaM.
BREAD-CORN: rowIkaraRopayogigoDUmAdiSasyam.
BREAD-CORN , s. goDUmaH, sumanAH m. (s), sumanaH, SasyaM, DAnyaM, ApupyaM
BREAD-FRUIT: (1) kaRwa- or kaRwaka- or kaRwakiPalam; (2) panasaM or panasaPalam.
BREAD-FRUIT , s. panasaH, panasanAlikA, kaRwakiPalaH, kaRwakaPalaH.
BREAD-FRUIT-TREE: (1) panasaH;(2) kaRwaki (kI)- -PalaH;(3) kaRwakaPalaH.
BREAD-ROOT: pAlaNgAkAraH SAkaBedaH.

BREADTH: I Width:(1) vistAraH;(2) parisaraH; (3) prasTaH;(4) AyAmaH (rare);(5) pariRAhaH; (6) vizkamBaH (rare). Ph.: two fingers in b. dvyaNgulaH (lA, laM); (the doors) should be made two cubits in b. tAni dvihastavistftAni kAryARi.II In painting: b. of effect: vistAraH (?).
BREADTH , s. pfTutA, pArTavaM, praTimA m. (n), viSAlatA, vipulatA, vistAraH, vistIrRatA, parisaraH, prasTaH, vitatiH f., AyAmaH, AyatanaM, pAwaH.

Break, v. t. BaMj 7 P (fig. also), KaMq 10. 2 kzud-piz 7 P, cUrR 10, mfd 9 P. 3 atikram 1 U, 4 P, ullaMG 1 A, 10, aticar 1 P; vilup c. 4 Bid 7 U, viGaw c. (Gawayati); vidF 9 P, 10, sPuw c. (as heart); ‘b(reak) fast’ pAraRAM nirvft c., prAtarASaM-kalyavartaM sev 1 A; ‘b(reak) wind’ gudaravaM kf 8 U, pard 1 A; ‘b(reak) the way for’ apasf 1 P, apa-i 2 P, apakram. 5 vinaS c., ucCid 7 P. v. i. Bid-dF-BaMj- pass., truw 6, 4 P, sPuw 6 P, (sPuwati hfdayaM), dal 1 P. 2 praBA 2 P; ‘the day broke’ uzAH samAGatA, praBAtA rajanI, dfzwaM dinamuKaM. 3 kzi pass., avasad 1 P, viSF pass., DvaMs 1 A, jf 4, 9 P. s. vicCedaH, nivftti f., virAmaH, BaMgaH; ‘b(reak) of day’ praBAtaM, uzaHkAlaH, aruRodayaH; ‘the story has suffered a b(reak)’ vicCedamApa kaTAprabaMDaH (Ka. 239). [Break] down, cUrR 10; (v. i.) See Fail. [Break] in upon, prasahya-sahasA-praviS 6 P. [Break] into, vinI 1 P, dam c. (damayati). [Break] into (a house), saMDiM kftvA praviS. [Break] loose, pramuc, vimuc pass.; ‘the elephant broke loose from the post’ AlAnastaMBaM BaMktvA nirjagAma. [Break] off, BaMj, BaMgaM kf 8 U; (v. i.) akasmAt viram 1 P, tyaj 1 P, nivft 1 A. [Break] open, balAt-sahasA-udGaw c. or apavf 5 U. [Break] out, (v. i.) udDa 1 P, utpad 4 A, prAdurBU, udi 2 P. 2 nirgam 1 P. [Break]-through, nirBaMj, apAnud 6 P, niras 4 P; See Dispel. [Break]-up, (v. t.) See Break (v. i.) ‘the party broke up’ saByAH svaM svaM sTAnaM pratijagmuH. [Break] upon, Ahan 2 A; ‘the dawn broke upon his eyes’ tasyAkzRoH praBAtamAsIt (S. 2). [Break] with, vivad 1 A, kalahaM kf. [Break]er, s. BaMjakaH, BedakaH. 2 prastara or tawa-BagnA Urmi f., lahari f. [Break]fast, s. prAtarASaH, kalyavartaH. [Break]-water, s. setuH, DaraRaH.

BREAK (v. t.): I Lit.:(1) Banakti (BaYj, c. 7.), the flag-staff is broken BagnaH syandanaketuH, Ve. ii.; (2) cUrRayati, saM-, (cUrR, c. 10.) (=reduce to powder), shall I not b. Suyodhana's thighs with my mace saMcUrRayAmi gadayA na suyoDanorU, Ve. ii. To weaken or subdue: q. v.: Banakti.III To make bankrupt: avasAdayati (c. of sad) (?). Miscell.: but do not b. my meditation mA punaH samADiM BaMkzyasi, V. ii.; b. ing his silence mOnaBaNgaM viDAyAsya, Vet.; to b. one's sleep nidrABaNga karoti, Si.; to b. an agreement samayaM Binatti (Bid, c. 7.), M. v. To violate; I will b. all order Banajmi sarvamaryAdAH, B. vi. 38.; to “b. one's mind” hfdayaM vivfRoti (vf, c. 5.), Ki. v. To open; to b. horse etc.: v. To break in; to b. wind pardate (pard, c. l.); I will b. their union tAn viGawayAmi (Gaw, c. 10.) (the time) has come (for) b. ing my fast by (sucking) blood upasTitA SoRitapAraRA me, R. ii. 39.; to b. ground mfttikAm uttolayati (tul, c. 10.) (?); to b. one's heart hfdayaM vidArayati (c. of df), U.

BREAK (v. i.): I Lit.:(1) Bajyate (pass. of BaYj) or more commonly BagnaH (gnA, gnaM) Bavati (BU, c. l.);(2) truwyati (truw, c. 4.). Fig. my heart is b. ing sPuwati hfdayam, U.; v. To rend. II To become bankrupt: avasIdati (sad, c. l.) (?).III To dawn: Ph. the day has nearly broken praBAtaprAyA rajanI, Sa. iv.IV To decline in health; Ph. you are b. ing every day anudivasaM parihIyase'Ngezu, Sa. iii. V. To burst: q. v.VI To fall out: Ph. their union broke BedastezAmajani.
BREAK (subs.): I An interruption:(1) vicCedaH;(2) CedaH.II An opening made by fracture: BaNgaH.III. B. of day: v. Dawn.

To BREAK , v. a. (Burst or part asunder by force) BaYj (c. 7. Banakti, BaMktuM), niBaYj, vinirBaYj, praBaYj; Bid (c. 7. Binatti, BettuM), KaRq (c. 10. KaRqayati -yituM), pariKaRq, vidF in caus. (-dArayati -yituM), sPuw (c. 10. sPowayati -yituM), ruja (c. 6. rujati, roktuM), avaruj, Aruj, [Page063-a+ 51] samAruj; kzud (c. 7. kzuRatti, kzottuM), prakzud; SakalIkf, dal in caus. (dAlayati -yituM), vidal. — (Penetrate, break through) vyaD (c. 4. viDyati, vyadDuM), nirBid, Cidr (c. 10. Cidrayati -yituM). — (Crush) mfd (c. 9. mfdnAti, marddituM), piz (c. 7. pinazwi, pezwuM). — (Break or sink the spirit) mano KaRq or han (c. 2. hanti, hantuM) or pratihan, BagnASaM -SAM -SaM kf, ASAviBinnaM -nnAM -nnaM kf, KaRqitASaMsaM -sAM -saM kf. — (Tame) dam in caus. (damayati -yituM or c. 4. dAmyati, damituM), pradam; vinI (c. 1. -nayati -netuM). — (Make bankrupt) parikzIRaM -RAM -RaM kf, nirDa- nIkf. — (Overcome) parAji (c. 1. -jayati -te -jetuM). — (Break down, destroy) avaBaYj, praBaYj, vinaS in caus. (-nASayati -yituM), ucCid (c. 7. -Cinatti -CettuM). — (Violate a promise) saMvidaM vyatikram (c. 1. -krAmati -kramituM), visaMvad (c. 1. -vadati -vadituM), visaMvid (c. 2. -vetti -vedituM). — (Infringe a law) vyavasTAm atikram or vyatikram or laNG (c. 1. laNGate, laNGituM, c. 10. laNGayati -yituM), ullaNG, vilaNG, or aticar (c. 1. -carati -carituM) or lup in caus. (lopayati -yituM). — (Break a vow) vrataM lup in caus. — (Interrupt) lup, vilup, vipralup in caus., ucCid, vicCid, pratihan, antari (c. 2. -eti -etuM). — (Break intelligence) praTamasaMvAdaM kf, praTamAKyAnaM kf. — (Break the heart) daladDfdayaM -yAM -yaM kf, BagnAntaHkaraRaM -RAM -RaM kf. — (Break into a house) sanDiM kf, kuqyaM Cid. — (Break a bone) asTi BaYj or Bid. — (Make to cease) nivft in caus. (-varttayati -yituM). — (Separate) viyuj (c. 7. -yunakti -yuMkte -yoktuM). — (Break off, re- linquish) tyaj (c. 1. tyajati, tyaktuM). — (Reform a bad habit) dozaKaRqanaM kf. — (Dissolve friendship) sOhfdyaM Bid. — (Break one's sleep) nidrAM BaYj, nidrABaNgaM kf. — (Break one's fast) pAraRaM kf, prAtarBojanaM kf, upavAsAnantaraM praTamAhAraM kf. — (Break wind) pard (c. 1. pardate, pardituM), gudaravaM kf.

To BREAK , v. n. (Part in two) BaYj in pass. (Bajyate), Bid in pass. (Bidyate), viBid, vicCid in pass. (-Cidyate), truw (c. 4. truwyati, truwituM), vidF in pass. (-dIryyate), sPuw (c. 6. sPuwati, sPuwituM), SakalIBU. — (Dawn) praBA (c. 2. -BAti -BAtuM), uz (c. 1. ozati, ozituM or ucCati, ucCituM), vyuz, samuz. — (Open as a sore) pUy (c. 1. pUyate, pUyituM), pUyanaM kf, pakvaH -kvA -kvaM BU. — (Become bankrupt) parikzIRaH -RA -RaM BU. — (Decline, decay) jF (c. 4. jIryyati, jarituM, jarItuM), kzi in pass. BREWER , s. yavasurakvaTitA m. (tf), yavasurapAcakaH.

BREWHOUSE or BREWERY: *yavasurapAcakasTalI; yavasurapAkaSAlA.
BREWING (subs.): *yavasurapAkaH.
BREWING , s. yavasurapacanaM, yatkiYcid yavasuram ekakAle pacyate.
BREWIS , s. yUzakvaTitaH pizwakaH or apUpaH.
Briar, Brier, s. gokzuraH, kaMwakagulmaH. [Briar]y, a. kaMwakAvfta.
Bribe, s. utkocaH, upAyana. v. t. utkocaM dA 3 U, utkocadAnena vaSIkf 8 U. [Bribe]ry, s. utkocadAnaM-grahaRaM. 2 utkocadAnAdAnAparADaH.

BRIBE (subs.): utkocaH, taking b. s even from the ministers sacivamaRqalAdapyutkocagrAhI, D.; not corruptible by b. etc. DanadAnAdinABedyaH, K. b. one who receives b. (1) utkocakaH (rare);(2) utkocagrAhakaH.
BRIBE (v. t.): utkocaM dadAti (dA, c. 3.) Ph. the judge has been b. d utkocadAnena vaSIkfto vicArakaH.
BRIBE , s. utkocaH -cA -cakaH, upapradAnaM, upAyanaM, aByupAyanaM, koSalikaM, pAritozikaM; ‘the receiver of a bribe,’ utkocakaH, utkocAdAtA m. (tf), utkocagrAhakaH.
To BRIBE , v. a. utkocaM dA (c. 3. dadAti, dAtuM) or upapradA, anyAyyaka- rmmasampAdanArTam upAyanaM dA.
BRIBE , s. avadAnaM, yogadAnaM, AmizaM. BRIDGE, s. (Of mus. inst.) kakuBaH.
BRIBER: utkocadAtA (=one who gives bribe).
BRIBER , s. utkocadAtA m. (tf), utkocadAyI m. (n), upapradAtA m. (tf),
BRIBERY: (1) utkocadAnam (giving bribe):(2) utkocagrahaRam (taking b.).
BRIBERY , s. utkocasya dAnAdAnAparADaH. — (Giving bribes) utkocadAnaM, utkocacaryyA. — (Receiving bribes) utkocagraha -haRaM.
Brick, s. izwakA, suDA; ‘burnt b(rick)’ pakvezwakA; ‘b(rick) bit’ izwakASakalaM; ‘b(rick) kiln’ ApAkaH, pacanasTAnaM; ‘b(rick) layer’ lepakaH, suDAjIvin m.; ‘b(rick) work’ izwakAnirmitaM.
BRICK (subs.): izwakA, baked b. pakvezwakA; unbaked b. ABezwakA, Mr. A b. house izwakAgfham; a pile of b. s izwakArASiH.
BRICK , s. izwakA, izwikA, suDA; ‘burnt brick,’ pakvezwakA, JAmakaM; ‘a brick-house,’ izwakAgfhaM, suDABavanaM; ‘brick-built,’ izwakAni- rmmitaH -tA -taM; ‘a pile of bricks,’ izwakArASiH f.
To BRICK , v. a. izwakAnyAsaM kf, izwakAnyAsaM kftvA nirmmA (c. 2. -mAti -mAtuM).
BRICK-BAT , s. izwakASakalaM, izwakAKaRqaM, BinnezwakA, BagnezwakASakalaM.
BRICK-DUST , s. izwakAcUrRaM, izwakAkzodaH, izwakAkzoditaM.
BRICK-KILN: izwakApAkaH (?): v. Kiln.
BRICK-KILN , s. pAkapuwI, ApAkaH, izwakApacanasTAnaM, pavanaM.
BRICK-WORK: izwakABirnirmitaH (tA, taM); these are b. s etAnIzwakABirnirmitAni.
BRICKBAT: (1) izwakAKaRqam (?);(2) izwakA- Sakalam (?).
BRICKLAYER: (1) lepakaH;(2) palagaRqaH: v. Mason.
BRICKLAYER , s. lepakaH, lepI m. (n), lepyakft m., pralepakaH, suDAjIvI m. (n), awwAlikAkAraH, palagaRqaH.
BRICKMAKER: (1) izwakApAcakaH (?);(2) izwakA- kAraH (?).
BRICKMAKER , s. izwakAkArI m. (n), izwakAkft, izwakAkAraH, suDAkft.
BRICKWORK , s. izwakAnyAsaH, suDAnyAsaH, izwakAnirmmARaM, izwakAnirmmitaM yatkiYcid BavanAdi.
Bridal, s. vivAhotsavaH, udvAhakarman n. a. vEvAhika (kA f.), vivAhayogya.
BRIDAL (subs.): vivAhotsavaH: v. Marriage.
BRIDAL (adj.): vEvAhikaH (kI, kaM). B. procession (of the bridegroom) varayAtrA N. xvi. 4.; b. string kOtukam; b. chamber kOtukAgAram. Ku.
BRIDAL , s. vivAhotsavaH, vivAhaparvva n. (n), vivAhaH, vivAhakarmma n. (n) or udvAhakarmma.
BRIDAL , a. vEvAhikaH -kI -kaM, udvAhikaH -kA -kaM, vivAhayogyaH -gyA -gyaM, pARigrahaRikaH -kI -kaM; ‘bridal clothes,’ AnandapawaM.
Bride, s. vaDUH, navavaDU; pARigfhItA, navoQA. 2 kanyA, kumArI. [Bride]groom, s. varaH, pariRetf m., parigrahItf m., pARigrAhakaH; ‘bride and b(ridegroom)’ vaDUvara-rO. [Bride]maid, s. janyA.

BRIDE: (1) vaDUH; the b. and the bridegroom vaDUvaram, Ku. vii. 78.;(2) navavaDaH;(3) navoQA (=just married);(4) AsannapARigrahaRA (=about to marry). A young b.:(1) kanyA;(2) kumArI, R. vii. 22. A b. who chooses her own husband: svayaMvarA.
BRIDE , s. navoQA, navaBAryyA, navavaDUH f., navapatnI, UQA, navakArikA, navavarikA, pARigfhItA, suvAsinI; ‘one who chooses her own husband,’ svayaMvarA.
BRIDE-BED , s. vivAhaSayyA, navoQASayanaM, AnandaSayyA, UQAvoQror navaSayanaM.
BRIDE-CAKE , s. vivAhotsavakAle gfhAByAgatEH svAdanIyaH pizwakaH or apUpaH, AnandapizwakaH.
BRIDE-MAID: janyA.
BRIDEGROOM: varaH.
BRIDEGROOM , s. varaH, voQA m. (-Qf), pariRetA m. (tf), pARigrAhaH, vivAhodyataH.
BRIDEMAID , s. (Attendant on the bride) janyA.
BRIDEMAN , s. (Attendant on the bridegroom) janyaH.
BRIDESMAN: janyaH; varasya vaDvASca sahacaraH.
BRIDEWELL: kArAgAram: v. Prison.
BRIDEWELL , s. nigrahagfhaM, nigrahAgAraM, daRqapraRayanagfhaM, kArAgAraM, kArA- veSma n. (n).

Bridge, s. setuH, DaraRaM, saMvaraH. 2 Ali-lI f., DaraRaH (small); ‘make a b(ridge)’ setuM nirmA 3 A, or kf 8 U, or baMD 9 P; ‘fort b(ridge)’ sakramaH; ‘b(ridge) of the nose’ nAsAvaMSaH. v. t. setunA baD 9 P, savf 5 U.

BRIDGE (subs.): (1) setuH, stone b. pApARasetuH, Raj.; to make a b. setuM baDnAti R. or karoti, Mah. or nirmAti, Vi, or vidaDAti, Ma. n. (with loc. or gen. and upari);(2) saNkramaH (=foot -b.);(3) saMvaraH (rare). B. of the nose nAsAvaMSaH.
BRIDGE (v. t.): setunA baDnAti, ni-, (banD, c. 9.), Mah.; b. d the Padmā, with boats: nOBiH padmAM babanDa.

BRIDGE , s. setuH m., piRqalaH, piRqilaH, DaraRaH, saMvaraH, sambaraH. — (Foot- bridge) saNkamaH. — (A bridge of boats) nOsetuH m. — (Of the nose) nAsAvaMSaH. — (Of a musical instrument) tantrAlambaH, tantraDAraRArTaM kAzWaKaRqaM.
To BRIDGE , v. a. (Connect by a bridge) setunA banD (c. 9. baDnAti, bandDuM).

Bridle, s. valgA; raSmiH; ‘giving the b(ridle) to the passions’ rAgADInaH, rAgavaSaH. 2 nigrahaH, saMyamaH. v. t. valgAsanATa a. kf, raSmiBiH yam 1 P. 2 nigrah 9 P, ni-saM-yam; See Control, ‘by un-b(ridl)ed tongue’ niryaMtraRayA vAcA.
BRIDLE (subs.): I Lit.: valgA: v. Bit, reins. II Fig.: v. Restraint, check.
BRIDLE (v. t.): I Lit.: Perh. valgitaH (tA, taM) karoti v. To bit, rein.II Fig.: To restrain, check: q. v.: niyantrayati (yantr, c. 10.).
BRIDLE , s. vAgA, raSmiH m., valgA, dantAlikA. — (Restraint) saMyamaH, yamaH, yantraRaM, nigrahaH.
To BRIDLE , v. a. raSmiBir yam (c. 1. yacCati, yantuM). — (To restrain) yam, niyam, saMyam, nigrah (c. 9. -gfhlAti -grahItuM), vaSIkf.
BRIDLEHAND , s. aSvArUQasya yo hasto vAgAM saNgfhlAti or Darati.

Brief, a. svalpa, acira, alpakAla, kzaRika (kI f.), acirasTAyin, saMkzipta, parimita, sahfta, adIrGaM, saMkucita; ‘to be b(rief)’ kiM bahunA. 2 saMgrahaH, saMkzepaH. 3 sArapatraM. [Brief]ly, adv. saMkzepataH, saMkzepeRa, samAsataH, samAsena. 2 acireRa, ASu, kzipraM. [Brief]ness, s. saMkzepaH, samAsaH, saMhAraH, parimitatA.

BRIEF (adj.): I Compressed, terse: v.: saMkziptaH (ptA, ptaM). To be b. (when=b. ly): kiM bahunA.II Lasting but little time: kzaRikaH (kA, kaM), b. enjoyment kzaRikA prItiH H.;(2) acirasTAyin (f. nI): v. Temporary.III Short: q. v.
BRIEF (subs.): I An epitome: q. v.II A dispatch: q. v.III An abridgment of a client's case: *vivAdatattvam.

BRIEF , a. (Concise) saNkziptaH -ptA -ptaM, sANkzepikaH -kI -kaM, sAmAsikaH -kI -kaM, parimitaH -tA -taM, saNgfhItaH -tA -taM. — (Not long, as time, &c.) aciraH -rA -raM, alpaH -lpA -lpaM, alpakAlaH -lA -laM. — (Contracted) saNkucitaH -tA -taM, saMhftaH -tA -taM, hrasvaH -svA -svaM; ‘in a brief space of time,’ acireRa, acirAt, na cireRa; ‘for a brief space,’ alpamAtraM.
BRIEF , s. (Writing of any kind) patraM. — (An epitome) saNgrahaH, saNkzepaH, saMhAraH. — (A writ) AjYApatraM. — (A writing explaining the case) nivedanapatraM, arTatattvajYApakaM patraM.
BRIEFLESS: Ph. he is a b. barrister *taM vyavahAra- paRqitaM kAryopadeSArTamarTipratyarTino nASrayante; vivAdatatrva- hIno vyavahArapaRqitaH.
BRIEFLY: (1) saMkzepeRa;(2) saMkzepataH;(3) samAsataH.
BRIEFLY , adv. (Concisely) saNkzepeRa, saNkzepAt, saNkzepatas, samAsatas, avistaraSas, na vistareRa, parimitaprakAreRa. — (Quickly) acireRa, kzipraM, ASu, avilambitaM.
BRIEFNESS , s. saNkziptiH f., saNkziptatvaM, saNkzepaH, upasaNkzepaH, samastatvaM, samAsaH, samasanaM, saMhAraH, parimitatA, alpatvaM -tA. — (Of life) AyuralpatvaM.
BRIER or BRIAR, s. gokzuraH, kaRwakagulmaH, SfgAlakaRwakaH, SfgAlakoliH m.
BRIER or BRIAR: kaRwakigulmaviSezaH; also = kaRwaki- gulmaH.
BRIERY , a. kaRwakI -kinI -ki (n), kaRwakitaH -tA -taM, SfgAlakaRwa- kAvftaH -tA -taM.
Brig, s. kUpakadvayayutaH potaH.
BRIG: sAmudrapotaBedaH.
BRIG , s. kUpakadvayaviSizwaH sAmudrapotapraBedaH.
Brigade, s. camUH, vAhinI, sEnyadalaM, gulmaH-lmaM. [Brigad]ier, s. vAhinIpatiH, camUpatiH.
BRIGADE: *pftanA.
BRIGADE , s. vyUhaH, camUH f., gulmaH, vAhinI, sEnyadalaM, senAmuKaM.
To BRIGADE , v. a. vAhinIM vyUh (c. 1. -Uhate -UhituM), vyUhIkf.
BRIGADIER, BRIGADIER-GENERAL: *pftanApatiH.
BRIGADIER , s. vAhinIpatiH m., gulmADipatiH m., camUpatiH m., vyUhADyakzaH, sEnyavyUhapatiH m.
Brigand, s. dasyuH, cOraH.
BRIGAND: (1) paripanTI;(2) dasyuH: v. Robber.
BRIGAND , s. dasyuH m., prasahyacOraH, apahArakaH, sAhasikaH, cOraH, loptra- jIvI m. (n).
BRIGANDAGE: dasyutA: v. Robbery, plunder.
BRIGANTINE: Perh. vahitram, D. vi.
BRIGANTINE , s. sAmudradasyuBiH prayukto laGunOkAviSezaH.

Bright, a. ujjvala, pradIpta, BAsura, rucira, tejasvin, BAsvat, BrAjamAna, praBAvat, dIptimat, dEdIpyamAna. 2 viSada, nirmala, Suci. 3 viSruta. [Bright]en, v. t. pra-ut-dyut c., pra-ut-dIp c., udBAs c., BrAj c., virAj c. 2 vimalayati (D.), viSadIkf 8 U. v. i. vimalIBU 1 P, prasad 1 P, prasAdaM gam 1 P, viSadIBU, (diSaH praseduH R. iii. 14). 2 SuB-dyut 1 A, See Shine. [Bright]ly, adv. ujjvalaM, vimalaM, tejasA, kAMtyA. [Bright]ness, s. tejas n., Ojjvalya; dyutiH, ruciH, kAMtiH, praBA, dIptiH, SoBA, (all fem.); BAsuratvaM, tejasvitA; ‘b(rightness) of intellect’ pradIptA prajYA.

BRIGHT: I Shining, lustrous:(1) ujjvalaH (lA, laM);(2) BAsuraH (rA, raM);(3) dIpraH (prA, praM);(4) dyotanaH (nA, naM);(5) rocizRu (mfn.).II Clear, transparent: q. v.: ujjvalaH (lA, laM).III Sparkling with wit, clever: Perh. ujjvala (lA, laM).

BRIGHT , a. dIptimAn -matI -mat (t), dIpraH -prA -praM, dyutimAn -matI -mat (t), praBAvAn -vatI -vat (t), supraBaH -BA -BaM, varccasvI -svinI -svi (n), dyotI -tinI -ti (n), dyotanaH -nA -naM, SoBI -BinI -Bi (n), SoBanaH -nA -naM, ruciraH -rA -raM, tejomayaH -yI -yaM, tEjasaH -sI -saM, ujjvalaH -lA -laM, pratiBAnavAn -vatI -vat (t); ‘having bright eyes,’ dIptAkzaH -kzI -kzaM, dIptalocanaH -nA -naM. — (Clear) viSadaH -dA -daM, vimalaH -lA -laM, nirmmalaH -lA -laM, svacCaH -cCA -cCaM, SuciH -ciH -ci. — (Illustrious) kIrttimAn -matI -mat (t), viSrutaH -tA -taM, mahAyaSAH -SAH -SaH (s). — (Acute) sUkzmabudDiH -dDiH -dDi, nipuRamatiH -tiH -ti.

BRIGHTEN (v. t.): I Lit.: To make bright: (1) dyotayati, ut-, pra-, (c. of dyut);(2) ujjvalayati (c. of jval);(3) udBAsayati (c. of BAs);(4) dIpayati (c. of dIp), b. ing the skies with its rays dIpayannaTa naBaH kiraROGEH, Ki., ix. 23.II Fig.:(1) ujjvalayati;(2) udBAsayati.III To improve: q. v.
BRIGHTEN (v. i.): i. e. to be or become bright: expr. by the adj. s under bright. Ph. the sky did not quite b. na prasAdamucitaM gamitA dyOH, Ki. ix. 25.

To BRIGHTEN , v. a. (To make to shine, &c.) dyut in caus. (dyotayati yituM), BAs in caus. (BAsayati -yituM), praBAs, udBAs, BrAj in caus. (BrAjayati -yituM), virAj in caus. (-rAjayati -yituM), prakAS in caus. (-kASayati -yituM), vimala (nom. vimalayati -yituM).

To BRIGHTEN , v. n. (To become bright) dIprIBU, vimalIBU. — (To be bright) SuB (c. 1. SoBate, SoBituM), ruc (c. 1. rocate, rocituM), dyut (c. 1. dyotate, dyotituM), BrAj (c. 1. BrAjate, BrAjituM); BAs (c. 1. BAsate, BAsituM), rAj (c. 1. rAjati -te, rAjituM), virAj, kAS (c. 1. kASate, kASituM), cakAs (c. 2. cakAsti, cakAsituM), Suci (nom. SucIyate yituM). — (To become bright as the sky) gatatoyadaH -dA -daM BU.
BRIGHTLY: (1) ujjvalam;(2) vimalam (=clearly).
BRIGHTLY , adv. tejasA, dIptyA, dyutyA, kAntyA, dIptaprakAreRa, vimalaM.
BRIGHTNESS: I Splendour, brilliancy:(1) praBA;(2) tejas;(3) dyutiH;(4) Ojjvalyam.II Acuteness, sharpness: q. v.: Perh. Ojjvalyam.

BRIGHTNESS , s. dyutiH f., dyutimattvaM, dIptiH f., dIptimattvaM, dIptatA, jyotiH n. (s), ruciH f., praBA, ujjvalatA, CaviH f., kAntiH f., tejaH n. (s), SoBA. — (Acuteness) budDisUkzmatvaM, nEpuRyaM, matiprakarzaH. — (Beauty) sOndaryyaM.
BRILL: suKAdyamatsyaviSezaH
BRILLIANCY: (1) praBA;(2) ujjvalatA;(3) dIptiH; (4) rocizRutA;(5) BrAjaTuH.
BRILLIANCY , s. dIptiH f., praBA, kAntimattvaM, dyutiH f., CaviH f., tejaH n. (s), BrAjizRutA.
BRILLIANT: (1) mahojjvalaH (lA, laM);(2) pradyotanaH (nA, naM);(3) BAsuraH (rA, raM); rocizRu (mfn.); (5) BrAjizRu (mfn.);(6) pradIptaH (ptA, ptaM).
BRILLIANT , s. atidIptimAn bahukaRaviSizwo vajraBedaH, BinnacCAyo hIraviSezaH.

BRILLIANT , a. praBAvAn -vatI -vat (t), dIptimAn -matI -mat (t), dedI- pyamAnaH -nA -naM, dIptaH -ptA -ptaM, kAntimAn -matI -mat (t), rocizRuH -zRuH -zRu, tejasvI -svinI -svi (n), tejomayaH -yI -yaM, dyotamAnaH -nA -naM, prakASamAnaH -nA -naM, ujjvalaH -lA -laM.
BRILLIANTLY , adv. praBayA, atikAntyA, CavyA, tejasA, dIptipUrvvaM.

Brim, s. kaMWaH, prAMtaH, muKaM, DAraH, karRaH; ‘to the b(rim)’ AmuKaM, AkaMWaM. 2 (of a river) tIraM, tawaH-wa. 3 aMcalaH, daSA (of a cloth). [Brim]ful, a. paripUrRa, AkarRaM pUrRa; ex. by maya (yI f.), nirBara; ‘b(rimful) of joy’ harzanirBaraH.
BRIM: I Rim, border: q. v.: prAntaH.II Of any vessel: muKam, to the b. AmuKam.

BRIM , s. (Edge of any thing) DAraH -rA, prAntaH, antaH -ntaM, upAntaM, paryyantaM, utsaNgaH. — (Edge of a vessel) karRaH, DAraH, muKaM. — (Margin of a river) tIraM, tawaH, tawaM, kacCaH. — (Border of a cloth, &c.) aYcalaH; ‘up to the brim,’ AkarRaM, DAraparyyantaM, AmuKAt.
To BRIM , v. a. AkarRaM pAtraM pF in caus. (pUrayati -yituM), pAtraplAvaM kf.
BRIMFUL: paripUrRaH (rRA, rRaM) or ekAntaM pUrRaM (rRA, rRaM), “B. of glory” tejomayaH (yI, yaM).
BRIMFUL , a. AkarRaM or DAraparyyantaM pUrRaH -rRA -rRaM, ekAntapUrRaH -rRA -rRaM.
BRIMMER , s. AkarRaM or DAraparyyantaM or muKaparyyantaM pUritaM pAtraM, atipUrRaM BAjanaM.
Brimstone, s. gaMDakaH. [Brimston]y, a. gaMDakapUrRaviSizwa.
BRIMSTONE: ganDakaH: v. Sulphur.
BRIMSTONE , s. ganDakaH, ganDASmA m. (n), ganDamodanaM, krUraganDaH, SulvAriH m.
BRIMSTONY , a. ganDakamayaH -yI -yaM, ganDakapUrRaH -rRA -rRaM, ganDakaviSizwaH -zwA -zwaM.
BRINDED, BRINDLED: (1) SavalaH (lA, laM);(2) karbU (rbu) raH (rA, raM);(3) kirmIraH (rA, raM);(4) citraH (trA, traM).
BRINDED or BRINDLED, a. SavalaH -lA -laM, citrANgaH -NgI -NgaM, citraH -trA -traM, citritaH -tA -taM, nAnAvarRaH -rRA -rRaM, reKANkitaH -tA -taM.
Brindle, s. citratA, citrAMgatvaM, SabalatvaM. [Brindl]ed, a. Sabala, citrita, kalmAzita.
BRINDLE , s. SavalatvaM, SavalaBAvaH, citrANgatvaM, citratA.
Brine, s. lavaRajalaM. 2 bAzpaH, aSru n., astraM.
BRINE: I Water saturated with salt:(1) lavaRodam;(2) lavaRajalam.II The ocean:(1) lavaRodaH;(2) lavaRodaDiH;(3) lavaRAmburASiH;(4) lavaRAbDiH.III Tears: q. v.
BRINE , s. lavaRodaM, lavaRajalaM. — (The briny deep) lavaRAmburASiH. — (Tears) vAzpaH, aSru n., nayanasalilaM.
BRINE-PIT , s. lavaRajalapUrRaM KAtaM or kuRqaM, lavaRodakUpaH.

Bring, v. t. AnI, 1 P, A-upA-hf 1 P, Avah 1 P. 2 prAp c., Agam c. (gamayati). 3 anunI 1 P, Akfz 1 P. 4 janHjan c. (janayati), utpad c.; ex. by praBU 1 P, jan 4 A; ‘poverty b(ring)s one to shame’ dAridryAd hriyameti (Mr. 1); ‘b(ring) to end’ samAp c., nirvft c., avaso 4 P; ‘b(ring) to ruin’ naS c., nASakAraRaM BU; ‘b(ring) word’ nivid c., vArtAM AKyA 2 P; ‘b(ring) action’ aBiyuj 7 A. [Bring] about, (to pass) sAD 5 P, 10; Gaw c., (Gawayati), saMpad c., Avah 1 P; kxp 1 A, saMpad 4 A, (with dat.). [Bring] down, ni-ava-pat c. apakfz, aBiBU [Bring] forth, See Beget. [Bring] forward, upanyas. 4 P, udAhf 1 P, upakzip 6 P, upAnAupAnI, puraskf. 2 agre-puraH-AnI, prahf c. [Bring] on, Avah 1 P; or with dat.; ‘disgrace b(ring)s on despair’ pariBavaH nirvedamAvahati, nirvedAya (Bavati); oft. by praBU, jan; ‘avarice b(ring)s on anger’ loBAt kroDaH praBavati-jAyate &c. [Bring] out, prakAS c., prakawIkf. [Bring] together, samA-nI, samupAhf; See Assemble. [Bring] under, Anam c. (namayati); ‘b(ring) under oneʼs power’ vaSaM nI, dam c. (damayati), aBiBU. [Bring] up, saMvfD c., pozaRaM-pAlanaM-kf 8 U (with gen.); puz 10.

BRING: I To fekSfetch or cause to come:(1) Anayati (nI, c. l.), b. my darling here dayita- mihAnaya, Ki. x. 47.;(2) Aharati, upa-, (hf, c. 1.), b. two dishes uBe SarAve cAhara, D. vi. Ph. winter b. s cold hemantena saha SItamAgacCati.II To cause the obtaining of:(1) by verbs of motion or verbs signifying to obtain and the ins. or abl. of the cause: poverty b. s shame dAridryAdDriyameti, Mr. i.; disgrace b. s despondency pariBavAnnirvedamApadyate, Mr. i.;(2) dadAti (=to give: q. v.);(3) vikarzati (kfz, c. l.), b. s fortune SriyaM vikarzati, Ki. iii. 7.III To induce, prevail on: q. v. Ph.: to b. an action aBiyogaM karoti (?): b. to an end samApayati (c. of Ap); b. to pass: v. Bring about.

To BRING , v. a. (Fetch from another place) AnI (c. 1. -nayati -te -netuM), upAnI, Ahf (c. 1. -harati -harttuM). — (Carry to a place) nI, Avah (c. 1. -vahati -voQuM), upavah, saMvah. — (Cause to come) Agam in caus. (-gamayati -yituM), prAp in caus. (-Apayati -yituM), upapad in caus. (-pAdayati -yituM). — (Reduce to a particular state) gam in caus., kf; ‘brought to misery,’ kfcCragataH -tA -taM; ‘brought low,’ alpIkftaH -tA -taM, astaNgamitaH -tA -taM. — (Induce) anunI, upAgam in caus., protsah in caus. (-sAhayati -yituM), Akfz (c. 1. -karzati -krazwuM). — (Bring about) Gaw (c. 1. Gawate, GawituM), siD in caus. (sADayati -yituM), saMsiD, sampad in caus. (-pAdayati -yituM), upapad. — (Bring back) pratyAnI, pratipad in caus., pratyf in caus. (-arpayati -yituM). — (Bring down, humble) apakfz, aBiBU (c. 1. -Bavati -BavituM); ‘having his pride brought down,’ AttagarvvaH, BagnadarpaH. — (Bring forth, give birth to) su (c. 1. savati, c. 2. sOti, sotuM), prasu; prajan (c. 4. -jAyate -janituM), jan in caus. (janayati -yituM), utpad in caus.; ‘act of bringing forth,’ prasavaH. — (Bring forward) praRI, aBipraRI, AnI, upanI, agre nI, puraskf, pragam in caus., samprasTA in caus. (-sTApayati -yituM), prasf in caus. (-sArayati -yituM); ‘brought forward as an example,’ upanyastaH -stA -staM. — (Bring in) praviS in caus. (-veSayati -yituM), niviS, upanyas (c. 4. -asyati, asituM). — (Bring on) Avah, utpad in caus. (-pAdayati -yituM); ‘that would bring on death,’ tanmftyum Avahet; ‘bringing happiness,’ suKAvahaH -hA -haM. — (Bring out) prakAS in caus. (-kASayati -yituM), pracar in caus. (-cArayati -yituM), prakawIkf, dfS in caus. (darSayati -yituM). — (Bring together) samAnI, ekatra nI or kf, samBf (c. 1. -Barati -BarttuM). — (Bring under) apakfz, aBiBU, dam in caus. (damayati -yituM), vaSIkf. — (Bring up) vinI, puz in caus. (pozayati -yituM), vfD in caus. (varDayati -yituM). — (Bring to an end) nirvah in caus. (-vAhayati -yituM), nirvft in caus. (-varttayati -yituM), samAp in caus. (-Apayati -yituM), siD in caus. — (Bring to light) prakAS in caus., spazwIkf. — (Bring to pass). [Page066-a+ 51] See Bring about. — (Bring word) nivid in caus. (-vedayati -yituM), vArttAm or saMvAdam AKyA (c. 2. -KyAti -KyAtuM), saMvad in caus. (-vAdayati -yituM). — (Bring an action against) aBiyuj (c. 7. -yunakti -yoktuM), vivAdAspadIkf.
BRING ABOUT: Gawayati (c. of Gaw): v. To effect, accomplish.
BRING BACK: (1) pratyAnayati (nI, c. l.), will b. the fortune of victory jayaSriyaM pratyAnezyati, Ku. ii. 52.;(2) pratyAharati (hf, c. l.), M. n.
BRING DOWN: I Lit.:(1) Anayati, brought them down to the earth kzitimAninyuH, Ki. vii. 19.;(2) avatArayati (c. of tF) (=cause to descend) V. i.II To humble, abuse: q. v.

BRING FORTH: I To beget: q. v.: sUte, pra-, (sU, c. l.), Sumitrā brought f. twins sumitrA suzuve yamO, R. x. 71.II To yield: q. v.: sUte, the aśoka tree at once brought f. flowers asUta sadyaH kusumAnyaSokaH, Ku. iii. 26.III To b. forward: q. v.
BRING FORWARD: (1) Anayati;(2) upanyasyati (as, c. 4.);(3) udAharati (hf, c. l.), argu- ments have been forcibly brought f. upapattirudAhftA balAt, Ki. ii. 28.
BRING OFF: (1) apanayati (nI, c. l.);(2) apa- harati (hf, c. l.), Ve. iv.
BRING ON: Avahati (vah, c. l.): v. To produce.
BRING OUT: bahizkaroti, b. ing his son out tatputraM bahizkftya, H. ii.: v. To publish, expose, or detect.

BRING OVER: I To bear across: Anayati (with double acc.), I brought him over to London *tamahaM laRqanamAnItavAn.II To draw to a new party or opinion: Ph. b. ing the Brahmins over by gold dvijAn svIkftya svarRena, Raj.
BRING TO: v. To resuscitate. Ph. I have brought troubles to my husband kleSAvahA BartuH, R. xiv. 5.
BRING TOGETHER: (1) samAnayati (nI, c. l.); [Page090] (2) samAharati (hf, c. l.): v. To collect, assemble.
BRING UNDER: (1) namayati (c. of nam), R. xiii. 9.;(2) Avarjayati (vfj, c. 10.), D. ii. To b. one's power vaSaM nayati or AnayatiH v. To subdue.
BRING UP: I Lit.:(1) Anayati;(2) upAnayati; (3) Aharati.II To train up, rear: q. v.: varDayati (c. of vfD), (the child) was brought up by Vinayavati avarData vinayavatyA, D. iv.
BRINGER , s. AnetA m. (tf), upAnetA m. (tf), AvahaH in comp.
BRINISH or BRINY, a. lavaRaH -RA -RaM, lAvaRaH -RI -RaM, kzArarasaH -sA -saM.
BRINISHNESS , s. lAvaRyaM, lavaRatvaM, kzAratA, kzArarasaH.
Brink, s. tIraM, tawaH-waM, kUlaM. 2 prAMtaH, aMtaH, paryaMtaH; DArA, utsaMgaH, parisaraH, kaMWaH.
BRINK , s. (Of a river) tIraM, kUlaM, tawaM, kacCaH. — (Of any thing) prAntaH, antaH -ntaM, upAntaM, paryyantaM, DAraH -rA. — (Of a precipice) utsaNgaH, SElakawakaH.
BRINY: lAvaRaH (RI, RaM): v. Salty.
Brisk, a. capala, tvarita, kzipra, avilaMba. 2 prabala, sasAra, tIvra; ‘b(risk) shower’ DArAsaMpAtaH. [Brisk]ly, adv. satvaraM, kzipraM, ASu. [Brisk]ness, s. tejas n., sAraH, satvaMsattvaM.
BRISK: capalaH (lA, laM) (of movements, etc.); (2) caturaH (rA, raM) (=clever, sharp): v. Lively.

BRISK , a. laGuH -GuH -Gu, tvaritaH -tA -taM, avilambaH -mbA -mbaM, kzipraH -prA -praM, atandraH -ndrA -ndraM, praPullaH -llA -llaM. — (Powerful, spirituous) prabalaH -lA -laM, tIvraH -vrA -vraM, tEjasaH -sI -saM, sAravAn -vatI -vat (t), sOrikaH -kI -kaM; ‘a brisk shower,’ DArAsampAtaH.
BRISKET: Ph. b. of beef *govakzomAMsam; b. of mutton mezavakzomAMsam.
BRISKET , s. paSor vakzaH n. (s), or uraH n. (s), or vakzassTalaM.
BRISKLY: tvaritam (=quickly): v. Vigorously.
BRISKLY , adv. tvaritaM, kzipraM, satvaraM, prayatnatas, sAratas, avilambitaM, atandritaM, balavat.
BRISKNESS , s. lAGavaM, kzipratvaM, SIGratA, avilambatA. — (Vigour) tejaH n. (s), sAratA, sattvaM, tIvratA.

Bristle, v. i. pulakita-romAMcita-kaMwakita a. BU 1 P; ‘his body b(ristl)ing with joy’ harzaromAMcita-pulakita-tanuH; hfz 4 P (of hair). s. SUkaH-kaM, dfQaloman n. 2 SUkaraloman n. [Bristl]ing, a. hfzita, pulakita, romAMcita.
BRISTLE (subs.): sawA, Ki. viii. 2.
BRISTLE (v. t.): Ph. b. ing of the hairs badDa- sawonnatiH, Ki. xiii. 2. or udBf tasawAH (m. pl.), R. ix. 60.
BRISTLE (v. i.): (1) stabDaH (bDA, bDaM) or unnataH (tA, taM) Bavati;(2) hfzyati (hfz, c. 4.) or pulakitaH (tA, taM) Bavati (only of man in joy).
BRISTLE , s. SUkaH -kaM, dfQaloma n. (n), stabDaroma n. (n), roma n. (n), sUciH f. — (Of a hog) SUkaraloma n. (n).

To BRISTLE , v. n. SUkavat or SUkaralomavad hfz (c. 4. hfzyati, harzituM) or pulakitaH -tA -taM or unnataH -tA -taM or udgataH -tA -taM BU or stabDIBU; SUka (nom. SUkAyate), pulaka (nom. pulakAyate); ‘the hairs of his skin bristled up,’ tasya romARy ahfzan.
BRISTLING , part. hfzitaH -tA -taM, hfzwaH -zwA -zwaM, pulakitaH -tA -taM, pulakI -kinI -ki (n), danturaH -rA -raM; ‘bristling hairs,’ hfzitAni romARi.
BRISTLY: kaRwakitaH (tA, taM), their skins b. with joy prItikaRwakitatvacaH, Ku. vi. 15.
BRISTLY , a. SUkI -kinI -ki (n), SUkavAn -vatI -vat (t), sUcIromA -mA -ma (n), dfQalomA -mA -ma (n), stabDaromA -mA -ma (n).
BRITAIN , s. (The white island) SvetadvIpaH.
BRITISH , a. pUrvvoktadeSasambanDI -nDinI -nDi (n).
Brittle, a. BaMgura, Bidura, suKaBedya, suBaMga.
BRITTLE: (1) BaNguraH (rA, raM);(2) suBaNgaH (NgA, NgaM);(3) BaNgaBAj (mfn.) (rare).
BRITTLE , a. BaNguraH -rA -raM, BiduraH -rA -raM, BidelimaH -mA -maM, suKaBedyaH -dyA -dyaM, BedyaH -dyA -dyaM, KaRqanIyaH -yA -yaM, suBaNgaH -NgA -NgaM, komalaH -lA -laM.
BRITTLENESS: (1) BaNguratA;(2) suBaNgatA.
BRITTLENESS , s. BaNguratA -tvaM, suBaNgatA, BiduratvaM, KaRqanIyatA, BedyatA, komalatA.
Brize, s. daMSaH; gomakzikA.
BRIZE , s. daMSaH, daMSakaH, vanamakzikA, gomakzikA.
Broach, s. SUlaH, SaMkuH, kIlaH-laM. v. t. apAvf 5 U. 2 nivid c., prakAS c., kaT 10. 3 Cidra 10.
BROACH (v. t.): I To spit: q. v.: SUlAkaroti. II To tap, pierce: q. v.III To put forth, publish first: q. v.: pracArayati (c. of car).
BROACH , s. (A spit) SUlaH, SalAkA, SalyaM, SaNkuH m. — (An orna- ment). See BROOCH.

To BROACH , v. a. (To spit) SUl (c. 1. SUlati, SUlituM), SUlAkf. — (To tap a vessel) madyAdiSrAvaRArTaM surABAjane CidraM kf, madyAdimoca- nArTaM BARqaM Cidr (c. 10. Cidrayati -yituM). — (To open) vivf (c. 5. -vfRoti -varituM -varItuM), apAvf, udGaw (c. 10. -GAwayati -yituM). — (To give out, utter) uccar in caus. (-cArayati -yituM), pracar, prakAS in caus. (-kASayati -yituM), nivid in caus. (-vedayati -yituM), pracalIkf.

Broad, a. vistIrRa, pfTu, vipula, vistfta, viSAla, pariRAhavat, Ayata; ‘10 yojanas b(road)’ daSayojanamAyatA (nagarI). 2 asaBya, aSlIla, garhita; ‘b(road) day-break’ supraBAtaM; spazwe jAte pratyUzasi (Ka. 26); ‘b(road) day-light’ praKaratejasi savitari; ‘b(road) awake’ prabudDa, unnidra; ‘b(road) breasted’ vyUQoraskaH; viSAlavakzas. [Broad]ness, Breadth, s. vistAraH, pariRAhaH, AyAmaH, viSAlatA, pfTutA; ‘five fingers in b(readth)’ paMcAMgulaM (dAru).

BROAD: I Wide (in measurement): q. v.: (1) vistftaH (tA, taM);(2) expr. by a comp. with the words given under breadth (I) or by adj. formed with any of those words and the affix vat: seven cubits long and one cubit b. saptahastadIrGA ekahastavistArAH: Ph.: a b. road suvistAravAnmArgaH (?) (not viSAlamArgaH): one who has a b. chest viSAlavakzas (mfn.), R.; a breast beautiful and b. as the leaf of a door kapAwa- -vistIrRamanoramoraH, Si. iii. 13.II Extensive, vast: q. v.: vistIrRaH (rRA, rRaM). Ph.: b. jokes grAmyaparihAsAH (m. pl.); b. nonsense *spazwanirarTaka- BAzitam; thefts are not rare here even in b. day- light *dedIpyamAne sUryo'pyatra cOryARi na viralAni; it is as b. as long, i. e. (it makes no difference) atra ko viSezaH.

BROAD , a. (Wide, large) pfTuH -TuH -Tu, viSAlaH -lA -laM, vipulaH -lA -laM, prasTaH -sTA -sTaM. — (Spacious, expanded) vistIrRaH -rRA -rRaM, vitataH -tA -taM. — (Coarse) asaByaH -ByA -ByaM, aparizkftaH -tA -taM, aSudDaH -dDA -dDaM. — (Indelicate) avAcyaH -cyA -cyaM, garhitaH -tA -taM; ‘to make broad,’ praT (nom. praTayati -yituM); ‘broad-waisted,’ pfTumaDyaH -DyA -DyaM.
BROAD CLOTH: *banAtaH.
BROAD-AWAKE , a. prajAgaraH -rA -raM, prabudDaH -dDA -dDaM, unnidraH -drA -draM.
BROAD-BLADE , a. utpalapatraH &c. BROKEN-WINDED, a. BagnaSvAsaH &c.
BROAD-BREASTED , a. vyUQoraskaH -skA -skaM, urasvAn -svatI -svat (t), [Page066-b+ 51] urasilaH -lA -laM.
BROAD-BRIMMED , a. pfTuDAraH -rA -raM, viSAlAYcalaH -lA -laM, vipulaDAraH -rA -raM.
BROAD-CLOTH , s. aDunAtanajanEr BftaM mezalomanirmmitaM sUkzmavastraM.
BROAD-SHOULDERED , a. pfTuskanDaH -nDA -nDaM, aMsalaH -lA -laM, pfTubAhuH -huH -hu.
To BROADEN , v. n. praT (c. 1. praTate, praTituM), vipraT, vistF in pass. (-stIryyate).
BROADLY: v. Widely. Ph. b. these are the species ityetA jAtayaH sTOlyAt, Śr.
BROADNESS , s. pfTutA, pArTavaM, praTimA m. (n), viSAlatA, vistAraH, vistIrRatA, vipulatA, prasTatA, parisaraH, pAwaH. — (Coarseness) asaByatA, aSudDatA, avAcyatvaM, garhyatA.

sanskrit.slp1: sAmudrayudDasamaye ye lohagolakA ekakAle nOkApArSvAt prakzipyante
sanskrit.word: सामुद्रयुद्धसमये ये लोहगोलका एककाले नौकापार्श्वात् प्रक्षिप्यन्ते
sanskrit.iast: sāmudrayuddhasamaye ye lohagolakā ekakāle naukāpārśvāt prakṣipyante

details.body: BROADSIDE: to fire a b. raRapotasyEkapArSvasTAM banduka- SreRiM samaM visarjayati.
BROADSIDE , s. nOpArSvaH -rSvaM, nOkApArSvaH, potapArSvaH. — (Volley of shot) sAmudrayudDasamaye ye lohagolakA ekakAle nOkApArSvAt prakzipyante.
BROADSWORD: KaNgaviSezaH.
BROADSWORD , s. pfTupatraH KaqgaviSezaH, pfTuPalakaviSizwaH kfpARaH.
Brocade, s. kArmikavastraM.
BROCADE: kArmikavastram (?).
BROCADE , s. suvarRarUpyatantusyUtaM dukUlaM, kArmmikavastraM, nAnAvarRakOSAmbaraM.
BROCADED , a. citradukUlAmbaraH -rA -raM, nAnAvarRadukUlAlaNkftaH -tA -taM.

BROCAGE , BROKAGE, or BROKERAGE, s. (The profit gotten by promoting bargains) SulkaH -lkaM, pAritozikaM, kretfvikretrormaDye paRasampAdakena gfhItaM SulkaM or mUlyaM, parakAryyanirvvAhaRAt prati nirUpi- tapratiPalaM, paRaprayojakapAritozikaM. — (The trade of dealing in old things) jIrRadravyARAM krayavikrayaH. — (The transaction of business for other men) parasya kfte paRAyA or paRasampAdanaM, parakAryyanirvvAhaH.
Brochure, s. laGupustakaM.
BROCKET: dvivarzIRo hariRaH.
BROCKET , s. dvivarzIRas tAmratanuviSizwo hariRapraBedaH.
BROCOLI: SAkaBedaH; PullakabisadfSaH kabiBedaH.
BROCOLI , s. SAkapraBedaH, haritakaBedaH, SigruH m., potakI.
Brogue, s. prAkftaBAzA, apaBraMSaH. 2 carmapAdukA.
BROGUE: pAdukAviSezaH.
BROGUE , s. BrazwaBAzA, prAkftaBAzA, apaSabdaH, aSudDoccAraRaM, asaByavyAharaRaM, mlecCaBAzA. — (A kind of shoe) carmmapAdukAviSezaH.
Broider, v. t. citr 10, sUcyA vastre puzpAdikaM siv 4 P. [Broider]y, s. sUcikarman n.
To BROIDER , v. a. sUcyA puzpAdyalaNkArAn siv (c. 4. sIvyati, sevituM) or niziv, or citr (c. 10. citrayati -yituM) or liK (c. 6. liKati, leKituM).
BROIDERY , s. sUcikarmma n. (n), sUcitA, sUcyA puzpAdyalaNkArasIvanaM.
Broil, v. i. tap-pac- pass. v. t. Brasj 6 P; (fig.) saMkzuB c., prakup c., uddIp c. s. kalahaH, dvaMdvaM, kaliH, tumulaM.
BROIL (subs.): kalahaH: v. Quarrel.
BROIL (v. t.): (1) aNgAre pacati, Bha.;(2) Barjayati (c. of Bfj) (upon a gridiron): v. To fry.
BROIL (v. i.): Bfjjati, -te (Brajj, c. 6.).
BROIL , s. (A quarrel) kalahaH, dvandvaM, viroDaH, vyavakroSanaM, kaliH m., tumulaM; ‘to raise broils,’ kalaha (nom. kalahAyate).
To BROIL , v. a. Brajj (c. 6. Bfjjati, BrazwuM), Bfj (c. 1. Barjate, BarjituM), fYja (c. 1. fYjate, fYjituM).
To BROIL , v. n. (To be hot) tap in pass. (tapyate), pac in pass. (pacyate).
BROILED , p. p. BarjitaH -tA -taM, BfzwaH -zwA -zwaM, taptaH -ptA -ptaM.
To BROKE , v. n. paRaM or parakAryyARi sampad in caus. (-pAdayati -yituM) or siD in caus. (sADayati -yituM); parArTaM paR (c. 1. paRate, paRituM or paRAyati -yituM).
BROKEN: v. Break. Ph. b. number BagnAMSaH; b. - winded alpaSvAsaH (sA, saM); b.-hearted BagnASaH (SA, SaM) or BagnamAnasaH (sA, saM), Mah.

BROKEN , p. p. BagnaH -gnA -gnaM, BinnaH -nnA -nnaM, KaRqitaH -tA -taM, rugnaH -gnA -gnaM, vidIrRaH -rRA -rRaM, SakalIkftaH -tA -taM, viGawwitaH -tA -taM, truwitaH -tA -taM. — (Trained) vinItaH -tA -taM, damitaH -tA -taM.
BROKEN-HEARTED , a. BagnahfdayaH -yA -yaM, daladDfdayaH -yA -yaM, vidIrRahfdayaH -yA -yaM, BagnAntaHkaraRaH -RA -RaM, SokAkulaH -lA -laM, BagnASaH -SA -SaM.
BROKEN-KNEED , a. BagnajAnuH -nuH -nu, BinnajAnuH -nuH -nu.
BROKEN-WINDED , a. nazwaSvAsaH -sA -saM, nazwaprARaH -RA -RaM, yazwiprARaH -RA -RaM.
Broker, s. nirUpitamUlyena kAryanirvAhakaH. [Broker]age, s. kAryanirvAhaRArTaM dattaM dravyaM.
BROKER: *dallAlaH.

BROKER , s. nirUpitaSulkena or nirUpitapAritozikeRa parArTe kretA vikretA vA or parArTe vyavasAyI m. (n) or krayavikrayaprayojakaH or parakAryya- nirvvAhakaH or parakAryyasampAdakaH, GawakaH. — (A dealer in old things) jIrRadravyakrayavikrayikaH, jIrRaparicCadakrayavikrayI m. (n).
BROKERAGE: *dallAliH.
BROMINE: *pUyam; bromiRam.
BRONCHIAL , a. kaRWyaH -RWyA -RWyaM, kaRWasambanDIyaH -yA -yaM, grEveyaH -yI -yaM.
BRONZE: Perh. Aram (comp. Lat. aes, aeris.) or ArakUwam: v. Brass.
BRONZE , s. kAMsyaM, pittalaM, tAmraM, rItiH f., retyaM, AraH.
To BRONZE , v. a. pittalIkf, tAmrasAtkf, pittalarUpeRa kaWinIkf.
BRONZED , p. p. tAmrasAtkftaH -tA -taM, rEtyaH -tyI -tyaM, kAMsyatulyaH -lyA -lyaM.
Brooch, s. vakzoBUzaRaM, uromaRiH.
BROOCH: *vakzoBUzaRam.

BROOCH , s. (A kind of ornament) vastrAYcalasaNgrahaRayogyo vakzassTale BftaH suvarRakIlaH, urasi kIlitaH sUkzmasuvarRaSaNkuyuktAlaNkAro yaddvAreRa vastrAYcaladvayaM saMlagnIkftaM, uromaRiH, vakzoBUzaRaM.
Brood, v. i. (lit.) (aMqAnAM) upari-sad 1 P, niviS 6 P; (fig.) ni-DyE 1 P, punaH punar Aloc 10; ciMtAvyagra a. BU. s. prajA, saMtati f., apatyaM. 2 samamutpannaH SAvakagaRaH, apatyajAtaM.
BROOD (v. i.): sevate (sev, c. l.) (?) (used in this sense in Hindi), b. ing on eggs aRqAni sevamAnaH (nA, naM) (?)
BROOD (adj.): Ph. b. mare bAlaprasavArTaM rakzitA GowakI.

To BROOD , v. n. (To sit on eggs) kulAyanilAyaM or nIqanilAyaM kf, kulAyaM nilI (c. 4. -lIyate -letuM), aRqaprasavAnantaram ApakziSAvako- tpatter nIqaM nilI; aRqAnAm upari upaviS (c. 6. -viSati -vezwuM).
BROOD , s. (A hatch) SAvakagaRaH, yaH SAvakagaRa ekakAle qimbAd utpadyate. — (Offspring) prajA, apatyaM, santAnaH.
BROOD OVER or ON: DyAyati (DyE, c. l.) (with acc.): v. Contemplate.
